content: Whose name opens the long family lists of 1 Chronicles?
explanation: The lists start at the very beginning. “Adam, Seth, Enosh” (1 Chronicles 1:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, what did Jabez ask God to enlarge?
explanation: God granted his request. “If only You would bless me and enlarge my territory!” (1 Chronicles 4:10, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, how did God answer the prayer of Jabez?
explanation: Jabez called on the God of Israel. “And God granted the request of Jabez.” (1 Chronicles 4:10, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, why should we give thanks to the LORD?
explanation: His love endures forever. “Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.” (1 Chronicles 16:34, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, what did King David tell Solomon before building the temple?
explanation: God would not fail him. “Be strong and courageous, and do it.” (1 Chronicles 28:20, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, whom did David have the Levites appoint to praise with joy?
explanation: With harps, lyres, and cymbals. “David also told the leaders of the Levites to appoint their relatives as singers” (1 Chronicles 15:16, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, why did Jabez's mother give him his name?
explanation: Yet he was honorable. “His mother had named him Jabez, saying, “Because I bore him in pain.”” (1 Chronicles 4:9, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, what was Jerusalem's earlier name?
explanation: The Jebusites lived there. “Then David and all the Israelites marched to Jerusalem (that is, Jebus)” (1 Chronicles 11:4, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, why did God not let David build the temple?
explanation: He had waged great wars. “You are not to build a house for My Name because you have shed so much blood on the ground before Me.” (1 Chronicles 22:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, what kind of man would Solomon be, according to God?
explanation: Israel would have peace in his reign. “But a son will be born to you who will be a man of rest.” (1 Chronicles 22:9, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, why did David make lavish preparations for the temple?
explanation: The temple had to be magnificent. “My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent” (1 Chronicles 22:5, BSB)

content: In David's prayer in 1 Chronicles, to whom does everything in heaven and earth belong?
explanation: His is the kingdom. “for everything in heaven and on earth belongs to You.” (1 Chronicles 29:11, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, where did David say the people's generous gifts came from?
explanation: Everything comes from God. “For everything comes from You, and from Your own hand we have given to You.” (1 Chronicles 29:14, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, why did Saul die?
options: He was unfaithful to the LORD
explanation: He even consulted a medium. “So Saul died for his unfaithfulness to the LORD” (1 Chronicles 10:13, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, how is King David described at his death?
options: Full of years, riches, and honor
explanation: Solomon reigned after him. “He died at a ripe old age, full of years, riches, and honor” (1 Chronicles 29:28, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, what did Satan incite David to do?
explanation: It displeased God. “Then Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to take a census of Israel.” (1 Chronicles 21:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, to which prophet did David say the ark was under a tent?
explanation: David lived in a cedar house. “he said to Nathan the prophet, “Here I am, living in a house of cedar, while the ark of the covenant of the LORD is under a tent.”” (1 Chronicles 17:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Chronicles, who is listed right after Adam?
explanation: The list continues with Enosh. “Adam, Seth, Enosh” (1 Chronicles 1:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, speaking in tongues without love makes you like what?
explanation: Love gives meaning to gifts. “but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.” (1 Corinthians 13:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, faith that moves mountains without love makes you what?
explanation: Love matters most. “and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.” (1 Corinthians 13:2, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, how does Paul begin describing love?
options: Love is patient, love is kind
explanation: It does not envy or boast. “Love is patient, love is kind.” (1 Corinthians 13:4, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, which of these does love NOT do?
explanation: Love is not proud. “It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.” (1 Corinthians 13:4, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what does love keep no account of?
explanation: Love forgives. “it keeps no account of wrongs.” (1 Corinthians 13:5, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what does Paul say love never does?
explanation: Other gifts will pass away. “Love never fails.” (1 Corinthians 13:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, which three things remain?
explanation: The greatest is love. “And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love” (1 Corinthians 13:13, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, which is the greatest of faith, hope, and love?
explanation: Love never fails. “but the greatest of these is love.” (1 Corinthians 13:13, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul tells believers they are the body of whom?
explanation: Each is a member of it. “Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.” (1 Corinthians 12:27, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, whatever you eat, drink, or do, do it all to the what of God?
explanation: All of life is for God. “So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.” (1 Corinthians 10:31, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul says to do everything in what?
explanation: Love guides every action. “Do everything in love.” (1 Corinthians 16:14, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, the message of the cross is foolishness to some, but what to us who are saved?
explanation: The cross saves. “but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.” (1 Corinthians 1:18, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul planted and Apollos watered, but who made it grow?
explanation: Growth comes from God. “I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.” (1 Corinthians 3:6, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul says believers themselves are God's what?
explanation: God's Spirit dwells in them. “Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple” (1 Corinthians 3:16, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, since you were bought at a price, what should you do?
explanation: Your body is the Spirit's temple. “you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.” (1 Corinthians 6:20, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul tells believers to run like runners in a race in order to do what?
explanation: Live with purpose. “Run in such a way as to take the prize.” (1 Corinthians 9:24, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, when you are tempted, what will God provide?
explanation: God is faithful. “But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape” (1 Corinthians 10:13, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what did Jesus say when He broke the bread?
explanation: Do this in remembrance of Me. “This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.” (1 Corinthians 11:24, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Jesus called the cup the new covenant in His what?
explanation: We remember His death. “This cup is the new covenant in My blood” (1 Corinthians 11:25, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, the body has many parts but forms how many bodies?
explanation: So it is with Christ. “And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is with Christ.” (1 Corinthians 12:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, there are different gifts but the same what?
explanation: God gives each believer gifts. “There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.” (1 Corinthians 12:4, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, when Paul became a man, what did he set aside?
explanation: Love is mature. “When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.” (1 Corinthians 13:11, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, now we see as in a mirror, but then we shall see how?
explanation: We will know fully. “Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face.” (1 Corinthians 13:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, on which day was Christ raised according to the Scriptures?
explanation: This is of first importance. “that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures” (1 Corinthians 15:4, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul taunts death, asking, “Where, O Death, is your…”
explanation: Christ has won the victory. “Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?” (1 Corinthians 15:55, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what foundation has already been laid?
explanation: No other foundation can be laid. “For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.” (1 Corinthians 3:11, BSB)

content: Who is named with Paul at the start of 1 Corinthians?
explanation: He is called our brother. “and our brother Sosthenes” (1 Corinthians 1:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, which name did some believers follow besides Paul, Apollos, and Christ?
explanation: Paul warned against divisions. ““I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” or “I follow Christ.”” (1 Corinthians 1:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, to how many brothers at once did the risen Christ appear?
explanation: Most were still living. “After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once” (1 Corinthians 15:6, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what does Paul call the risen Christ?
explanation: Others will be raised too. “the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.” (1 Corinthians 15:20, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, at the last trumpet, how fast will we be changed?
options: In the twinkling of an eye
explanation: The dead will be raised. “in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet.” (1 Corinthians 15:52, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, where did Paul say he would stay until Pentecost?
explanation: A door for work was open. “But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost” (1 Corinthians 16:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what does Paul call Christ who has been sacrificed?
explanation: So remove the old leaven. “For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.” (1 Corinthians 5:7, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what has no eye seen and no ear heard?
options: What God prepared for those who love Him
explanation: God's plans are wonderful. “what God has prepared for those who love Him.” (1 Corinthians 2:9, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, love bears, believes, hopes, and endures how many things?
explanation: Love does not give up. “It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.” (1 Corinthians 13:7, BSB)

content: In 1 John, what does John say God is?
explanation: Whoever does not love does not know God. “Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.” (1 John 4:8, BSB)

content: In 1 John, why should we love one another?
explanation: Everyone who loves knows God. “Beloved, let us love one another, because love comes from God.” (1 John 4:7, BSB)

content: In 1 John, how was God's love revealed among us?
explanation: So that we might live through Him. “God sent His one and only Son into the world, so that we might live through Him.” (1 John 4:9, BSB)

content: In 1 John, love is not that we loved God, but that what?
explanation: God loved first. “not that we loved God, but that He loved us” (1 John 4:10, BSB)

content: In 1 John, since God so loved us, what ought we to do?
explanation: God's love flows through us. “Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.” (1 John 4:11, BSB)

content: In 1 John, what does perfect love drive out?
explanation: There is no fear in love. “There is no fear in love, but perfect love drives out fear” (1 John 4:18, BSB)

content: In 1 John, why do we love?
explanation: Our love answers God's love. “We love because He first loved us.” (1 John 4:19, BSB)

content: In 1 John, whoever loves God must also love whom?
explanation: This is God's command. “Whoever loves God must love his brother as well.” (1 John 4:21, BSB)

content: In 1 John, what will God do if we confess our sins?
explanation: He is faithful and just. “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins” (1 John 1:9, BSB)

content: In 1 John, what has the Father's love made us?
explanation: And that is what we are! “that we should be called children of God. And that is what we are!” (1 John 3:1, BSB)

content: In 1 John, God is light, and in Him there is no what?
explanation: This is the message from Him. “God is light, and in Him there is no darkness at all.” (1 John 1:5, BSB)

content: In 1 John, if anyone sins, who is our advocate before the Father?
explanation: He is the Righteous One. “we have an advocate before the Father—Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.” (1 John 2:1, BSB)

content: In 1 John, we should love not only in word, but in what?
explanation: Real love acts. “Little children, let us love not in word and speech, but in action and truth.” (1 John 3:18, BSB)

content: In 1 John, what are believers told not to love?
explanation: The Father's love must come first. “Do not love the world or anything in the world.” (1 John 2:15, BSB)

content: In 1 John, why did John write to believers?
options: So they know they have eternal life
explanation: Believers can be sure. “so that you may know that you have eternal life.” (1 John 5:13, BSB)

content: In 1 John, what is someone who says he loves God but hates his brother?
explanation: Love for God shows in love for others. “If anyone says, “I love God,” but hates his brother, he is a liar.” (1 John 4:20, BSB)

content: How does the letter of 1 John end?
explanation: A final warning to his little children. “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” (1 John 5:21, BSB)

content: In 1 John, no one has ever seen God, but if we love one another, what happens?
explanation: His love is perfected in us. “but if we love one another, God remains in us, and His love is perfected in us.” (1 John 4:12, BSB)

content: In 1 John, perfected love gives us confidence on which day?
explanation: We are like Him in this world. “so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment” (1 John 4:17, BSB)

content: When the LORD appeared to young King Solomon in a dream, what did He say?
options: Ask, and I will give it
explanation: God offered Solomon any gift. “Ask, and I will give it to you!” (1 Kings 3:5, BSB)

content: In his dream, how did King Solomon describe himself to God?
explanation: He felt too young to rule. “But I am only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in.” (1 Kings 3:7, BSB)

content: When God said “Ask,” what did King Solomon ask for?
explanation: He wanted to judge God's people well. “Therefore give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people” (1 Kings 3:9, BSB)

content: How did the Lord feel about King Solomon's request for wisdom?
explanation: Solomon did not ask selfishly. “Now it pleased the Lord that Solomon had made this request.” (1 Kings 3:10, BSB)

content: Besides wisdom, what did God also give King Solomon that he did not ask for?
explanation: God gave more than he asked. “Moreover, I will give you what you did not request—both riches and honor” (1 Kings 3:13, BSB)

content: When two women claimed the same baby, what did King Solomon order as a test?
explanation: The real mother would show herself. “Cut the living child in two and give half to one and half to the other.” (1 Kings 3:25, BSB)

content: How did King Solomon know who the baby's real mother was?
explanation: Her love for the child showed. “Give the living baby to the first woman. By no means should you kill him; she is his mother.” (1 Kings 3:27, BSB)

content: What did King Solomon plan to build for the Name of the LORD?
explanation: God had promised this to David. “So behold, I plan to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God” (1 Kings 5:5, BSB)

content: For the temple, what wood did King Solomon order from Lebanon?
explanation: Lebanon's cedars were famous. “Now therefore, order that cedars of Lebanon be cut down for me.” (1 Kings 5:6, BSB)

content: While Solomon's temple was built, what tools were never heard there?
explanation: Stones were cut at the quarry. “so that no hammer or chisel or any other iron tool was heard in the temple while it was being built.” (1 Kings 6:7, BSB)

content: What did King Solomon overlay the whole inside of the temple with?
explanation: It was a glorious house for God. “So he overlaid with gold the whole interior of the temple” (1 Kings 6:22, BSB)

content: How many years did it take King Solomon to build the temple?
explanation: It was finished in every detail. “So he built the temple in seven years.” (1 Kings 6:38, BSB)

content: When Solomon's temple was dedicated, what filled the house of the LORD?
explanation: God's glory filled it. “the cloud filled the house of the LORD” (1 Kings 8:10, BSB)

content: At the temple's dedication, what did King Solomon say cannot contain God?
explanation: God is greater than any building. “Even heaven, the highest heaven, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.” (1 Kings 8:27, BSB)

content: What did the prophet Elijah tell King Ahab would not come for years?
explanation: Only at Elijah's word would it rain. “there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!” (1 Kings 17:1, BSB)

content: By the Brook of Cherith, which birds did God command to feed Elijah?
explanation: God cared for His prophet. “and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.” (1 Kings 17:4, BSB)

content: What did the ravens bring Elijah each morning and evening?
explanation: He drank from the brook. “The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening” (1 Kings 17:6, BSB)

content: Why did Elijah have to leave the Brook of Cherith?
explanation: There was no rain. “Some time later, however, the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.” (1 Kings 17:7, BSB)

content: After the brook dried up, who did God say would provide for Elijah?
explanation: She lived in Zarephath. “Behold, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.” (1 Kings 17:9, BSB)

content: When Elijah asked for bread, what did the widow of Zarephath have left?
explanation: She planned a last meal for her son. “only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug.” (1 Kings 17:12, BSB)

content: What happened to the widow's flour and oil after she fed Elijah?
explanation: God kept His word. “The jar of flour was not exhausted and the jug of oil did not run dry” (1 Kings 17:16, BSB)

content: On which mountain did Elijah challenge the prophets of Baal?
explanation: All Israel gathered there. “Now summon all Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel” (1 Kings 18:19, BSB)

content: On Mount Carmel, what did Elijah ask the people?
explanation: They had to choose between God and Baal. “How long will you waver between two opinions?” (1 Kings 18:21, BSB)

content: On Mount Carmel, Elijah said the true God would answer by what?
explanation: Baal's prophets agreed to the test. “The God who answers by fire, He is God.” (1 Kings 18:24, BSB)

content: When Baal's prophets called on Baal all morning, what happened?
explanation: Baal was not real. “But there was no sound, and no one answered” (1 Kings 18:26, BSB)

content: Before praying on Mount Carmel, what did Elijah have poured on the offering?
explanation: It made the miracle even greater. “Fill four waterpots and pour the water on the offering and on the wood.” (1 Kings 18:34, BSB)

content: When Elijah prayed on Mount Carmel, what fell from the LORD?
explanation: It burned up even the water. “Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the sacrifice” (1 Kings 18:38, BSB)

content: After the fire fell on Mount Carmel, what did the people shout?
explanation: They fell facedown. “The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!” (1 Kings 18:39, BSB)

content: Which priest anointed Solomon as king?
explanation: The people shouted, “Long live King Solomon!” “Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon.” (1 Kings 1:39, BSB)

content: After King David died, who sat on his throne?
explanation: His kingdom was firmly established. “So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was firmly established.” (1 Kings 2:12, BSB)

content: Where did the LORD appear to Solomon in a dream?
explanation: God offered him any gift. “One night at Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream” (1 Kings 3:5, BSB)

content: After Solomon judged the two women's case, what did all Israel see in him?
explanation: They stood in awe. “for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.” (1 Kings 3:28, BSB)

content: Solomon's understanding was beyond measure, like what on the seashore?
explanation: God gave him great wisdom. “and understanding beyond measure, like the sand on the seashore.” (1 Kings 4:29, BSB)

content: How many proverbs did King Solomon compose?
explanation: His songs numbered a thousand and five. “Solomon composed three thousand proverbs” (1 Kings 4:32, BSB)

content: Why could the priests not minister when Solomon's temple was dedicated?
explanation: The cloud filled the house. “for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.” (1 Kings 8:11, BSB)

content: Which queen came to test Solomon with difficult questions?
explanation: She had heard of his fame. “Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon” (1 Kings 10:1, BSB)

content: When Solomon grew old, what turned his heart after other gods?
explanation: He was not fully devoted like David. “For when Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods” (1 Kings 11:4, BSB)

content: Which king of Israel did more evil than all before him and opposed Elijah?
explanation: He was the son of Omri. “However, Ahab son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD, more than all who were before him.” (1 Kings 16:30, BSB)

content: When Elijah prayed for the widow's son who had died, what happened?
explanation: The LORD listened to Elijah. “and the child’s life returned to him, and he lived.” (1 Kings 17:22, BSB)

content: On Mount Carmel, what did Elijah say Baal might be doing?
explanation: He was mocking the false god. “Perhaps he is sleeping and must be awakened!” (1 Kings 18:27, BSB)

content: On Mount Carmel, how many stones did Elijah use to build the altar?
explanation: One for each tribe. “And Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe of the sons of Jacob” (1 Kings 18:31, BSB)

content: After Carmel, how big was the first cloud Elijah's servant saw rising from the sea?
explanation: Then heavy rain fell. “There is a cloud as small as a man’s hand rising from the sea.” (1 Kings 18:44, BSB)

content: When Elijah fled and slept under a broom tree, who woke him?
explanation: The angel told him to eat. “Suddenly an angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”” (1 Kings 19:5, BSB)

content: At the mountain of God, after wind, earthquake, and fire, what came to Elijah?
explanation: God spoke gently. “And after the fire came a still, small voice.” (1 Kings 19:12, BSB)

content: In what year after leaving Egypt did Solomon begin building the temple?
explanation: It was Solomon's fourth year. “In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt” (1 Kings 6:1, BSB)

content: How many cubits long, wide, and high was the temple's inner sanctuary?
explanation: It was a perfect cube of gold. “The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high.” (1 Kings 6:20, BSB)

content: Solomon said no one was as skilled in logging as which people?
explanation: They cut the cedars of Lebanon. “for you know that there are none among us as skilled in logging as the Sidonians.” (1 Kings 5:6, BSB)

content: How many songs did King Solomon write?
explanation: He also wrote 3,000 proverbs. “and his songs numbered a thousand and five.” (1 Kings 4:32, BSB)

content: Where was the prophet Elijah from?
explanation: He is called Elijah the Tishbite. “Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was among the settlers of Gilead” (1 Kings 17:1, BSB)

content: By which brook did Elijah hide during the drought?
explanation: It was east of the Jordan. “hide yourself by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.” (1 Kings 17:3, BSB)

content: In which town did the widow who fed Elijah live?
explanation: God sent him there. “Get up and go to Zarephath of Sidon, and stay there.” (1 Kings 17:9, BSB)

content: How many prophets of Baal faced Elijah on Mount Carmel?
explanation: Elijah stood alone. “along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal” (1 Kings 18:19, BSB)

content: Under what kind of tree did Elijah sit and pray to die?
explanation: He was worn out and afraid. “He sat down under a broom tree and prayed that he might die.” (1 Kings 19:4, BSB)

content: Strengthened by the angel's food, how long did Elijah walk to Horeb?
explanation: Horeb is the mountain of God. “he walked forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God.” (1 Kings 19:8, BSB)

content: In which month was Solomon's temple finished?
explanation: It was the eighth month. “In his eleventh year and eighth month, the month of Bul, the temple was finished” (1 Kings 6:38, BSB)

content: Which apostle wrote the letter of 1 Peter?
explanation: He wrote to scattered believers. “Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ” (1 Peter 1:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, why should we cast all our anxiety on God?
explanation: God loves His children. “Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.” (1 Peter 5:7, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, the devil prowls around like what?
explanation: Be alert. “Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.” (1 Peter 5:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, what covers over a multitude of sins?
explanation: Love one another deeply. “because love covers over a multitude of sins.” (1 Peter 4:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, believers should crave spiritual milk like what?
explanation: So they grow in salvation. “Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk” (1 Peter 2:2, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, what should you always be ready to explain to anyone who asks?
explanation: Answer with gentleness and respect. “Always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks you the reason for the hope that is in you.” (1 Peter 3:15, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, believers are called a chosen people and a royal what?
explanation: Called out of darkness into light. “But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation” (1 Peter 2:9, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, God has given us new birth into a living what?
explanation: Through Jesus' resurrection. “He has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead” (1 Peter 1:3, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, while grass withers, what stands forever?
explanation: Peter quotes Isaiah. “but the word of the Lord stands forever.” (1 Peter 1:25, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, where did Christ bear our sins in His body?
explanation: So we might live to righteousness. “He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree” (1 Peter 2:24, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, believers have returned to the Shepherd and what of their souls?
explanation: They had been like straying sheep. “but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.” (1 Peter 2:25, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, how many people were saved in Noah's ark?
explanation: They were saved through water. “In the ark a few people, only eight souls, were saved through water.” (1 Peter 3:20, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, through whom did Peter write the letter?
explanation: Peter called him a faithful brother. “Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly” (1 Peter 5:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, whom does Peter call “my son”?
explanation: Mark sent greetings too. “as does my son Mark.” (1 Peter 5:13, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, the church in which city sends greetings?
explanation: It was chosen together with them. “The church in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you greetings” (1 Peter 5:13, BSB)

content: In 1 Peter, which of these regions is named among the readers' homes?
explanation: They were exiles of the Dispersion. “throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia” (1 Peter 1:1, BSB)

content: As a boy, Samuel served the LORD under which priest?
explanation: Samuel grew up in the house of the LORD. “And the boy Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli.” (1 Samuel 3:1, BSB)

content: When the LORD first called young Samuel at night, what did Samuel answer?
explanation: Samuel was ready to listen. “Then the LORD called to Samuel, and he answered, “Here I am.”” (1 Samuel 3:4, BSB)

content: When young Samuel heard his name called at night, who did he think was calling?
explanation: He did not yet know the LORD's voice. “He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.”” (1 Samuel 3:5, BSB)

content: How many times did the LORD call young Samuel before Eli realized it was God?
explanation: Then Eli knew the LORD was calling the boy. “Once again, for the third time, the LORD called to Samuel.” (1 Samuel 3:8, BSB)

content: What did Eli tell young Samuel to say if God called him again?
options: Speak, LORD, Your servant is listening
explanation: Samuel learned to listen to God. “Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.” (1 Samuel 3:9, BSB)

content: Where was young Samuel lying down when God called him?
options: In the temple of the LORD
explanation: The ark of God was there. “Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was located.” (1 Samuel 3:3, BSB)

content: As Samuel grew up, what did all Israel come to know about him?
explanation: The LORD was with Samuel. “knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.” (1 Samuel 3:20, BSB)

content: After God rejected King Saul, to whose family did He send Samuel to find a new king?
explanation: God had chosen a king from Jesse's sons. “I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem” (1 Samuel 16:1, BSB)

content: When Samuel was impressed by Jesse's tall son, what did God say He looks at?
explanation: People judge by looks, but God sees inside. “For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” (1 Samuel 16:7, BSB)

content: How many of Jesse's sons passed before Samuel without being chosen?
explanation: The LORD had not chosen any of them. “Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel” (1 Samuel 16:10, BSB)

content: When Samuel came to anoint a new king, where was Jesse's youngest son?
explanation: No one thought the youngest would be chosen. ““There is still the youngest,” Jesse replied, “but he is tending the sheep.”” (1 Samuel 16:11, BSB)

content: What did Samuel use to anoint young David?
explanation: He anointed David in front of his brothers. “So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers” (1 Samuel 16:13, BSB)

content: After Samuel anointed David, what came upon him?
explanation: From that day God's Spirit was with David. “and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward.” (1 Samuel 16:13, BSB)

content: When King Saul was troubled, what instrument did young David play for him?
explanation: Saul felt better when David played. “David would pick up his harp and play” (1 Samuel 16:23, BSB)

content: Which Philistine champion challenged the army of Israel?
explanation: He was a giant warrior from Gath. “Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out from the Philistine camp.” (1 Samuel 17:4, BSB)

content: When Goliath shouted his challenge, how did Saul and the Israelites feel?
explanation: No one wanted to fight the giant. “Saul and all the Israelites were dismayed and greatly afraid.” (1 Samuel 17:11, BSB)

content: Before facing Goliath, which wild animals did David say he had fought while keeping sheep?
explanation: God had already helped David against them. “and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock” (1 Samuel 17:34, BSB)

content: Why did David take off King Saul's armor before facing Goliath?
options: He was not used to it
explanation: David trusted God, not armor. “I am not accustomed to them.” (1 Samuel 17:39, BSB)

content: How many smooth stones did David choose from the brook before facing Goliath?
explanation: He put them in his shepherd's bag. “selected five smooth stones from the brook” (1 Samuel 17:40, BSB)

content: Facing Goliath, in whose name did David say he came?
explanation: Goliath had defied the living God. “but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts” (1 Samuel 17:45, BSB)

content: Where did David's stone hit Goliath?
explanation: The giant fell facedown. “striking the Philistine on the forehead.” (1 Samuel 17:49, BSB)

content: With what did young David defeat Goliath?
explanation: God gave the victory without a sword in David's hand. “Thus David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone” (1 Samuel 17:50, BSB)

content: After David defeated Goliath, whose soul became knit together with David's?
explanation: Jonathan, Saul's son, loved David as himself. “the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together” (1 Samuel 18:1, BSB)

content: Why did Jonathan make a covenant with David?
explanation: They became best friends. “Then Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.” (1 Samuel 18:3, BSB)

content: What did Jonathan give David as a sign of their friendship?
explanation: He also gave David his tunic and belt. “And Jonathan removed the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt.” (1 Samuel 18:4, BSB)

content: What song of the women made King Saul jealous of David?
options: Saul his thousands, David tens of thousands
explanation: Saul was angry that David got more praise. “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.” (1 Samuel 18:7, BSB)

content: In his jealousy, what did King Saul throw at David?
explanation: David escaped that night. “Saul tried to pin him to the wall with his spear.” (1 Samuel 19:10, BSB)

content: To send David a secret warning, what did Jonathan plan to shoot?
explanation: Where the arrows landed would tell David what to do. “I will shoot three arrows to the side of it” (1 Samuel 20:20, BSB)

content: When David and Jonathan said goodbye, what did they do?
explanation: David had to flee from Saul. “Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and wept together” (1 Samuel 20:41, BSB)

content: When King Saul hunted David with three thousand men, where was David?
explanation: Saul was told where David was hiding. “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.” (1 Samuel 24:1, BSB)

content: When Saul stepped into a cave at En-gedi, who was hiding deep inside?
explanation: Saul did not know they were there. “And David and his men were hiding in the recesses of the cave.” (1 Samuel 24:3, BSB)

content: In the cave at En-gedi, what did David secretly cut off?
explanation: David could have killed Saul, but he did not. “Then David crept up secretly and cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.” (1 Samuel 24:4, BSB)

content: Why would David not harm King Saul in the cave?
explanation: David left Saul's fate to God. “May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.” (1 Samuel 24:6, BSB)

content: How did David feel after cutting the corner of Saul's robe?
explanation: Even that small act felt wrong to him. “Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken” (1 Samuel 24:5, BSB)

content: After David spared his life, what did King Saul say to him?
options: You are more righteous than I
explanation: David had repaid evil with good. “You are more righteous than I” (1 Samuel 24:17, BSB)

content: When Saul heard David calling to him outside the cave, what did Saul do?
explanation: Saul was moved by David's mercy. “Then Saul wept aloud” (1 Samuel 24:16, BSB)

content: Who were the two wives of Elkanah, Samuel's father?
explanation: Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none. “He had two wives, one named Hannah and the other Peninnah.” (1 Samuel 1:2, BSB)

content: What did Hannah promise God if He gave her a son?
options: To give a lamb every year
To dedicate him to the LORD
explanation: She kept her promise. “then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life” (1 Samuel 1:11, BSB)

content: Why did Hannah name her son Samuel?
options: He was born in the temple
She asked the LORD for him
explanation: God answered her prayer. “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.” (1 Samuel 1:20, BSB)

content: When Samuel was a boy, how often did the word of the LORD come?
explanation: Visions were scarce in those days. “Now in those days the word of the LORD was rare and visions were scarce.” (1 Samuel 3:1, BSB)

content: When the Philistines captured the ark of God, which of Eli's sons died?
explanation: It was a dark day for Israel. “The ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.” (1 Samuel 4:11, BSB)

content: When Samuel was old, what did the people of Israel ask him to give them?
explanation: They wanted to be like other nations. “Now appoint a king to judge us like all the other nations.” (1 Samuel 8:5, BSB)

content: When Israel asked Samuel for a king, whom did God say they had really rejected?
explanation: God was meant to be their king. “For it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected Me as their king.” (1 Samuel 8:7, BSB)

content: How is Saul described before he became Israel's first king?
explanation: He was choice and handsome. “a head taller than any of the people.” (1 Samuel 9:2, BSB)

content: When Samuel presented Saul to Israel as king, what did the people shout?
explanation: Saul became Israel's first king. “And all the people shouted, “Long live the king!”” (1 Samuel 10:24, BSB)

content: When Saul disobeyed, Samuel said the LORD had found a man after what?
explanation: That man would be David. “the LORD has sought a man after His own heart” (1 Samuel 13:14, BSB)

content: Samuel told disobedient King Saul that what is better than sacrifice?
explanation: God wants His people to listen and obey. “Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice” (1 Samuel 15:22, BSB)

content: Which of Jesse's sons did Samuel first think was God's chosen king?
explanation: Samuel judged by appearance at first. “When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab” (1 Samuel 16:6, BSB)

content: How is young David described when he was brought in from the sheep?
explanation: The LORD said, “He is the one.” “He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance.” (1 Samuel 16:12, BSB)

content: Goliath the giant came from which Philistine city?
explanation: He was the Philistines' champion. “Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath” (1 Samuel 17:4, BSB)

content: Before the battle with Goliath, what did David go back and forth to do?
explanation: He was still a shepherd in Bethlehem. “but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s sheep in Bethlehem.” (1 Samuel 17:15, BSB)

content: Why did Saul first say David could not fight Goliath?
explanation: Goliath had been a warrior from his youth. “You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.” (1 Samuel 17:33, BSB)

content: David told Goliath that God does not save by sword or spear, because the battle belongs to whom?
explanation: David trusted God to win. “for the battle is the LORD’s” (1 Samuel 17:47, BSB)

content: After Goliath fell, what did the Philistine army do?
explanation: Their hero was dead. “When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran.” (1 Samuel 17:51, BSB)

content: Which of King Saul's daughters did David marry?
explanation: Saul gave her to David as his wife. “Then Saul gave his daughter Michal to David in marriage.” (1 Samuel 18:27, BSB)

content: After the women's song about David, how did King Saul treat him?
options: Kept a jealous eye on him
explanation: Saul feared David would take the kingdom. “And from that day forward Saul kept a jealous eye on David.” (1 Samuel 18:9, BSB)

content: While running from Saul, where did David take refuge after leaving Gath?
explanation: His family came to him there. “So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam.” (1 Samuel 22:1, BSB)

content: Who was the wise wife of harsh Nabal?
explanation: She was intelligent and beautiful. “His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail.” (1 Samuel 25:3, BSB)

content: Before his last battle, whom did King Saul seek out at Endor?
explanation: Saul had turned away from the LORD. “There is a medium at Endor” (1 Samuel 28:7, BSB)

content: How did King Saul die in battle with the Philistines?
options: He fell on his own sword
explanation: His armor-bearer was too afraid to kill him. “So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.” (1 Samuel 31:4, BSB)

content: Elkanah, Samuel's father, came from which town?
explanation: It was in the hill country of Ephraim. “Now there was a man named Elkanah who was from Ramathaim-zophim” (1 Samuel 1:1, BSB)

content: Hannah promised that her son would never have what come over his head?
explanation: He would be set apart for God all his life. “and no razor shall ever come over his head.” (1 Samuel 1:11, BSB)

content: When God called young Samuel, what was wrong with old Eli?
explanation: Eli could not see. “Eli, whose eyesight had grown so dim that he could not see” (1 Samuel 3:2, BSB)

content: Samuel was known as a true prophet across Israel from where to where?
explanation: This meant the whole land. “So all Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew” (1 Samuel 3:20, BSB)

content: Which son of Jesse was presented to Samuel right after Abinadab?
explanation: The LORD had not chosen him either. “Next Jesse presented Shammah” (1 Samuel 16:9, BSB)

content: How tall was Goliath?
explanation: That is about nine and a half feet. “He was six cubits and a span in height” (1 Samuel 17:4, BSB)

content: How much did the iron point of Goliath's spear weigh?
explanation: His spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. “and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels.” (1 Samuel 17:7, BSB)

content: What was Goliath's coat of mail made of?
explanation: It weighed five thousand shekels. “He wore a bronze coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels” (1 Samuel 17:5, BSB)

content: How many Philistines did David and his men kill to become Saul's son-in-law?
explanation: Then Saul gave him Michal. “David and his men went out and killed two hundred Philistines.” (1 Samuel 18:27, BSB)

content: In Jonathan's arrow signal, which words meant David had to flee?
options: The arrows are on this side
explanation: It meant the LORD was sending David away. “Look, the arrows are beyond you” (1 Samuel 20:22, BSB)

content: How many chosen men did Saul take to hunt David near En-gedi?
explanation: They searched the rocky hills. “So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel” (1 Samuel 24:2, BSB)

content: In which rocky region did Saul look for David near En-gedi?
options: The Rocks of the Wild Goats
explanation: David was hiding in the caves there. “in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.” (1 Samuel 24:2, BSB)

content: Nabal, Abigail's harsh husband, belonged to which clan?
explanation: He was evil in his dealings. “but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.” (1 Samuel 25:3, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, Paul says to rejoice how often?
explanation: Joy is for every day. “Rejoice at all times.” (1 Thessalonians 5:16, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, Paul says to pray how?
explanation: Stay close to God always. “Pray without ceasing.” (1 Thessalonians 5:17, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, in what circumstances should we give thanks?
explanation: This is God's will for you. “Give thanks in every circumstance, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.” (1 Thessalonians 5:18, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, the Day of the Lord will come like what?
explanation: No one knows the hour. “the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.” (1 Thessalonians 5:2, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, where will believers meet the Lord when He comes?
explanation: We will always be with the Lord. “to meet the Lord in the air. And so we will always be with the Lord.” (1 Thessalonians 4:17, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, Paul tells believers to encourage and do what to one another?
explanation: They were already doing it. “Therefore encourage and build one another up” (1 Thessalonians 5:11, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, after describing the Lord's coming, what does Paul say to do with these words?
explanation: They bring hope. “Therefore encourage one another with these words.” (1 Thessalonians 4:18, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, after testing all things, what should you hold fast to?
explanation: Avoid every form of evil. “but test all things. Hold fast to what is good.” (1 Thessalonians 5:21, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, why did Paul write about those who sleep in death?
explanation: Believers have hope. “so that you will not grieve like the rest, who are without hope.” (1 Thessalonians 4:13, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, who will rise first when the Lord descends?
explanation: Then the living will be caught up. “and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.” (1 Thessalonians 4:16, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, which instrument of God will sound when the Lord descends?
explanation: With the voice of an archangel. “and with the trumpet of God” (1 Thessalonians 4:16, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, Paul says he was gentle among them like whom?
explanation: He cared deeply for them. “we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother caring for her children.” (1 Thessalonians 2:7, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, Paul remembers their work of faith and labor of what?
explanation: And their enduring hope. “your work of faith, your labor of love, and your enduring hope” (1 Thessalonians 1:3, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, Paul urges believers to work with their own what?
explanation: Live quietly. “and to work with your own hands” (1 Thessalonians 4:11, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, from what should believers abstain?
explanation: Hold fast to good. “Abstain from every form of evil.” (1 Thessalonians 5:22, BSB)

content: Besides Paul and Timothy, who sent 1 Thessalonians?
explanation: Silvanus is also called Silas. “Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, To the church of the Thessalonians” (1 Thessalonians 1:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, whom did Paul send to strengthen the believers' faith?
explanation: He was Paul's fellow worker. “We sent Timothy, our brother and fellow worker for God” (1 Thessalonians 3:2, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, whose voice will be heard when the Lord descends?
explanation: With a loud command. “with the voice of an archangel” (1 Thessalonians 4:16, BSB)

content: In 1 Thessalonians, Paul urges believers to aspire to live how?
explanation: Mind your own matters. “and to aspire to live quietly” (1 Thessalonians 4:11, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, what does Paul call Timothy?
options: My true child in the faith
explanation: Paul was like a spiritual father. “To Timothy, my true child in the faith” (1 Timothy 1:2, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, Paul tells Timothy not to let anyone despise his what?
explanation: Young people can set an example. “Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers” (1 Timothy 4:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, why does Paul say Christ Jesus came into the world?
explanation: Paul called himself the worst. “Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst.” (1 Timothy 1:15, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, what is called a root of all kinds of evil?
explanation: Craving it leads people astray. “For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil.” (1 Timothy 6:10, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, godliness with contentment is what?
explanation: We brought nothing into the world. “Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain.” (1 Timothy 6:6, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, Paul tells Timothy to fight the good fight of what?
explanation: Take hold of eternal life. “Fight the good fight of the faith.” (1 Timothy 6:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, who is the one mediator between God and men?
explanation: There is one God and one mediator. “and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus” (1 Timothy 2:5, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, physical exercise has some value, but what is valuable in every way?
explanation: It holds promise for this life and the next. “but godliness is valuable in every way” (1 Timothy 4:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, what did we bring into the world?
explanation: We cannot carry anything out. “For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it.” (1 Timothy 6:7, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, with what two things should we be content?
explanation: Contentment is great gain. “But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these.” (1 Timothy 6:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, a person who wants to be an overseer desires what?
explanation: Church leadership is good work. “If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.” (1 Timothy 3:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, in which city did Paul urge Timothy to stay?
explanation: To stop false teaching. “you should stay on at Ephesus to instruct certain men not to teach false doctrines” (1 Timothy 1:3, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, what did Paul advise Timothy to use because of his stomach?
explanation: He had frequent ailments. “Stop drinking only water and use a little wine instead, because of your stomach” (1 Timothy 5:23, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, in which areas should young Timothy set an example?
explanation: Youth is no excuse. “set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.” (1 Timothy 4:12, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, if God's people humble themselves and pray, what will He heal?
explanation: He will hear and forgive. “then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.” (2 Chronicles 7:14, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, when Solomon finished praying, what came down from heaven?
explanation: It consumed the offerings. “When Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering” (2 Chronicles 7:1, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, what did Solomon ask God for to lead the people?
explanation: God gave him riches too. “Now grant me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may lead this people.” (2 Chronicles 1:10, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, when a vast army came against Judah, to whom did the battle belong?
explanation: Do not be afraid. “for the battle does not belong to you, but to God.” (2 Chronicles 20:15, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, who went out in front of King Jehoshaphat's army?
explanation: God set ambushes for the enemy. “and appointed those who would sing to the LORD and praise the splendor of His holiness.” (2 Chronicles 20:21, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, which queen came to test Solomon with hard questions?
explanation: She brought camels with spices and gold. “Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon, she came to test him with difficult questions.” (2 Chronicles 9:1, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, why could the priests not minister in the new temple?
explanation: God's glory filled the house. “so that the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud” (2 Chronicles 5:14, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, what did the singers proclaim when the temple filled with a cloud?
explanation: His love endures forever. “For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.” (2 Chronicles 5:13, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, where do the eyes of the LORD roam?
explanation: He strengthens the fully devoted. “For the eyes of the LORD roam to and fro over all the earth” (2 Chronicles 16:9, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, what broke out on King Uzziah when he burned incense in the temple?
explanation: Only priests could burn incense. “leprosy broke out on his forehead.” (2 Chronicles 26:19, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, King Hezekiah said Assyria had only what on its side?
explanation: God was with Judah. “With him is only the arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God to help us” (2 Chronicles 32:8, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, after God answered his prayer, what did King Manasseh know?
explanation: He humbled himself in distress. “Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.” (2 Chronicles 33:13, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, which Persian king did God stir to send a proclamation?
explanation: It fulfilled Jeremiah's word. “the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia to send a proclamation” (2 Chronicles 36:22, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, what did Cyrus say God appointed him to build?
explanation: God's people could go home. “has appointed me to build a house for Him at Jerusalem in Judah.” (2 Chronicles 36:23, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, how many years did King Joash reign in Jerusalem?
explanation: He began at seven years old. “and he reigned in Jerusalem forty years.” (2 Chronicles 24:1, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, which priest went in after King Uzziah to stop him?
explanation: Eighty brave priests went with him. “Then Azariah the priest, along with eighty brave priests of the LORD, went in after him.” (2 Chronicles 26:17, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, in which year of his reign did young Josiah begin to seek God?
explanation: He later cleansed Judah of idols. “In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, Josiah began to seek the God of his father David” (2 Chronicles 34:3, BSB)

content: In 2 Chronicles, when did the LORD set ambushes against Judah's enemies?
explanation: Praise came before victory. “The moment they began their shouts and praises, the LORD set ambushes” (2 Chronicles 20:22, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says anyone in Christ is a new what?
explanation: The old has passed away. “Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” (2 Corinthians 5:17, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says we walk by faith, not by what?
explanation: We trust what we cannot see. “For we walk by faith, not by sight.” (2 Corinthians 5:7, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, what kind of giver does God love?
explanation: Give from the heart. “For God loves a cheerful giver.” (2 Corinthians 9:7, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, the Lord told Paul, “My grace is sufficient for…”
explanation: His power is perfected in weakness. “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” (2 Corinthians 12:9, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says, “When I am weak, then I am…”
explanation: Christ's power rests on him. “For when I am weak, then I am strong.” (2 Corinthians 12:10, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, Paul calls God the God of all what?
explanation: He comforts us in all troubles. “the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort” (2 Corinthians 1:3, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says we have this treasure in jars made of what?
explanation: The power is from God, not us. “Now we have this treasure in jars of clay” (2 Corinthians 4:7, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says believers are ambassadors for whom?
explanation: God appeals through us. “Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ” (2 Corinthians 5:20, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, how many times did Paul say he was shipwrecked?
explanation: He suffered much for the gospel. “three times I was shipwrecked.” (2 Corinthians 11:25, BSB)

content: How does Paul close 2 Corinthians?
explanation: Grace, love, and fellowship. “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.” (2 Corinthians 13:14, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, why does God comfort us in our troubles?
explanation: Comfort is passed on. “so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.” (2 Corinthians 1:4, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, what is being renewed day by day?
explanation: So we do not lose heart. “yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.” (2 Corinthians 4:16, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, what does Paul say is eternal?
explanation: What is seen is temporary. “For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.” (2 Corinthians 4:18, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, Paul calls the believers a letter from Christ written on what?
explanation: Written by the Spirit, not ink. “not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.” (2 Corinthians 3:3, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, though Christ was rich, what did He become for our sakes?
explanation: So we might become rich. “that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor” (2 Corinthians 8:9, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, whoever sows generously will also do what?
explanation: Generosity brings blessing. “and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.” (2 Corinthians 9:6, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, what was Paul given to keep him from becoming conceited?
explanation: He pleaded for it to be removed. “I was given a thorn in my flesh” (2 Corinthians 12:7, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, how many times did Paul plead for his thorn to be taken away?
explanation: God's grace was enough. “Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.” (2 Corinthians 12:8, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, how did Paul escape the governor in Damascus?
explanation: Through a window in the wall. “But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp.” (2 Corinthians 11:33, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, Paul asks what fellowship light has with what?
explanation: Do not be unequally yoked. “Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?” (2 Corinthians 6:14, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, in whom should anyone who boasts boast?
explanation: All credit belongs to God. “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.” (2 Corinthians 10:17, BSB)

content: Who joined Paul in greeting the church at Corinth in 2 Corinthians?
explanation: The letter also went to Achaia. “and Timothy our brother, To the church of God in Corinth” (2 Corinthians 1:1, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says a man in Christ was caught up to which heaven?
explanation: It was fourteen years earlier. “was caught up to the third heaven.” (2 Corinthians 12:2, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, under which king did the Damascus governor try to arrest Paul?
explanation: Paul escaped in a basket. “In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas secured the city” (2 Corinthians 11:32, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, whose arrival comforted Paul?
explanation: God comforts the downcast. “comforted us by the arrival of Titus” (2 Corinthians 7:6, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, how many times did Paul receive forty lashes minus one?
explanation: He listed his sufferings. “Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.” (2 Corinthians 11:24, BSB)

content: In 2 Corinthians, how long did Paul say he spent in the open sea?
explanation: It was after a shipwreck. “I spent a night and a day in the open sea.” (2 Corinthians 11:25, BSB)

content: In 2 John, how does the writer call himself?
explanation: He wrote to the chosen lady. “The elder, To the chosen lady and her children” (2 John 1:1, BSB)

content: In 2 John, what old command does the elder urge?
explanation: It was from the beginning. “that we love one another.” (2 John 1:5, BSB)

content: In 2 John, why was the elder overjoyed?
explanation: As the Father commanded. “I was overjoyed to find some of your children walking in the truth” (2 John 1:4, BSB)

content: In 2 John, how does the elder define love?
explanation: Love obeys God. “And this is love, that we walk according to His commandments.” (2 John 1:6, BSB)

content: In 2 John, why did the elder not write more with paper and ink?
options: He hoped to visit face to face
explanation: So their joy would be complete. “Instead, I hope to come and speak with you face to face, so that our joy may be complete.” (2 John 1:12, BSB)

content: When Elijah told Elisha to stay behind, what did Elisha answer?
explanation: He said it three times. “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” (2 Kings 2:2, BSB)

content: How did Elijah part the waters of the Jordan?
explanation: The two crossed on dry ground. “And Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the waters” (2 Kings 2:8, BSB)

content: Before Elijah was taken away, what did Elisha ask to inherit?
options: A double portion of his spirit
explanation: Elijah said it was a hard request. “Please, let me inherit a double portion of your spirit” (2 Kings 2:9, BSB)

content: What appeared and separated Elijah from Elisha?
explanation: It had horses of fire. “suddenly a chariot of fire with horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them” (2 Kings 2:11, BSB)

content: How did Elijah go up into heaven?
explanation: He did not die. “and Elijah went up into heaven in a whirlwind.” (2 Kings 2:11, BSB)

content: After Elijah went up to heaven, what did Elisha pick up?
explanation: It had fallen from Elijah. “Elisha also picked up the cloak that had fallen from Elijah” (2 Kings 2:13, BSB)

content: When Elisha struck the Jordan with Elijah's cloak, what happened?
explanation: God was with Elisha now. “And when he had struck the waters, they parted to the right and to the left, and Elisha crossed over.” (2 Kings 2:14, BSB)

content: What did the woman of Shunem persuade Elisha to do when he passed by?
explanation: She was kind to the prophet. “a prominent woman who lived there persuaded him to have a meal.” (2 Kings 4:8, BSB)

content: What did the Shunammite woman and her husband make for Elisha?
explanation: It had a bed, table, chair, and lamp. “Please let us make a small room upstairs and put in it a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp for him.” (2 Kings 4:10, BSB)

content: What was the name of Elisha's servant at the Shunammite woman's house?
explanation: He called the woman for Elisha. “And he said to Gehazi his servant, “Call the Shunammite woman.”” (2 Kings 4:12, BSB)

content: What did the kind Shunammite woman not have?
explanation: Her husband was old. “Well, she has no son” (2 Kings 4:14, BSB)

content: What did Elisha promise the Shunammite woman?
explanation: God kept the promise. “At this time next year, you will hold a son in your arms.” (2 Kings 4:16, BSB)

content: When Elisha prayed over the Shunammite's son, what did the boy do?
explanation: Then he opened his eyes. “and the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.” (2 Kings 4:35, BSB)

content: After the boy came back to life, what did Elisha tell the Shunammite woman?
explanation: She bowed at his feet. “Pick up your son.” (2 Kings 4:36, BSB)

content: Who was Naaman?
explanation: He was great, but had leprosy. “Now Naaman, the commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man” (2 Kings 5:1, BSB)

content: What disease did the army commander Naaman have?
explanation: He was mighty, yet sick. “And he was a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.” (2 Kings 5:1, BSB)

content: Who told Naaman's wife about the prophet who could heal him?
explanation: She served Naaman's wife. “If only my master would go to the prophet who is in Samaria, he would cure him of his leprosy.” (2 Kings 5:3, BSB)

content: How many times did Elisha tell Naaman to wash in the Jordan?
explanation: Then he would be clean. “Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan” (2 Kings 5:10, BSB)

content: How did Naaman first react to Elisha's message to wash in the Jordan?
explanation: He expected something grand. “But Naaman went away angry” (2 Kings 5:11, BSB)

content: After dipping in the Jordan, what was Naaman's skin like?
explanation: He was clean. “and his flesh was restored and became like that of a little child, and he was clean.” (2 Kings 5:14, BSB)

content: When healed Naaman offered Elisha a gift, what did Elisha do?
explanation: God's healing was free. “I will not accept it.” (2 Kings 5:16, BSB)

content: How old was Josiah when he became king of Judah?
explanation: He reigned thirty-one years. “Josiah was eight years old when he became king” (2 Kings 22:1, BSB)
tags: King Josiah Finds the Book of the Law

content: How did young King Josiah live?
explanation: He walked in David's ways. “And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD” (2 Kings 22:2, BSB)
tags: King Josiah Finds the Book of the Law

content: In King Josiah's time, what did the high priest find in the temple?
explanation: It had been forgotten. “I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD!” (2 Kings 22:8, BSB)
tags: King Josiah Finds the Book of the Law

content: When King Josiah heard the Book of the Law read, what did he do?
explanation: He was grieved by Judah's sin. “When the king heard the words of the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes” (2 Kings 22:11, BSB)
tags: King Josiah Finds the Book of the Law

content: What did King Josiah read to all the people in the temple?
explanation: Everyone, small and great, heard it. “and in their hearing he read all the words of the Book of the Covenant” (2 Kings 23:2, BSB)
tags: King Josiah Finds the Book of the Law

content: What did King Josiah make before the LORD after reading the law?
explanation: All the people joined it. “So the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the LORD” (2 Kings 23:3, BSB)
tags: King Josiah Finds the Book of the Law

content: How did King Josiah turn to the LORD?
explanation: No king was like him. “who turned to the LORD with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength” (2 Kings 23:25, BSB)
tags: King Josiah Finds the Book of the Law

content: As Elijah went up, what did Elisha cry out?
explanation: He called him the chariots of Israel. “My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!” (2 Kings 2:12, BSB)

content: What sign did Elijah give that Elisha would receive a double portion?
explanation: Elisha did see it. “if you see me as I am taken from you, it will be yours.” (2 Kings 2:10, BSB)

content: When a poor widow asked Elisha for help, what did she have in her house?
explanation: God multiplied it. “Your servant has nothing in the house but a jar of oil.” (2 Kings 4:2, BSB)

content: In the miracle of the widow's oil, when did the oil stop flowing?
options: When there were no more jars
explanation: She sold it to pay her debt. “But he replied, “There are no more jars.” Then the oil stopped flowing.” (2 Kings 4:6, BSB)

content: Which rivers did Naaman think were better than Israel's waters?
explanation: They were rivers of Damascus. “Are not the Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?” (2 Kings 5:12, BSB)

content: Who persuaded angry Naaman to wash in the Jordan?
explanation: They called it a simple command. “Naaman’s servants, however, approached him” (2 Kings 5:13, BSB)

content: What happened to Gehazi after he chased Naaman for a gift?
explanation: Naaman's leprosy clung to him. “And as Gehazi left his presence, he was leprous—as white as snow.” (2 Kings 5:27, BSB)

content: When a borrowed axe head fell into the water, what did Elisha make it do?
explanation: He threw a stick in the water. “the man of God cut a stick, threw it there, and made the iron float.” (2 Kings 6:6, BSB)

content: When God opened his servant's eyes, what did he see around Elisha?
explanation: God's army protected them. “he saw that the hills were full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.” (2 Kings 6:17, BSB)

content: Surrounded by enemies, what did Elisha tell his frightened servant?
explanation: God's army was greater. “for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.” (2 Kings 6:16, BSB)

content: How old was Joash when he became king?
explanation: He was one of Judah's youngest kings. “Joash was seven years old when he became king.” (2 Kings 11:21, BSB)

content: Which empire captured Samaria and carried Israel away?
explanation: It was in Hoshea's ninth year. “the king of Assyria captured Samaria and carried away the Israelites to Assyria” (2 Kings 17:6, BSB)

content: Which king of Judah trusted the LORD so that no king was like him?
explanation: He removed the high places. “Hezekiah trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel.” (2 Kings 18:5, BSB)

content: How many years did God add to King Hezekiah's life?
explanation: God heard his prayer and saw his tears. “I will add fifteen years to your life.” (2 Kings 20:6, BSB)

content: As a sign for Hezekiah, what went back ten steps?
explanation: It was on the stairway of Ahaz. “and He brought the shadow back the ten steps it had descended on the stairway of Ahaz.” (2 Kings 20:11, BSB)

content: When Babylon took Jerusalem, what happened to the house of the LORD?
explanation: The walls were broken down too. “He burned down the house of the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem” (2 Kings 25:9, BSB)

content: From which town were Elijah and Elisha traveling just before Elijah was taken up?
explanation: They went on to Bethel and Jericho. “Elijah and Elisha were on their way from Gilgal” (2 Kings 2:1, BSB)

content: How many sons of the prophets watched from a distance at the Jordan?
explanation: They saw Elijah part the water. “Then a company of fifty of the sons of the prophets went and stood at a distance” (2 Kings 2:7, BSB)

content: On the road to Bethel, what did a group of boys jeer at Elisha?
explanation: They mocked the prophet. “Go up, you baldhead! Go up, you baldhead!” (2 Kings 2:23, BSB)

content: How many sets of clothing did Naaman take to Israel?
explanation: He also took silver and gold. “taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten sets of clothing.” (2 Kings 5:5, BSB)

content: What was the name of the bronze snake King Hezekiah destroyed?
explanation: People burned incense to it. “He also demolished the bronze snake called Nehushtan that Moses had made” (2 Kings 18:4, BSB)

content: How many years did Hezekiah reign in Jerusalem?
explanation: He became king at twenty-five. “and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years.” (2 Kings 18:2, BSB)

content: How many Assyrians did the angel of the LORD strike in one night?
explanation: God defended Jerusalem. “and struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians.” (2 Kings 19:35, BSB)

content: What did Isaiah have placed on King Hezekiah's boil?
explanation: Hezekiah recovered. “Prepare a poultice of figs.” (2 Kings 20:7, BSB)

content: Which high priest found the Book of the Law in King Josiah's day?
explanation: He gave it to Shaphan the scribe. “Then Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe” (2 Kings 22:8, BSB)

content: Which scribe read the newly found Book of the Law to King Josiah?
explanation: The king tore his clothes. “And Shaphan read it in the presence of the king.” (2 Kings 22:10, BSB)

content: Who was the Babylonian captain of the guard who burned Jerusalem?
explanation: He served the king of Babylon. “Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.” (2 Kings 25:8, BSB)

content: In 2 Peter, with the Lord a day is like how many years?
explanation: God is not bound by time. “With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.” (2 Peter 3:8, BSB)

content: In 2 Peter, why is the Lord patient?
explanation: He does not want anyone to perish. “not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance.” (2 Peter 3:9, BSB)

content: In 2 Peter, how will the Day of the Lord come?
explanation: No one knows the time. “But the Day of the Lord will come like a thief.” (2 Peter 3:10, BSB)

content: In 2 Peter, in what should believers grow?
explanation: To Him be the glory. “But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.” (2 Peter 3:18, BSB)

content: In 2 Peter, how did the prophets speak from God?
explanation: Prophecy did not come from man. “but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.” (2 Peter 1:21, BSB)

content: In 2 Peter, Peter says he did not follow fables but was an eyewitness of what?
explanation: He saw it on the holy mountain. “but we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.” (2 Peter 1:16, BSB)

content: In 2 Peter, what did the voice from the Majestic Glory say about Jesus?
explanation: God was well pleased with Him. “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” (2 Peter 1:17, BSB)

content: In 2 Peter, whom does Peter call a preacher of righteousness?
explanation: God preserved him in the flood. “but preserved Noah, a preacher of righteousness, among the eight” (2 Peter 2:5, BSB)

content: In 2 Peter, which brother does Peter mention as writing with God's wisdom?
explanation: Peter calls him beloved. “just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote you with the wisdom God gave him.” (2 Peter 3:15, BSB)

content: In 2 Peter, where did Peter hear the voice from heaven?
explanation: He was with Jesus there. “And we ourselves heard this voice from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.” (2 Peter 1:18, BSB)

content: After Saul and Jonathan died, what did David take up for them?
explanation: David mourned his king and his friend. “Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan” (2 Samuel 1:17, BSB)

content: After Saul's death, the men of Judah anointed David king in which town?
explanation: He first ruled only Judah. “Then the men of Judah came to Hebron, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah.” (2 Samuel 2:4, BSB)

content: How old was David when he became king?
explanation: He reigned forty years. “David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years.” (2 Samuel 5:4, BSB)

content: What fortress did King David capture, later called the City of David?
explanation: It became his capital, Jerusalem. “Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David).” (2 Samuel 5:7, BSB)

content: As the ark was brought to Jerusalem, what did King David do before the LORD?
explanation: He rejoiced in God. “And David, wearing a linen ephod, danced with all his might before the LORD” (2 Samuel 6:14, BSB)

content: Why was King David troubled about his cedar house?
options: God's ark was in a tent
explanation: He wanted to build a house for God. “Here I am, living in a house of cedar, while the ark of God remains in a tent.” (2 Samuel 7:2, BSB)

content: What did God promise about King David's throne?
explanation: Jesus came from David's line. “Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me, and your throne will be established forever.” (2 Samuel 7:16, BSB)

content: For whose sake did King David want to show kindness to Saul's family?
explanation: Jonathan had been his loyal friend. “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?” (2 Samuel 9:1, BSB)

content: What did King David promise Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth?
options: To always eat at his table
explanation: David kept his promise to Jonathan. “and you will always eat at my table.” (2 Samuel 9:7, BSB)

content: Which prophet did the LORD send to King David after his sin with Bathsheba?
explanation: He told a story to show David his sin. “Then the LORD sent Nathan to David” (2 Samuel 12:1, BSB)

content: In Nathan's story to David, what did the poor man own?
explanation: The rich man took it. “but the poor man had nothing except one small ewe lamb that he had bought.” (2 Samuel 12:3, BSB)

content: After his story about the stolen lamb, what did Nathan tell David?
explanation: David saw his own sin. “You are that man!” (2 Samuel 12:7, BSB)

content: When confronted by Nathan, what did King David confess?
options: I have sinned against the LORD
explanation: God took away his sin. “I have sinned against the LORD.” (2 Samuel 12:13, BSB)

content: What did David and Bathsheba name the son the LORD loved?
explanation: He later became king. “So she gave birth to a son, and they named him Solomon. Now the LORD loved the child” (2 Samuel 12:24, BSB)

content: In his song of praise, what did King David call the LORD?
explanation: God was his safe place. “The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer.” (2 Samuel 22:2, BSB)

content: In David's lament, Saul and Jonathan were swifter than what?
explanation: They were also stronger than lions. “They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.” (2 Samuel 1:23, BSB)

content: During the long war between Saul's house and David's house, who grew stronger?
explanation: Saul's house grew weaker. “And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.” (2 Samuel 3:1, BSB)

content: Which people held Jerusalem before King David captured it?
explanation: They said David could never get in. “Now the king and his men marched to Jerusalem against the Jebusites who inhabited the land.” (2 Samuel 5:6, BSB)

content: Which king sent cedar logs and builders to build King David's palace?
explanation: Tyre was famous for cedar. “Now Hiram king of Tyre sent envoys to David, along with cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons” (2 Samuel 5:11, BSB)

content: Whose house was blessed while God's ark stayed there before going to Jerusalem?
explanation: Then David brought the ark up with joy. “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God.” (2 Samuel 6:12, BSB)

content: Who looked from a window and despised King David for dancing before the ark?
explanation: David was worshiping with all his heart. “Saul’s daughter Michal looked down from a window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD” (2 Samuel 6:16, BSB)

content: God told David that his descendant, not David, would build what?
explanation: Solomon built the temple. “He will build a house for My Name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.” (2 Samuel 7:13, BSB)

content: What did Ziba tell King David about Jonathan's surviving son?
options: He was lame in both feet
explanation: David still welcomed him. “There is still Jonathan’s son, who is lame in both feet.” (2 Samuel 9:3, BSB)

content: What was the name of Jonathan's son whom King David welcomed?
explanation: He fell facedown before David. “And when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown in reverence.” (2 Samuel 9:6, BSB)

content: Bathsheba was the wife of which soldier in King David's army?
explanation: David sinned against him. “This is Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite.” (2 Samuel 11:3, BSB)

content: In Nathan's story, how many times over did David say the rich man must pay for the lamb?
explanation: David was angry before he saw his own sin. “he must pay for the lamb four times over.” (2 Samuel 12:6, BSB)

content: Which of David's sons stole the hearts of the men of Israel?
explanation: He turned people against the king. “In this way he stole the hearts of the men of Israel.” (2 Samuel 15:6, BSB)

content: When Absalom rode under a large oak, what got caught in the tree?
explanation: He was left hanging in midair. “Absalom’s head was caught fast in the tree.” (2 Samuel 18:9, BSB)

content: What did King David cry out when he heard Absalom had died?
explanation: He wished he had died instead. “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom!” (2 Samuel 18:33, BSB)

content: When his mighty men brought water from Bethlehem's well, what did David do?
options: Poured it out to the LORD
