explanation: They had risked their lives for it. “But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out to the LORD” (2 Samuel 23:16, BSB)

content: Why did King David insist on paying for the threshing floor?
explanation: True worship costs something. “for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” (2 Samuel 24:24, BSB)

content: How long did David reign over Judah in Hebron?
explanation: Then he reigned in Jerusalem. “In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months” (2 Samuel 5:5, BSB)

content: How many years did David reign in Jerusalem over all Israel and Judah?
explanation: His total reign was forty years. “and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.” (2 Samuel 5:5, BSB)

content: How old was Mephibosheth when his nurse dropped him and he became lame?
explanation: She was fleeing after Saul's death. “He was five years old when the report about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel.” (2 Samuel 4:4, BSB)

content: In which town was Mephibosheth living when David asked for him?
explanation: He was at the house of Machir. “he is in Lo-debar at the house of Machir son of Ammiel.” (2 Samuel 9:4, BSB)

content: Who was the servant of Saul's family who told David about Mephibosheth?
explanation: He was summoned to the king. “And there was a servant of Saul’s family named Ziba.” (2 Samuel 9:2, BSB)

content: How long did the ark stay at Obed-edom's house?
explanation: The LORD blessed his household. “Thus the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months” (2 Samuel 6:11, BSB)

content: In his last words, what does David call himself?
explanation: He wrote many psalms. “and the sweet psalmist of Israel” (2 Samuel 23:1, BSB)

content: How much did David pay for the threshing floor and oxen?
explanation: He refused it as a gift. “So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.” (2 Samuel 24:24, BSB)

content: What was David wearing when he danced before the ark?
explanation: He worshiped humbly. “And David, wearing a linen ephod, danced with all his might before the LORD” (2 Samuel 6:14, BSB)

content: In 2 Thessalonians, Paul says the Lord is faithful and will guard you from whom?
explanation: He will strengthen you. “But the Lord is faithful, and He will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.” (2 Thessalonians 3:3, BSB)

content: In 2 Thessalonians, what did Paul say about anyone unwilling to work?
explanation: Everyone should do their part. “If anyone is unwilling to work, he shall not eat.” (2 Thessalonians 3:10, BSB)

content: In 2 Thessalonians, Paul tells the brothers not to grow weary in what?
explanation: Keep doing good. “But as for you, brothers, do not grow weary in well-doing.” (2 Thessalonians 3:13, BSB)

content: In 2 Thessalonians, what false claim alarmed the believers?
options: The Day of the Lord had come
explanation: Paul told them not to be shaken. “alleging that the Day of the Lord has already come.” (2 Thessalonians 2:2, BSB)

content: In 2 Thessalonians, how did Paul mark his letters as truly his?
options: A greeting in his own hand
explanation: It was his mark in every letter. “This greeting is in my own hand—Paul. This is my mark in every letter” (2 Thessalonians 3:17, BSB)

content: Who sent 2 Thessalonians together with Paul and Timothy?
explanation: The same three wrote 1 Thessalonians. “Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, To the church of the Thessalonians” (2 Thessalonians 1:1, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, Paul says all Scripture is what?
explanation: It comes from God. “All Scripture is God-breathed” (2 Timothy 3:16, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, what is God-breathed Scripture useful for?
explanation: And training in righteousness. “and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness” (2 Timothy 3:16, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, since when had Timothy known the Holy Scriptures?
explanation: His family taught him. “From infancy you have known the Holy Scriptures” (2 Timothy 3:15, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, the Scriptures make you wise for what?
explanation: Through faith in Christ Jesus. “which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.” (2 Timothy 3:15, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, Scripture equips the man of God for every what?
explanation: He becomes complete. “so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.” (2 Timothy 3:17, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, what does Paul tell Timothy to continue in?
explanation: He knew who taught him. “But as for you, continue in the things you have learned and firmly believed” (2 Timothy 3:14, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, right after describing God-breathed Scripture, what does Paul charge Timothy to preach?
explanation: In season and out of season. “Preach the word; be prepared in season and out of season” (2 Timothy 4:2, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, God has not given us a spirit of what?
explanation: He gives power, love, and self-control. “For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.” (2 Timothy 1:7, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, near the end of his life, what did Paul say he had kept?
explanation: He finished the race. “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.” (2 Timothy 4:7, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, in whom did Timothy's sincere faith first dwell?
explanation: Then in his mother Eunice. “which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice” (2 Timothy 1:5, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, Paul tells Timothy to suffer like a good what?
explanation: A soldier of Christ Jesus. “Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.” (2 Timothy 2:3, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, a workman approved by God accurately handles what?
explanation: He has no need to be ashamed. “an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.” (2 Timothy 2:15, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, what crown did Paul say was laid up for him?
explanation: The Lord will award it. “From now on there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness” (2 Timothy 4:8, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, what will come in the last days?
explanation: People will love themselves and money. “In the last days terrible times will come.” (2 Timothy 3:1, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, what was the name of Timothy's mother?
explanation: Her faith lived in Timothy. “and your mother Eunice” (2 Timothy 1:5, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, who was the only one still with Paul?
explanation: Paul asked for Mark too. “Only Luke is with me.” (2 Timothy 4:11, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, whom did Paul ask Timothy to bring because he was useful?
explanation: Useful in the ministry. “Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is useful to me in the ministry.” (2 Timothy 4:11, BSB)

content: In 2 Timothy, where had Paul left his cloak with Carpus?
explanation: He also wanted his scrolls. “bring the cloak that I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.” (2 Timothy 4:13, BSB)

content: To whom did the elder write 3 John?
explanation: He loved him in the truth. “The elder, To the beloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth” (3 John 1:1, BSB)

content: In 3 John, what is the elder's greatest joy?
explanation: Faithfulness brings joy. “I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth.” (3 John 1:4, BSB)

content: In 3 John, the elder says do not imitate evil, but imitate what?
explanation: The one who does good is of God. “Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good.” (3 John 1:11, BSB)

content: In 3 John, what does the elder pray Gaius will enjoy?
explanation: As his soul prospers. “I pray that in every way you may prosper and enjoy good health, as your soul also prospers.” (3 John 1:2, BSB)

content: In 3 John, who loved to be first and would not accept the elder?
explanation: He rejected the elder's instruction. “but Diotrephes, who loves to be first, will not accept our instruction.” (3 John 1:9, BSB)

content: In 3 John, who received a good testimony from everyone?
explanation: Even the truth spoke for him. “Demetrius has received a good testimony from everyone, and from the truth itself.” (3 John 1:12, BSB)

content: After rising from the dead, for how many days did Jesus appear to His apostles?
explanation: He spoke about the kingdom of God. “He appeared to them over a span of forty days” (Acts 1:3, BSB)

content: Before going up to heaven, which city did Jesus tell His apostles not to leave?
explanation: They were to wait for the Father's gift. “Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift the Father promised” (Acts 1:4, BSB)

content: Before going up to heaven, Jesus said His apostles would soon be baptized with what?
explanation: John had baptized with water. “in a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.” (Acts 1:5, BSB)

content: Before going up to heaven, what did Jesus say His apostles would receive when the Spirit came?
explanation: They would be His witnesses. “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you” (Acts 1:8, BSB)

content: Before going up to heaven, how far did Jesus say His witnesses would go?
options: To the ends of the earth
explanation: The good news is for everyone. “and to the ends of the earth.” (Acts 1:8, BSB)

content: As Jesus was taken up into heaven, what hid Him from the apostles' sight?
explanation: They watched Him go up. “they watched as He was taken up, and a cloud hid Him from their sight.” (Acts 1:9, BSB)

content: After Jesus went up to heaven, what did the two men in white promise?
options: He will come back the same way
explanation: Jesus will return. “will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven.” (Acts 1:11, BSB)

content: On which feast day were the believers all together when the Holy Spirit came?
explanation: They were in one place. “When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place.” (Acts 2:1, BSB)

content: On the day of Pentecost, what sound came from heaven and filled the house?
explanation: The Holy Spirit was coming. “Suddenly a sound like a mighty rushing wind came from heaven” (Acts 2:2, BSB)

content: On the day of Pentecost, what came to rest on each believer?
explanation: It was a sign of the Spirit. “They saw tongues like flames of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them.” (Acts 2:3, BSB)

content: On the day of Pentecost, after being filled with the Spirit, what did the believers do?
explanation: The Spirit enabled them. “began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them.” (Acts 2:4, BSB)

content: On the day of Pentecost, why was the crowd in Jerusalem amazed?
explanation: People came from every nation. “because each one heard them speaking his own language.” (Acts 2:6, BSB)

content: On the day of Pentecost, which apostle stood up and spoke to the crowd?
explanation: He stood with the Eleven. “Then Peter stood up with the Eleven, lifted up his voice, and addressed the crowd” (Acts 2:14, BSB)

content: About how many people were baptized after Peter's sermon at Pentecost?
explanation: They embraced his message. “about three thousand were added to the believers that day.” (Acts 2:41, BSB)

content: In the first church in Jerusalem, what did the believers devote themselves to?
explanation: These were the habits of the first church. “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.” (Acts 2:42, BSB)

content: How did the first believers in Jerusalem treat what they owned?
explanation: They cared for one another. “All the believers were together and had everything in common.” (Acts 2:44, BSB)

content: In the first church, why did believers sell their possessions?
options: To share with anyone in need
explanation: No one was left in need. “they shared with anyone who was in need.” (Acts 2:45, BSB)

content: In the first church in Jerusalem, how often did believers meet in the temple courts?
explanation: They broke bread in their homes too. “With one accord they continued to meet daily in the temple courts” (Acts 2:46, BSB)

content: Where did the first believers break bread together?
explanation: They shared meals with gladness. “and to break bread from house to house” (Acts 2:46, BSB)

content: In the first church, who added to their number daily?
explanation: Salvation is God's work. “And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.” (Acts 2:47, BSB)

content: In the first church, what came over everyone as the apostles did wonders?
explanation: God was at work among them. “A sense of awe came over everyone” (Acts 2:43, BSB)

content: At which temple gate did the man lame from birth sit and beg?
explanation: He was put there every day. “the temple gate called Beautiful” (Acts 3:2, BSB)

content: Who was going up to the temple with Peter when they met the lame man?
explanation: It was the hour of prayer. “One afternoon Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer” (Acts 3:1, BSB)

content: What did the lame man at the temple gate ask Peter and John for?
explanation: He begged every day. “he asked them for money.” (Acts 3:3, BSB)

content: What did Peter say he did not have to give the lame man?
explanation: He gave something better. “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you” (Acts 3:6, BSB)

content: In whose name did Peter tell the lame man to get up and walk?
explanation: The power was Jesus', not Peter's. “In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!” (Acts 3:6, BSB)

content: How did Peter help the lame man at the temple gate up?
options: Took him by the right hand
explanation: At once his feet grew strong. “Taking him by the right hand, Peter helped him up” (Acts 3:7, BSB)

content: After Peter healed him, what did the lame man do in the temple courts?
explanation: He was full of joy. “walking and leaping and praising God.” (Acts 3:8, BSB)

content: When the church chose seven helpers, who was described as full of faith and the Holy Spirit?
explanation: He was the first named of the seven. “They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit” (Acts 6:5, BSB)

content: Stephen, one of the seven chosen helpers, was full of grace and what else?
explanation: He did great wonders and signs. “Now Stephen, who was full of grace and power” (Acts 6:8, BSB)

content: Before he was stoned, whom did Stephen see standing at God's right hand?
explanation: He saw heaven open. “I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.” (Acts 7:56, BSB)

content: When Stephen was stoned, at whose feet did the witnesses lay their garments?
explanation: Saul later became Paul. “the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.” (Acts 7:58, BSB)

content: While he was being stoned, what did Stephen pray?
explanation: He trusted Jesus to the end. “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” (Acts 7:59, BSB)

content: What did Stephen ask God about the people who were stoning him?
options: Do not hold this sin against them
explanation: He forgave like Jesus did. “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” (Acts 7:60, BSB)

content: What broke out against the church on the day Stephen died?
explanation: The believers were scattered. “On that day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem” (Acts 8:1, BSB)

content: Who told Philip to go to the desert road toward Gaza?
explanation: God had someone for him to meet. “Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south to the desert road” (Acts 8:26, BSB)

content: On the desert road to Gaza, whom did Philip meet?
explanation: He was in charge of a queen's treasury. “on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official” (Acts 8:27, BSB)

content: Which prophet was the Ethiopian official reading in his chariot?
explanation: He was returning from worship. “was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.” (Acts 8:28, BSB)

content: What did Philip ask the Ethiopian official reading in his chariot?
options: Do you understand what you're reading?
explanation: The official needed a guide. ““Do you understand what you are reading?” Philip asked.” (Acts 8:30, BSB)

content: The Ethiopian official read a scripture about someone led like what to the slaughter?
explanation: Philip explained it was about Jesus. “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter” (Acts 8:32, BSB)

content: When they came to some water, what did Philip do for the Ethiopian official?
explanation: The official believed the good news. “Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.” (Acts 8:38, BSB)

content: After his baptism, how did the Ethiopian official go on his way?
explanation: He had found the good news. “but went on his way rejoicing.” (Acts 8:39, BSB)

content: To which city was Saul traveling to arrest followers of Jesus?
explanation: He carried letters from the high priest. “and requested letters to the synagogues in Damascus” (Acts 9:2, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: On the road to Damascus, what suddenly flashed around Saul?
explanation: Jesus was about to speak to him. “suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.” (Acts 9:3, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: On the road to Damascus, what did the voice from heaven ask Saul?
explanation: Hurting believers was hurting Jesus. “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?” (Acts 9:4, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: When Saul asked, “Who are You, Lord?” on the road, who answered?
explanation: Saul met the risen Jesus. “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting” (Acts 9:5, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: After meeting Jesus on the road to Damascus, how long was Saul blind?
explanation: He did not eat or drink. “For three days he was without sight” (Acts 9:9, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: Which disciple in Damascus placed his hands on blind Saul?
explanation: The Lord sent him in a vision. “So Ananias went to the house, and when he arrived, he placed his hands on Saul.” (Acts 9:17, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: When Ananias prayed for Saul in Damascus, what fell from Saul's eyes?
explanation: His sight was restored. “something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes” (Acts 9:18, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: Which king put Peter in prison during the Feast of Unleavened Bread?
explanation: He had already killed James. “He arrested him and put him in prison” (Acts 12:4, BSB)

content: While Herod kept Peter in prison, what was the church doing?
explanation: Prayer was their weapon. “but the church was fervently praying to God for him.” (Acts 12:5, BSB)

content: On the night before his trial under Herod, how was Peter sleeping?
explanation: He was bound with two chains. “Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains” (Acts 12:6, BSB)

content: When the angel woke Peter in Herod's prison, what fell off his wrists?
explanation: God set him free. “And the chains fell off his wrists.” (Acts 12:7, BSB)

content: As the angel led Peter out of prison, how did the iron gate open?
explanation: Nothing could stop God's rescue. “came to the iron gate leading to the city, which opened for them by itself.” (Acts 12:10, BSB)

content: After escaping prison, who answered when Peter knocked at the house gate?
explanation: Many were praying inside. “a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.” (Acts 12:13, BSB)

content: When Rhoda heard Peter's voice at the gate, what did she forget to do?
explanation: She was so overjoyed. “she was so overjoyed that she forgot to open the gate” (Acts 12:14, BSB)

content: Who was beaten and thrown into prison with Paul in Philippi?
explanation: The magistrates ordered it. “The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas” (Acts 16:22, BSB)

content: In the Philippian prison, what were Paul's and Silas's feet fastened in?
explanation: They were in the inner cell. “he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.” (Acts 16:24, BSB)

content: What were Paul and Silas doing in prison about midnight?
explanation: The other prisoners listened. “About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God” (Acts 16:25, BSB)

content: While Paul and Silas sang in prison, what shook the prison's foundations?
explanation: All the doors flew open. “Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison.” (Acts 16:26, BSB)

content: When the jailer was about to kill himself, what did Paul shout?
explanation: No prisoner had escaped. “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!” (Acts 16:28, BSB)

content: What did the Philippian jailer ask Paul and Silas?
options: What must I do to be saved?
explanation: He trembled before them. “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?” (Acts 16:30, BSB)

content: What did Paul and Silas tell the jailer he must do to be saved?
explanation: His household could be saved too. “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.” (Acts 16:31, BSB)

content: To which country was Paul sailing as a prisoner when the great storm struck?
explanation: He was going to stand before Caesar. “When it was decided that we would sail for Italy” (Acts 27:1, BSB)

content: In the great storm on Paul's ship, what did not appear for many days?
explanation: They lost all hope. “When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days” (Acts 27:20, BSB)

content: During the storm at sea, who stood beside Paul in the night?
explanation: He brought a message of hope. “For just last night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me” (Acts 27:23, BSB)

content: During the storm, what did Paul say would be the only loss?
explanation: No one would die. “you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.” (Acts 27:22, BSB)

content: When Paul's ship broke up, how many people reached land safely?
explanation: God kept His promise. “In this way everyone was brought safely to land.” (Acts 27:44, BSB)

content: On which island did Paul land after the shipwreck?
explanation: The islanders were very kind. “we learned that the island was called Malta.” (Acts 28:1, BSB)

content: After the shipwreck, what fastened onto Paul's hand by the fire?
explanation: He shook it off and was not hurt. “a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.” (Acts 28:3, BSB)

content: Who was chosen by lot to replace Judas as an apostle?
explanation: He joined the eleven apostles. “and the lot fell to Matthias; so he was added to the eleven apostles.” (Acts 1:26, BSB)

content: From which mountain did the apostles return after Jesus went up to heaven?
explanation: It is near Jerusalem. “Then they returned to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives” (Acts 1:12, BSB)

content: After Jesus went up to heaven, where did the apostles stay in Jerusalem?
explanation: They prayed together there. “they went to the upper room where they were staying” (Acts 1:13, BSB)

content: At Pentecost, what did Peter tell the crowd to do?
explanation: They would receive the Holy Spirit. “Repent and be baptized, every one of you” (Acts 2:38, BSB)

content: Peter said salvation is found in no other name except whose?
explanation: Peter was speaking of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. “Salvation exists in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved.” (Acts 4:12, BSB)

content: The leaders saw Peter and John were ordinary men but noticed they had been with whom?
explanation: Time with Jesus made them bold. “and took note that these men had been with Jesus.” (Acts 4:13, BSB)

content: What does the name Barnabas mean?
explanation: The apostles gave him this name. “whom the apostles called Barnabas (meaning Son of Encouragement)” (Acts 4:36, BSB)

content: By secretly keeping back money from the land, whom did Peter say Ananias had lied to?
explanation: Lying to the church was lying to God. “how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit” (Acts 5:3, BSB)

content: How did Saul's disciples help him escape from Damascus?
explanation: They let him down through the wall. “lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall.” (Acts 9:25, BSB)

content: In which city were believers in Jesus first given the name Christians?
explanation: Barnabas and Saul taught there a year. “The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.” (Acts 11:26, BSB)

content: By what other name was Saul also called?
explanation: He is best known by this name. “Then Saul, who was also called Paul” (Acts 13:9, BSB)

content: Who was Cornelius, the God-fearing man in Caesarea?
explanation: He was in the Italian Regiment. “a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was called the Italian Regiment.” (Acts 10:1, BSB)

content: In Peter's vision of the sheet, what did the voice say about what God made clean?
explanation: God welcomes all nations. “Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.” (Acts 10:15, BSB)

content: At Cornelius's house, what did Peter say he now truly understood about God?
explanation: God welcomes every nation. “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism” (Acts 10:34, BSB)

content: Which apostle did King Herod put to death with the sword?
explanation: Then Herod arrested Peter. “He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.” (Acts 12:2, BSB)

content: When Rhoda said Peter was at the gate, what did the praying believers say?
options: You are out of your mind
explanation: They found it hard to believe. ““You are out of your mind,” they told her.” (Acts 12:15, BSB)

content: After parting with Barnabas, whom did Paul choose as his new partner?
explanation: Barnabas took Mark to Cyprus. “but Paul chose Silas and left” (Acts 15:40, BSB)

content: In Philippi, what did Lydia sell?
explanation: The Lord opened her heart. “a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth” (Acts 16:14, BSB)

content: After believing, what did the Philippian jailer do for Paul and Silas that night?
explanation: Then he and his household were baptized. “At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds.” (Acts 16:33, BSB)

content: In Athens, what was written on the altar Paul found?
explanation: Paul told them about the true God. “TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.” (Acts 17:23, BSB)

content: What trade did Paul share with Aquila and Priscilla?
explanation: He worked to support himself. “because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.” (Acts 18:3, BSB)

content: Which young man fell asleep and fell from a window while Paul preached?
explanation: Paul talked on and on. “a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep” (Acts 20:9, BSB)

content: Paul quoted the Lord Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to do what?
explanation: We must help the weak. “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” (Acts 20:35, BSB)

content: On Malta, what did Paul do with the viper that bit his hand?
options: Shook it off into the fire
explanation: He suffered no harm. “But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.” (Acts 28:5, BSB)

content: How did Paul live during his two years in Rome?
explanation: He welcomed all who came. “Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house” (Acts 28:30, BSB)

content: About how many believers were gathered when Peter stood up to choose Judas's replacement?
explanation: They were waiting in Jerusalem. “(a gathering of about a hundred and twenty)” (Acts 1:15, BSB)

content: Besides Matthias, who was the other man proposed to replace Judas?
explanation: He was also known as Justus. “Joseph called Barsabbas (also known as Justus) and Matthias.” (Acts 1:23, BSB)

content: At what hour of prayer did Peter and John go up to the temple and heal the lame man?
explanation: It was afternoon. “at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.” (Acts 3:1, BSB)

content: After the lame man was healed, where did the astonished people run to Peter and John?
explanation: Peter then preached to them. “the walkway called Solomon’s Colonnade.” (Acts 3:11, BSB)

content: Barnabas was a Levite from which island?
explanation: He later sailed back there. “Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus” (Acts 4:36, BSB)

content: The Ethiopian official was in charge of the treasury of which queen?
explanation: She was queen of the Ethiopians. “in charge of the entire treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians.” (Acts 8:27, BSB)

content: On which street in Damascus was Saul staying when Ananias came?
explanation: He was at the house of Judas. “Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street” (Acts 9:11, BSB)

content: Saul of the Damascus road came from which city?
explanation: The Lord named it to Ananias. “a man from Tarsus named Saul” (Acts 9:11, BSB)

content: How many squads of soldiers did Herod use to guard Peter in prison?
explanation: Herod wanted no escape. “handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each.” (Acts 12:4, BSB)

content: After escaping prison, Peter went to the house of Mary, the mother of whom?
explanation: Many were praying there. “he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark” (Acts 12:12, BSB)

content: In Lystra, the crowd called Paul Hermes. What did they call Barnabas?
explanation: Paul was the chief speaker. “Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes” (Acts 14:12, BSB)

content: Lydia, the seller of purple cloth, came from which city?
explanation: She listened to Paul in Philippi. “a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira” (Acts 16:14, BSB)

content: How many people were on board Paul's ship before the shipwreck?
explanation: All of them reached land. “In all, there were 276 of us on board.” (Acts 27:37, BSB)

content: What was the name of the centurion who guarded Paul on the voyage to Italy?
explanation: He belonged to the Imperial Regiment. “were handed over to a centurion named Julius” (Acts 27:1, BSB)

content: In Ephesus, what did former magicians burn in front of everyone?
explanation: They were worth fifty thousand drachmas. “brought their books and burned them in front of everyone.” (Acts 19:19, BSB)

content: Which king asked Paul, “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”
explanation: Paul was on trial before him. “Then Agrippa said to Paul” (Acts 26:28, BSB)

content: In Amos, what should roll on like a river?
explanation: And righteousness like a stream. “But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.” (Amos 5:24, BSB)

content: In Amos's vision, what was in the Lord's hand by the wall?
explanation: It measured Israel's straightness. ““A plumb line,” I replied.” (Amos 7:8, BSB)

content: In Amos, what was Amos doing when the LORD called him?
explanation: He was a herdsman. “But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’” (Amos 7:15, BSB)

content: In Amos, what kind of famine will God send?
explanation: People will search for God's word. “but a famine of hearing the words of the LORD.” (Amos 8:11, BSB)

content: In Amos, from which town was the shepherd-prophet Amos?
explanation: He was among its sheepherders. “These are the words of Amos, who was among the sheepherders of Tekoa” (Amos 1:1, BSB)

content: In Amos, what did Amos say he was before God called him?
explanation: He was not a professional prophet. “rather, I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.” (Amos 7:14, BSB)

content: In Amos, righteousness should flow like what?
explanation: Justice rolls on like a river. “and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.” (Amos 5:24, BSB)

content: In Amos, Amos's words came two years before what event?
explanation: In the days of King Uzziah. “what he saw concerning Israel two years before the earthquake” (Amos 1:1, BSB)

content: In Amos, which kind of trees did Amos tend?
explanation: He was a farmer, not a prophet. “I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.” (Amos 7:14, BSB)

content: In Colossians, Paul says to set your minds on things where?
explanation: Christ is seated at God's right hand. “Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.” (Colossians 3:2, BSB)

content: In Colossians, Paul says forgive as who forgave you?
explanation: Bear with one another. “Forgive as the Lord forgave you.” (Colossians 3:13, BSB)

content: In Colossians, what should you put on over all other virtues?
explanation: It binds everything in unity. “And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.” (Colossians 3:14, BSB)

content: In Colossians, what are children told to do in everything?
explanation: This pleases the Lord. “Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.” (Colossians 3:20, BSB)

content: In Colossians, for whom should you work at whatever you do?
explanation: Work with your whole being. “Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men” (Colossians 3:23, BSB)

content: In Colossians, what should rule in your hearts?
explanation: And be thankful. “Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts” (Colossians 3:15, BSB)

content: In Colossians, believers rooted in Christ should overflow with what?
explanation: They are built up in Him. “and overflowing with thankfulness.” (Colossians 2:7, BSB)

content: In Colossians, all things were created through whom?
explanation: And for Him. “All things were created through Him and for Him.” (Colossians 1:16, BSB)

content: In Colossians, our speech should be gracious and seasoned with what?
explanation: So you can answer everyone. “Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt” (Colossians 4:6, BSB)

content: In Colossians, what was Luke's job?
explanation: Paul calls him beloved. “Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas send you greetings.” (Colossians 4:14, BSB)

content: In Colossians, the Son is the image of whom?
explanation: He is firstborn over creation. “The Son is the image of the invisible God” (Colossians 1:15, BSB)

content: In Colossians, what holds together in Christ?
explanation: He is before all things. “He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.” (Colossians 1:17, BSB)

content: In Colossians, since you received Christ Jesus as Lord, what should you do?
explanation: Stay rooted in Him. “Therefore, just as you have received Christ Jesus as Lord, continue to walk in Him” (Colossians 2:6, BSB)

content: In Colossians, God's chosen people should clothe themselves with what?
explanation: Also humility, gentleness, and patience. “clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.” (Colossians 3:12, BSB)

content: In Colossians, what should richly dwell within you?
explanation: Teach and sing with gratitude. “Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you” (Colossians 3:16, BSB)

content: In Colossians, in whose name should you do everything in word or deed?
explanation: Give thanks to God through Him. “do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus” (Colossians 3:17, BSB)

content: In Colossians, where does Paul say Christ is seated?
explanation: So strive for things above. “where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.” (Colossians 3:1, BSB)

content: To the saints in which city did Paul write Colossians?
explanation: Timothy was with him. “To the saints and faithful brothers in Christ at Colossae” (Colossians 1:2, BSB)

content: In Colossians, which church was also to read Paul's letter?
explanation: Letters were shared between churches. “make sure that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans” (Colossians 4:16, BSB)

content: In Colossians, who was always wrestling in prayer for the believers?
explanation: He was one of them. “He is always wrestling in prayer for you” (Colossians 4:12, BSB)

content: In Colossians, who was sent with Tychicus as a faithful brother?
explanation: He was one of the Colossians. “With him I am sending Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you.” (Colossians 4:9, BSB)

content: In Colossians, who would tell the believers all the news about Paul?
explanation: He was a faithful minister. “Tychicus will tell you all the news about me.” (Colossians 4:7, BSB)

content: What did King Nebuchadnezzar set up on the plain of Dura for everyone to worship?
explanation: Everyone was ordered to bow down to it. “King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue” (Daniel 3:1, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: What would happen to anyone who did not bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
options: Be thrown into a fiery furnace
explanation: The king wanted everyone to obey. “will immediately be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.” (Daniel 3:6, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: Which three young Jews refused to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
explanation: They would worship only the true God. “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—who have ignored you, O king” (Daniel 3:12, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: Facing the furnace, what did Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego say their God was able to do?
explanation: They trusted God's power. “then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace” (Daniel 3:17, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego said that even if God did not save them, they would still never do what?
explanation: They would stay faithful no matter what. “we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.” (Daniel 3:18, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: How much hotter did Nebuchadnezzar order the furnace for the three friends?
explanation: The king was filled with rage. “He gave orders to heat the furnace seven times hotter than usual” (Daniel 3:19, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: Looking into the fiery furnace, how many men did King Nebuchadnezzar see walking in the fire?
explanation: Someone was with them in the fire. “I see four men, unbound and unharmed, walking around in the fire” (Daniel 3:25, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: When the three friends came out of the fiery furnace, what was there no smell of on them?
explanation: Not even a hair was singed. “and there was no smell of fire on them.” (Daniel 3:27, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: What law did King Darius's officials trick him into making to trap Daniel?
options: Pray to no one but the king
explanation: They knew Daniel prayed to God. “that for thirty days anyone who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.” (Daniel 6:7, BSB)

content: How long was King Darius's law against praying to anyone but him supposed to last?
explanation: Anyone who broke it would face the lions. “for thirty days” (Daniel 6:7, BSB)

content: After the law against prayer was signed, how many times a day did Daniel keep praying?
explanation: He prayed just as he had done before. “and three times a day he got down on his knees, prayed” (Daniel 6:10, BSB)

content: Which way did Daniel's windows face when he prayed in Babylon?
explanation: Jerusalem was the city of God's temple. “where the windows of his upper room opened toward Jerusalem” (Daniel 6:10, BSB)

content: Where was Daniel thrown for praying to God?
explanation: King Darius could not change the law. “and threw him into the den of lions.” (Daniel 6:16, BSB)

content: When did King Darius hurry to the lions' den to check on Daniel?
options: At the first light of dawn
explanation: The king could not wait to know. “At the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the den of lions.” (Daniel 6:19, BSB)

content: How did God protect Daniel in the lions' den?
options: His angel shut the lions' mouths
explanation: Daniel was innocent before God. “My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions.” (Daniel 6:22, BSB)

content: Why were no wounds found on Daniel when he came out of the lions' den?
options: He had trusted in his God
explanation: Faith in God kept him safe. “because he had trusted in his God.” (Daniel 6:23, BSB)

content: As a young captive in Babylon, what did Daniel refuse to eat and drink?
explanation: He did not want to defile himself. “he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine.” (Daniel 1:8, BSB)

content: In Babylon, what did Daniel and his friends ask to eat for ten days?
explanation: They asked to be tested. “Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.” (Daniel 1:12, BSB)

content: After ten days of vegetables and water, how did Daniel and his friends look?
explanation: God blessed their choice. “they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men” (Daniel 1:15, BSB)

content: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel given?
explanation: The chief official renamed all four young men. “To Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar” (Daniel 1:7, BSB)

content: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel's friend Hananiah given?
explanation: He later faced the fiery furnace. “to Hananiah, Shadrach” (Daniel 1:7, BSB)

content: Besides knowledge, what special gift did God give Daniel in Babylon?
explanation: This gift later helped him explain the king's dreams. “And Daniel had insight into all kinds of visions and dreams.” (Daniel 1:17, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream that Daniel explained, what was the statue's head made of?
explanation: Each metal stood for a kingdom. “The head of the statue was pure gold” (Daniel 2:32, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream that Daniel explained, what were the statue's feet made of?
explanation: The feet were the weak point. “and its feet were part iron and part clay.” (Daniel 2:33, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what did the stone that struck the statue become?
explanation: It filled the whole earth, like God's kingdom. “But the stone that had struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.” (Daniel 2:35, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, how was the stone that crushed the statue cut out?
explanation: It came from God, not people. “a stone was cut out, but not by human hands.” (Daniel 2:34, BSB)

content: What signal told everyone in Babylon to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
explanation: Horns, flutes, harps, and more were played. “As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music” (Daniel 3:5, BSB)

content: King Nebuchadnezzar said the fourth man in the fiery furnace looked like what?
explanation: God was with His servants in the fire. “and the fourth looks like a son of the gods!” (Daniel 3:25, BSB)

content: At King Belshazzar's feast, what appeared and wrote on the palace wall?
options: The fingers of a human hand
explanation: The king watched the hand writing. “At that moment the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall” (Daniel 5:5, BSB)

content: What words were written on the wall at King Belshazzar's feast?
explanation: Daniel explained what they meant. “MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.” (Daniel 5:25, BSB)

content: When jealous officials looked for a charge against Daniel, what did they find?
explanation: Daniel was trustworthy. “but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy” (Daniel 6:4, BSB)

content: Why did King Darius plan to set Daniel over the whole kingdom?
explanation: Daniel stood out among all the officials. “Soon, by his extraordinary spirit, Daniel distinguished himself among the administrators and satraps.” (Daniel 6:3, BSB)

content: As Daniel was thrown to the lions, what did King Darius say to him?
explanation: The king hoped Daniel's God would save him. “May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you!” (Daniel 6:16, BSB)

content: During the reigns of which two kings did Daniel prosper?
explanation: God blessed Daniel's faithfulness. “So Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.” (Daniel 6:28, BSB)

content: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel's friend Mishael given?
explanation: The chief official renamed him. “to Mishael, Meshach” (Daniel 1:7, BSB)

content: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel's friend Azariah given?
explanation: He was one of the three in the furnace. “and to Azariah, Abednego.” (Daniel 1:7, BSB)

content: On which plain did Nebuchadnezzar set up his golden statue?
explanation: It was in the province of Babylon. “and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.” (Daniel 3:1, BSB)

content: How high was Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
explanation: It was six cubits wide. “a golden statue sixty cubits high and six cubits wide” (Daniel 3:1, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what were the statue's chest and arms made of?
explanation: The head was gold, the chest silver. “its chest and arms were silver” (Daniel 2:32, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what were the statue's belly and thighs made of?
explanation: The legs were iron. “its belly and thighs were bronze” (Daniel 2:32, BSB)

content: At Belshazzar's feast, near what in the palace did the hand write on the wall?
explanation: The king could see it clearly. “near the lampstand in the royal palace.” (Daniel 5:5, BSB)

content: For how many days did Daniel ask to be tested on vegetables and water?
explanation: At the end they looked healthier than the rest. “Please test your servants for ten days.” (Daniel 1:12, BSB)

content: Who spoke the words of Deuteronomy to all Israel in the wilderness?
explanation: He spoke east of the Jordan. “These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel in the wilderness east of the Jordan” (Deuteronomy 1:1, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, Moses says, “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is…”
explanation: There is only one true God. “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.” (Deuteronomy 6:4, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, Moses says to love the LORD with all your heart, soul, and what?
explanation: Jesus called this the greatest commandment. “And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.” (Deuteronomy 6:5, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, to whom did Moses tell parents to teach God's words diligently?
explanation: Talk about them at home and on the road. “And you shall teach them diligently to your children” (Deuteronomy 6:7, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, where did Moses tell Israel to write God's words?
explanation: They should see them every day. “Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.” (Deuteronomy 6:9, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, Moses says man does not live on bread alone, but on what?
explanation: Jesus quoted this when tempted. “man does not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.” (Deuteronomy 8:3, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, what food did Moses remind Israel God gave them when hungry?
explanation: Their fathers had never known it. “and in your hunger He gave you manna to eat” (Deuteronomy 8:3, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, what did Moses say did not wear out during forty years in the wilderness?
explanation: God cared for every need. “Your clothing did not wear out and your feet did not swell during these forty years.” (Deuteronomy 8:4, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, Moses tells Israel to be strong and courageous, for God will never do what?
explanation: God goes with His people. “He will never leave you nor forsake you.” (Deuteronomy 31:6, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, whom did Moses call before Israel and tell, “Be strong and courageous”?
explanation: Joshua would lead them into the land. “Then Moses called for Joshua and said to him in the presence of all Israel, “Be strong and courageous” (Deuteronomy 31:7, BSB)

content: At the end of Deuteronomy, which mountain did Moses climb to see the promised land?
explanation: God showed him the whole land. “Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo” (Deuteronomy 34:1, BSB)

content: At the end of Deuteronomy, God let Moses see the promised land, but what could he not do?
explanation: Moses died in Moab. “I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross into it.” (Deuteronomy 34:4, BSB)

content: How old was Moses when he died, as told at the end of Deuteronomy?
explanation: His eyes were still not weak. “Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died” (Deuteronomy 34:7, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy's Ten Commandments, whom are we told to honor?
explanation: So that your days may be long. “Honor your father and your mother” (Deuteronomy 5:16, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, after reminding Israel He brought them out of Egypt, what does God command first?
explanation: God alone deserves worship. “You shall have no other gods before Me.” (Deuteronomy 5:7, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, which day did God tell Israel to keep holy?
explanation: It was a day of rest. “Observe the Sabbath day by keeping it holy” (Deuteronomy 5:12, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, where did Moses say Israel had tested the LORD?
explanation: Jesus quoted this verse when tempted. “Do not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah.” (Deuteronomy 6:16, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, what did Moses say Israel had lacked during forty years in the wilderness?
explanation: God was with them. “The LORD your God has been with you these forty years, and you have lacked nothing.” (Deuteronomy 2:7, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, why did God say He did not choose Israel?
explanation: They were the fewest of peoples. “The LORD did not set His affection on you and choose you because you were more numerous than the other peoples” (Deuteronomy 7:7, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, Moses promises Israel will find God if they seek Him with all their what?
explanation: God is found by those who seek Him. “you will find Him if you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul.” (Deuteronomy 4:29, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, how long did Moses say he stayed on the mountain to receive the stone tablets?
explanation: He ate no bread and drank no water. “I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.” (Deuteronomy 9:9, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, what happened to the first stone tablets of the law?
explanation: God wrote the words again. “the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke” (Deuteronomy 10:2, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, what wood did Moses use to make the ark for the new tablets?
explanation: The tablets were placed inside. “So I made an ark of acacia wood” (Deuteronomy 10:3, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, how were Israelites told to treat the poor and needy?
explanation: There would always be poor in the land. “that is why I am commanding you to open wide your hand to your brother and to the poor and needy in your land.” (Deuteronomy 15:11, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy's law, who should get a sheaf of grain forgotten in the field?
explanation: God blesses the generous. “It is to be left for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow” (Deuteronomy 24:19, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, after setting life and death before Israel, what did Moses urge them to choose?
explanation: So they and their children may live. “Therefore choose life, so that you and your descendants may live” (Deuteronomy 30:19, BSB)

content: In the Song of Moses in Deuteronomy, what does Moses call God, whose work is perfect?
explanation: God is solid and faithful. “He is the Rock, His work is perfect; all His ways are just.” (Deuteronomy 32:4, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, Moses says the eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are what?
explanation: God holds His people up. “The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms.” (Deuteronomy 33:27, BSB)

content: When Moses died, why was Joshua filled with the spirit of wisdom?
options: Moses had laid hands on him
explanation: Israel then obeyed him. “Now Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him.” (Deuteronomy 34:9, BSB)

content: After Moses died, how long did the Israelites grieve for him?
explanation: They mourned in the plains of Moab. “The Israelites grieved for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days” (Deuteronomy 34:8, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, how many days' journey is it from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea?
explanation: Israel took forty years instead. “It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by way of Mount Seir.” (Deuteronomy 1:2, BSB)

content: In which year of the wilderness journey did Moses proclaim the words of Deuteronomy?
explanation: It was the eleventh month. “In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month” (Deuteronomy 1:3, BSB)

content: From Mount Nebo, Moses stood on the top of which peak facing Jericho?
explanation: God showed him the whole land. “to the top of Pisgah, which faces Jericho.” (Deuteronomy 34:1, BSB)

content: According to Deuteronomy, what does no one know about Moses?
explanation: God Himself buried him in Moab. “and no one to this day knows the location of his grave.” (Deuteronomy 34:6, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, how did the LORD know Moses, unlike any later prophet?
explanation: No prophet rose like Moses. “whom the LORD knew face to face” (Deuteronomy 34:10, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, how many times a year were Israel's men to appear before the LORD?
explanation: At three great feasts. “Three times a year all your men are to appear before the LORD your God” (Deuteronomy 16:16, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy's law, what must you build around the roof of a new house?
explanation: So no one falls from it. “you are to construct a railing around your roof” (Deuteronomy 22:8, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, Moses says God will raise up for Israel a prophet like whom?
explanation: Israel must listen to him. “The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.” (Deuteronomy 18:15, BSB)

content: In the Song of Moses, God caring for Israel is compared to what bird stirring its nest?
explanation: God carried them on His wings. “As an eagle stirs up its nest and hovers over its young” (Deuteronomy 32:11, BSB)

content: In Deuteronomy, where did Moses tell the Levites to place the Book of the Law?
explanation: It would stand as a witness. “Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God” (Deuteronomy 31:26, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, the Teacher says to everything there is a what?
explanation: A time for every purpose under heaven. “To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven” (Ecclesiastes 3:1, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to plant and a time to do what?
explanation: Life has its seasons. “a time to plant and a time to uproot” (Ecclesiastes 3:2, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to weep and a time to do what?
explanation: Both sorrow and joy have their time. “a time to weep and a time to laugh” (Ecclesiastes 3:4, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to mourn and a time to do what?
explanation: Sadness does not last forever. “a time to mourn and a time to dance” (Ecclesiastes 3:4, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to be silent and a time to do what?
explanation: Wisdom knows when to talk. “a time to be silent and a time to speak” (Ecclesiastes 3:7, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time for war and a time for what?
explanation: Everything has its time. “a time for war and a time for peace.” (Ecclesiastes 3:8, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, what has God made beautiful in its time?
explanation: He set eternity in our hearts. “He has made everything beautiful in its time.” (Ecclesiastes 3:11, BSB)

content: Who is the Teacher whose words fill Ecclesiastes?
explanation: He was king in Jerusalem. “These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem” (Ecclesiastes 1:1, BSB)

content: What does the Teacher in Ecclesiastes say everything is?
explanation: Life without God has no lasting meaning. “Everything is futile!” (Ecclesiastes 1:2, BSB)

content: According to the Teacher in Ecclesiastes, there is nothing new where?
explanation: What has been will be again. “there is nothing new under the sun.” (Ecclesiastes 1:9, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, why are two better than one?
explanation: If one falls, the other lifts him up. “For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up” (Ecclesiastes 4:10, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, what kind of cord is not quickly broken?
explanation: Together we are stronger. “Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.” (Ecclesiastes 4:12, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, since God is in heaven and you are on earth, how should your words be?
explanation: Do not be quick to speak. “So let your words be few.” (Ecclesiastes 5:2, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, what is never satisfied by money?
explanation: Loving wealth brings no rest. “He who loves money is never satisfied by money” (Ecclesiastes 5:10, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, when should you remember your Creator?
options: In the days of your youth
explanation: Before hard days come. “Remember your Creator in the days of your youth” (Ecclesiastes 12:1, BSB)

content: How does the Teacher sum up everything at the end of Ecclesiastes?
explanation: It is the whole duty of man. “Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man.” (Ecclesiastes 12:13, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, how should you do whatever your hands find to do?
explanation: Life's time is limited. “Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might” (Ecclesiastes 9:10, BSB)

content: Over what was the Teacher of Ecclesiastes king?
explanation: He was David's son. “I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.” (Ecclesiastes 1:12, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, what has God set in the hearts of men?
explanation: Yet we cannot fathom all God's work. “He has also set eternity in the hearts of men” (Ecclesiastes 3:11, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, a patient spirit is better than what?
explanation: The end is better than the beginning. “and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.” (Ecclesiastes 7:8, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, what are we told to cast upon the waters?
explanation: After many days you will find it again. “Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.” (Ecclesiastes 11:1, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to cast away stones and a time to do what?
explanation: Everything has its time. “a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together” (Ecclesiastes 3:5, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says we have been saved by what, through faith?
explanation: Salvation is God's free gift. “For it is by grace you have been saved through faith” (Ephesians 2:8, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says being saved by grace is not from ourselves, but is what?
explanation: We cannot earn it. “and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God” (Ephesians 2:8, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says we are not saved by works, so that no one can do what?
explanation: All the credit goes to God. “not by works, so that no one can boast.” (Ephesians 2:9, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says God, because of His great love, is rich in what?
explanation: He made us alive with Christ. “But because of His great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy” (Ephesians 2:4, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says God made us alive with Christ even when we were what?
explanation: God gives life to the lost. “made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses.” (Ephesians 2:5, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says we are God's workmanship, created in Christ to do what?
explanation: Good works follow being saved. “For we are God’s workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do good works” (Ephesians 2:10, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says believers are no longer strangers, but members of whose household?
explanation: Grace brings us into God's family. “but fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household” (Ephesians 2:19, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, what does Paul tell believers to put on to stand against the devil?
explanation: God gives us what we need to stand. “Put on the full armor of God, so that you can make your stand against the devil’s schemes.” (Ephesians 6:11, BSB)

content: In the armor of God, what is the belt buckled around the waist?
explanation: Truth holds everything together. “with the belt of truth buckled around your waist” (Ephesians 6:14, BSB)

content: In the armor of God, what is the breastplate?
explanation: It guards the heart. “with the breastplate of righteousness arrayed” (Ephesians 6:14, BSB)

content: In the armor of God, which shield puts out the evil one's flaming arrows?
explanation: Faith trusts God's promises. “take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one.” (Ephesians 6:16, BSB)

content: In the armor of God, what is the helmet?
explanation: It protects the mind. “And take the helmet of salvation” (Ephesians 6:17, BSB)

content: In the armor of God, what is the sword of the Spirit?
explanation: God's word is our weapon. “and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.” (Ephesians 6:17, BSB)

content: In the armor of God, what are our feet fitted with?
explanation: We are ready to share good news. “and with your feet fitted with the readiness of the gospel of peace.” (Ephesians 6:15, BSB)

content: When Paul describes the armor of God, he says our struggle is not against what?
explanation: The real battle is spiritual. “For our struggle is not against flesh and blood” (Ephesians 6:12, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says to be strong in what?
explanation: Our strength comes from God. “Finally, be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power.” (Ephesians 6:10, BSB)

content: After describing God's armor, how often does Paul tell believers to pray in the Spirit?
explanation: Prayer keeps us alert. “Pray in the Spirit at all times, with every kind of prayer and petition.” (Ephesians 6:18, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says to forgive each other just as who forgave you?
explanation: Be kind and tenderhearted. “forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you.” (Ephesians 4:32, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says do not let what set upon your anger?
explanation: Deal with anger quickly. “Do not let the sun set upon your anger” (Ephesians 4:26, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, what does Paul tell children to do?
explanation: This is right in the Lord. “Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.” (Ephesians 6:1, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul calls “Honor your father and mother” the first commandment with what?
explanation: It promises a good life. “(which is the first commandment with a promise)” (Ephesians 6:2, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul tells believers to be imitators of whom?
explanation: As beloved children. “Be imitators of God, therefore, as beloved children” (Ephesians 5:1, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, who is called the cornerstone of God's household?
explanation: The church is built on Him. “with Christ Jesus Himself as the cornerstone.” (Ephesians 2:20, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul lists one Lord, one faith, and one what?
explanation: Believers are united. “one Lord, one faith, one baptism” (Ephesians 4:5, BSB)

content: To the saints in which city did Paul write the letter of Ephesians?
explanation: He was an apostle by God's will. “To the saints in Ephesus, the faithful in Christ Jesus” (Ephesians 1:1, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, whom did Paul send to tell the believers all his news?
explanation: He was a faithful servant. “Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will tell you everything” (Ephesians 6:21, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says God is able to do much more than all we what?
explanation: His power works within us. “to do so much more than all we ask or imagine” (Ephesians 3:20, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul says speak to one another with psalms, hymns, and what?
explanation: Make music to the Lord in your hearts. “Speak to one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.” (Ephesians 5:19, BSB)

content: In Ephesians, Paul urges believers to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of what?
explanation: Unity takes effort and love. “to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.” (Ephesians 4:3, BSB)

content: Before going to the king uninvited, what did Queen Esther ask the Jews in Susa to do?
explanation: She needed God's help. “Go and assemble all the Jews who can be found in Susa, and fast for me.” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: How many days did Queen Esther ask the Jews to fast before she went to the king?
explanation: Esther and her maidens fasted too. “Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: Knowing it was against the law to see the king uninvited, what did Esther say?
options: The king will never see me
explanation: Esther was willing to risk her life for her people. “And if I perish, I perish!” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: Mordecai told Esther that perhaps she had become queen for what?
explanation: God had placed her where she could help. “And who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?” (Esther 4:14, BSB)

content: When Queen Esther came to the king uninvited, what did he hold out to her?
explanation: It meant she was welcome and would live. “The king extended the gold scepter in his hand toward Esther” (Esther 5:2, BSB)

content: When Esther came before the king, how much did he offer to give her?
explanation: She had found favor in his sight. “Even up to half the kingdom, it will be given to you.” (Esther 5:3, BSB)

content: On the night King Xerxes could not sleep, what did he have read to him?
explanation: There he learned that Mordecai had saved his life. “so he ordered the Book of Records, the Chronicles, to be brought in and read to him.” (Esther 6:1, BSB)

content: Whom did King Xerxes order Haman to honor with the royal robe and horse?
explanation: Haman had to honor the man he hated. “Take the robe and the horse to Mordecai the Jew” (Esther 6:10, BSB)

content: At her banquet, whom did Queen Esther name as the enemy of her people?
explanation: Haman stood in terror before the king and queen. “The adversary and enemy is this wicked man—Haman!” (Esther 7:6, BSB)

content: In the story of Queen Esther, what happened to Haman in the end?
options: He was hanged on his own gallows
explanation: The gallows he built for Mordecai was used for him. “So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.” (Esther 7:10, BSB)

content: In the book of Esther, which king reigned over 127 provinces?
explanation: He ruled a huge empire. “This is what happened in the days of Xerxes, who reigned over 127 provinces” (Esther 1:1, BSB)

content: Which queen refused to come when King Xerxes called her?
explanation: The king was furious with her. “Queen Vashti, however, refused to come at the king’s command” (Esther 1:12, BSB)

content: Who raised Esther after her parents died?
explanation: Mordecai took her in as his own daughter. “And Mordecai had brought up Hadassah (that is, Esther), the daughter of his uncle” (Esther 2:7, BSB)

content: What was Queen Esther's Hebrew name?
explanation: Esther was her Persian name. “Mordecai had brought up Hadassah (that is, Esther)” (Esther 2:7, BSB)

content: Why did King Xerxes make Esther his queen?
options: He loved her more than all others
She won a contest of strength
explanation: She found favor in his sight. “And the king loved Esther more than all the other women” (Esther 2:17, BSB)

content: When Mordecai learned of a plot to kill King Xerxes, whom did he tell?
explanation: Esther told the king on Mordecai's behalf. “he reported it to Queen Esther” (Esther 2:22, BSB)

content: In the book of Esther, why was Haman angry with Mordecai?
options: Mordecai would not bow to him
explanation: Everyone else at the king's gate bowed down. “But Mordecai would not bow down or pay homage.” (Esther 3:2, BSB)

content: Because of his anger at Mordecai, whom did Haman plan to destroy?
options: All the Jews in the kingdom
explanation: He hated Mordecai's whole people. “he sought to destroy all of Mordecai’s people, the Jews, throughout the kingdom of Xerxes.” (Esther 3:6, BSB)

content: What did Haman cast to choose the day to destroy the Jews?
explanation: The feast of Purim is named after it. “the Pur (that is, the lot) was cast before Haman” (Esther 3:7, BSB)

content: When Mordecai learned of Haman's plot against the Jews, what did he put on?
explanation: He mourned loudly in the city. “he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes” (Esther 4:1, BSB)

content: When King Xerxes learned Mordecai had saved his life, what reward had Mordecai been given?
explanation: So the king decided to honor him. ““Nothing has been done for him,” replied the king’s attendants.” (Esther 6:3, BSB)

content: After Haman's death, who received King Xerxes' signet ring?
explanation: Esther also put Mordecai over Haman's estate. “The king removed the signet ring he had recovered from Haman and presented it to Mordecai.” (Esther 8:2, BSB)

content: Which feast remembers how the Jews were saved in Queen Esther's day?
explanation: The name comes from the word Pur. “Therefore these days are called Purim, from the word Pur.” (Esther 9:26, BSB)

content: On the third day of fasting, where did Queen Esther stand in her royal robes?
options: The inner court of the palace
explanation: The king could see her from his throne. “Esther put on her royal attire and stood in the inner court of the palace” (Esther 5:1, BSB)

content: The kingdom of Xerxes in the book of Esther stretched from India to where?
explanation: It had 127 provinces. “who reigned over 127 provinces from India to Cush.” (Esther 1:1, BSB)

content: Which two eunuchs plotted to kill King Xerxes?
explanation: Mordecai uncovered their plot. “Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs who guarded the entrance” (Esther 2:21, BSB)

content: In the book of Esther, Haman was the son of Hammedatha and was called what?
explanation: King Xerxes raised him above all the princes. “Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite” (Esther 3:1, BSB)

content: In Haman's plot, in which month did the lot fall for destroying the Jews?
explanation: The lot was cast in the month of Nisan. “And the lot fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar.” (Esther 3:7, BSB)

content: In which year of King Xerxes' reign was the Pur cast against the Jews?
explanation: It was cast in the first month. “In the twelfth year of King Xerxes” (Esther 3:7, BSB)

content: In which city did Queen Esther ask the Jews to gather and fast?
explanation: Susa was where the king's palace stood. “Go and assemble all the Jews who can be found in Susa” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: Esther told the king she would have stayed silent if her people had only been sold as what?
explanation: But they had been sold for destruction. “If we had merely been sold as menservants and maidservants, I would have remained silent” (Esther 7:4, BSB)

content: To save her baby boy from Pharaoh, what did Moses' mother put him in?
explanation: She coated it with tar and pitch so it would float. “she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch.” (Exodus 2:3, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: Where did Moses' mother place the basket with her baby inside?
options: Among the reeds by the Nile
explanation: She hid him along the riverbank. “set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.” (Exodus 2:3, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: Who stood at a distance to watch what would happen to baby Moses in the basket?
explanation: She kept watch over her little brother. “And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.” (Exodus 2:4, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: Who found baby Moses in his basket by the Nile?
explanation: She came down to the river to bathe. “Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile” (Exodus 2:5, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: Why did Pharaoh's daughter name the baby from the basket Moses?
options: He was born on the Nile
She drew him out of the water
explanation: Moses became her son. “She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.”” (Exodus 2:10, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: While Moses was tending sheep at Horeb, what amazing sight did he see?
options: A burning bush not burning up
explanation: The angel of the LORD appeared in the fire. “Moses saw the bush ablaze with fire, but it was not consumed.” (Exodus 3:2, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: At the burning bush, what did God tell Moses to take off?
explanation: Moses was standing on holy ground. “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.” (Exodus 3:5, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: At the burning bush, to whom did God send Moses?
explanation: Moses was to bring God's people out of Egypt. “I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.” (Exodus 3:10, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: When Moses asked God's name at the burning bush, what did God answer?
explanation: Moses was to tell Israel that I AM had sent him. “God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” (Exodus 3:14, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: In the first plague on Egypt, what did the water of the Nile turn into?
explanation: Aaron struck the river with his staff. “and all the water was turned to blood.” (Exodus 7:20, BSB)

content: During the plagues on Egypt, God warned Pharaoh He would fill the country with which animal?
explanation: Pharaoh still refused to let the people go. “I will plague your whole country with frogs.” (Exodus 8:2, BSB)

content: During the plagues on Egypt, what fell from the sky with thunder and lightning?
explanation: Moses stretched his staff toward heaven. “So the LORD rained down hail upon the land of Egypt.” (Exodus 9:23, BSB)

content: During the plagues on Egypt, which insects did God bring after the hail?
explanation: They covered the land and ate what was left. “I will bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.” (Exodus 10:4, BSB)

content: During the plagues on Egypt, how long did total darkness cover the land?
explanation: No one in Egypt could see anyone else. “and total darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.” (Exodus 10:22, BSB)

content: Before the plagues began, what message from the LORD did Moses and Aaron bring Pharaoh?
explanation: God wanted His people to worship Him in the wilderness. “Let My people go” (Exodus 5:1, BSB)

content: When Moses first asked Pharaoh to free Israel, how did Pharaoh answer?
options: I will not let Israel go
explanation: Pharaoh said he did not know the LORD. “and I will not let Israel go.” (Exodus 5:2, BSB)

content: In front of Pharaoh, what did Aaron's staff do to the magicians' staffs?
explanation: God showed He was greater than Egypt's magic. “But Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs.” (Exodus 7:12, BSB)

content: For the first Passover, what animal was each family to choose?
explanation: One lamb was chosen for each household. “each man must select a lamb for his family, one per household.” (Exodus 12:3, BSB)

content: For the first Passover, what kind of lamb was needed?
explanation: The lamb had to be perfect. “Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male” (Exodus 12:5, BSB)

content: At the first Passover, where did the Israelites put the lamb's blood?
explanation: The blood marked the houses of God's people. “They are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes” (Exodus 12:7, BSB)

content: At the first Passover, what did the Israelites eat with the roasted lamb?
explanation: They ate the meal that same night. “along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.” (Exodus 12:8, BSB)

content: At the first Passover, what did God do when He saw the blood on a house?
explanation: That is why the feast is called the Passover. “when I see the blood, I will pass over you.” (Exodus 12:13, BSB)

content: At midnight on the first Passover, what happened in Egypt?
explanation: It was the last of the ten plagues. “Now at midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn male in the land of Egypt” (Exodus 12:29, BSB)

content: After the tenth plague, what did Pharaoh tell Moses and the Israelites?
explanation: Pharaoh finally let God's people go. “Get up, leave my people, both you and the Israelites!” (Exodus 12:31, BSB)

content: As the Israelites left Egypt, what went before them to guide them by day?
explanation: By night a pillar of fire gave them light. “And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day” (Exodus 13:21, BSB)

content: When Pharaoh's army chased Israel to the edge of the sea, how did the Israelites feel?
explanation: They cried out to the LORD. “and they were terrified and cried out to the LORD.” (Exodus 14:10, BSB)

content: At the sea, Moses said the LORD would fight for Israel. What did the people need to do?
explanation: God Himself would save them. “The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still.” (Exodus 14:14, BSB)

content: At the sea, what did God tell Moses to lift up and stretch out over the water?
explanation: God would divide the sea. “lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it” (Exodus 14:16, BSB)

content: When Israel was trapped by the sea, what did the LORD use to drive back the water all night?
explanation: The wind turned the sea into dry land. “the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind that turned it into dry land.” (Exodus 14:21, BSB)

content: When God divided the sea, how did the Israelites cross?
explanation: Walls of water stood on both sides. “and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground” (Exodus 14:22, BSB)

content: What happened to Pharaoh's army when it followed Israel into the sea?
explanation: Not one of them survived. “The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen” (Exodus 14:28, BSB)

content: After Israel crossed the sea, who led the women with tambourines and dancing?
explanation: Miriam was Aaron's sister and a prophetess. “Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a tambourine in her hand” (Exodus 15:20, BSB)

content: In the wilderness after leaving Egypt, what did the hungry Israelites complain about?
explanation: They remembered the food of Egypt. “but you have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!” (Exodus 16:3, BSB)

content: When Israel was hungry in the wilderness, what did God promise to rain down from heaven?
explanation: The people were to gather enough each day. “Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you.” (Exodus 16:4, BSB)

content: That evening in the wilderness, what birds came and covered Israel's camp?
explanation: God gave them meat in the evening. “That evening quail came and covered the camp” (Exodus 16:13, BSB)

content: When the Israelites first saw thin flakes on the desert floor, what did they ask?
explanation: Moses told them it was bread from the LORD. “they asked one another, “What is it?”” (Exodus 16:15, BSB)

content: What did the Israelites call the bread God gave them in the wilderness?
explanation: They ate it every day in the wilderness. “Now the house of Israel called the bread manna.” (Exodus 16:31, BSB)

content: What did the manna in the wilderness taste like?
explanation: God's bread was sweet. “and tasted like wafers made with honey.” (Exodus 16:31, BSB)

content: For how many years did the Israelites eat manna?
