content: In Hebrews, how should we approach the throne of grace?
explanation: We will find grace and mercy. “Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence” (Hebrews 4:16, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, how is the word of God described?
explanation: It reaches the heart. “For the word of God is living and active.” (Hebrews 4:12, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, who by faith conceived a child though beyond the proper age?
explanation: She considered God faithful. “By faith Sarah, even though she was barren and beyond the proper age, was enabled to conceive a child” (Hebrews 11:11, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, how long did Moses' parents hide him by faith?
explanation: They did not fear the king's edict. “By faith Moses’ parents hid him for three months after his birth” (Hebrews 11:23, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, what did grown-up Moses refuse to be called?
explanation: He chose God's people. “By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.” (Hebrews 11:24, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, since we are surrounded by a great cloud of witnesses, how should we run?
explanation: Throw off every hindrance. “and let us run with endurance the race set out for us.” (Hebrews 12:1, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, what should believers not neglect?
explanation: Encourage one another. “Let us not neglect meeting together” (Hebrews 10:25, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, by showing hospitality, some have entertained whom without knowing?
explanation: Welcome strangers. “for by so doing some people have entertained angels without knowing it.” (Hebrews 13:2, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, which king of Salem and priest of God blessed Abraham?
explanation: He is a picture of Christ. “This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High.” (Hebrews 7:1, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, the Son is the radiance of God's what?
explanation: He upholds all things. “The Son is the radiance of God’s glory” (Hebrews 1:3, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, who did not perish because she welcomed the spies in peace?
explanation: Her faith saved her. “By faith the prostitute Rahab, because she welcomed the spies in peace, did not perish” (Hebrews 11:31, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, when Abraham was tested, whom did he offer on the altar?
explanation: His one and only son. “By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac on the altar.” (Hebrews 11:17, BSB)

content: In Hebrews, by faith we understand the universe was formed by what?
explanation: Seen things came from the unseen. “By faith we understand that the universe was formed at God’s command” (Hebrews 11:3, BSB)

content: In Hosea, what does God desire rather than sacrifice?
explanation: Jesus quoted this verse. “For I desire mercy, not sacrifice” (Hosea 6:6, BSB)

content: In Hosea, out of which land did God call His son Israel?
explanation: God loved Israel as a child. “When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called My son.” (Hosea 11:1, BSB)

content: In Hosea, what does the prophet urge Israel to do?
explanation: They had stumbled by sin. “Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God” (Hosea 14:1, BSB)

content: In Hosea, God says He led Israel with ropes of what?
explanation: And cords of kindness. “I led them with cords of kindness, with ropes of love” (Hosea 11:4, BSB)

content: Whom did the prophet Hosea marry?
explanation: His marriage pictured God and Israel. “So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim” (Hosea 1:3, BSB)

content: In Hosea, God told Hosea to love his wife again as the LORD loves whom?
explanation: God's love is faithful. “Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites” (Hosea 3:1, BSB)

content: In Hosea, God desires the knowledge of God rather than what?
explanation: He wants hearts, not rituals. “and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.” (Hosea 6:6, BSB)

content: In Hosea, what did God lift from His people's necks?
explanation: He bent down to feed them. “I lifted the yoke from their necks and bent down to feed them.” (Hosea 11:4, BSB)

content: Who was the prophet Hosea's father?
explanation: Hosea prophesied in Uzziah's days. “the word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri” (Hosea 1:1, BSB)

content: In Hosea, Gomer was the daughter of whom?
explanation: She bore Hosea a son. “So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim” (Hosea 1:3, BSB)

content: In the year King Uzziah died, what did Isaiah see?
explanation: His robe filled the temple. “In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted” (Isaiah 6:1, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: In Isaiah's vision of the Lord's throne, how many wings did each seraph have?
explanation: They covered faces and feet, and flew. “Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings” (Isaiah 6:2, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: In Isaiah's vision, what did the seraphim call out about the LORD?
explanation: The earth is full of His glory. “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.” (Isaiah 6:3, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: Seeing the LORD on His throne, what did Isaiah cry?
explanation: He knew his lips were unclean. “Woe is me, for I am ruined” (Isaiah 6:5, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: In Isaiah's vision, what did a seraph bring from the altar?
explanation: He took it with tongs. “and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.” (Isaiah 6:6, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: In Isaiah's vision, where did the seraph touch him with the coal?
explanation: His sin was atoned for. “And with it he touched my mouth” (Isaiah 6:7, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: When the Lord asked, “Whom shall I send?” what did Isaiah answer?
explanation: He was willing to go. “And I said: “Here am I. Send me!”” (Isaiah 6:8, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: In Isaiah's sign, the virgin's son would be called what?
explanation: Immanuel means God with us. “and will call Him Immanuel.” (Isaiah 7:14, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: Isaiah says the Lord will give a sign: who will give birth to a son?
explanation: Matthew says this was fulfilled in Jesus. “Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son” (Isaiah 7:14, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: In Isaiah, what have the people walking in darkness seen?
explanation: Light dawned on them. “The people walking in darkness have seen a great light” (Isaiah 9:2, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: Isaiah says, “For unto us a child is born, unto us a…”
explanation: The government will be on His shoulders. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given” (Isaiah 9:6, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: In Isaiah's prophecy of the child, which is one of His names?
explanation: Also Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God. “And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” (Isaiah 9:6, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: In Isaiah's prophecy, on whose throne will the promised child reign?
explanation: His kingdom will have no end. “He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom” (Isaiah 9:7, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: In Isaiah's prophecy, of the increase of the child's government and peace there will be what?
explanation: His reign is forever. “Of the increase of His government and peace there will be no end.” (Isaiah 9:7, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: In Isaiah, the suffering Servant is called a man of what?
explanation: He was despised and rejected. “He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief.” (Isaiah 53:3, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, for what was the suffering Servant pierced?
explanation: He suffered in our place. “But He was pierced for our transgressions” (Isaiah 53:5, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, by the suffering Servant's stripes we are what?
explanation: His punishment brought us peace. “and by His stripes we are healed.” (Isaiah 53:5, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, we all like what have gone astray?
explanation: Each turned to his own way. “We all like sheep have gone astray” (Isaiah 53:6, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, the suffering Servant was led like what to the slaughter?
explanation: He did not open His mouth. “He was led like a lamb to the slaughter” (Isaiah 53:7, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, what did the suffering Servant do when oppressed?
explanation: He was silent like a sheep. “He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth.” (Isaiah 53:7, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, what did the suffering Servant carry for us?
explanation: He took on our weakness. “Surely He took on our infirmities and carried our sorrows” (Isaiah 53:4, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as what?
explanation: God offers cleansing. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow” (Isaiah 1:18, BSB)

content: In Isaiah's vision of peace, what will nations beat their swords into?
explanation: No more training for war. “They will beat their swords into plowshares” (Isaiah 2:4, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, from whose stump will a shoot spring up?
explanation: Jesse was David's father. “Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse” (Isaiah 11:1, BSB)

content: In Isaiah's vision of peace, the wolf will live with what?
explanation: A little child will lead them. “The wolf will live with the lamb” (Isaiah 11:6, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, the LORD GOD is my strength and my what?
explanation: He has become my salvation. “For the LORD GOD is my strength and my song” (Isaiah 12:2, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, whom will God keep in perfect peace?
explanation: A steadfast mind finds peace. “You will keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.” (Isaiah 26:3, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, what does the voice calling in the wilderness say?
options: Prepare the way for the LORD
explanation: John the Baptist fulfilled this. “Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness” (Isaiah 40:3, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, the grass withers, but what stands forever?
explanation: God's word never fails. “The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands forever.” (Isaiah 40:8, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, those who wait on the LORD will mount up with wings like what?
explanation: They will renew their strength. “they will mount up with wings like eagles” (Isaiah 40:31, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, why does God tell His people not to fear?
explanation: He will strengthen and help. “Do not fear, for I am with you” (Isaiah 41:10, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, God tells Israel, “I have called you by your…”
explanation: You are Mine! “I have called you by your name; you are Mine!” (Isaiah 43:1, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, God's ways are higher than ours as the heavens are higher than what?
explanation: His thoughts are not our thoughts. “For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways” (Isaiah 55:9, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, if we are the clay, what is God?
explanation: We are the work of His hand. “we are the clay, and You are the potter” (Isaiah 64:8, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, the Spirit-anointed one preaches good news to whom?
explanation: Jesus read this in Nazareth. “because the LORD has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor.” (Isaiah 61:1, BSB)

content: Who was the prophet Isaiah's father?
explanation: Isaiah saw visions about Judah. “that Isaiah son of Amoz saw” (Isaiah 1:1, BSB)

content: What was the name of the son Isaiah took to meet King Ahaz?
explanation: They met at the upper pool. “Go out with your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz” (Isaiah 7:3, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, which king does God call “My shepherd”?
explanation: He would let Jerusalem be rebuilt. “who says of Cyrus, ‘My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire,’” (Isaiah 44:28, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, where does God say He has inscribed His people?
options: On the palms of His hands
explanation: He never forgets them. “Behold, I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands” (Isaiah 49:16, BSB)

content: Which Assyrian king attacked Judah's cities in Hezekiah's reign?
explanation: It was Hezekiah's fourteenth year. “Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.” (Isaiah 36:1, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, the suffering Servant was assigned a grave with the wicked and with whom in death?
explanation: Jesus was buried in a rich man's tomb. “and with a rich man in His death” (Isaiah 53:9, BSB)

content: In Isaiah's vision, the lame will leap like what?
explanation: Streams will flow in the desert. “Then the lame will leap like a deer” (Isaiah 35:6, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, God says He will comfort His people as who comforts her son?
explanation: God's love is tender. “As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you” (Isaiah 66:13, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, which region is called Galilee of the what?
explanation: Light would dawn there. “Galilee of the nations” (Isaiah 9:1, BSB)

content: In his letter, James says faith by itself, without action, is what?
explanation: Real faith shows itself in deeds. “So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.” (James 2:17, BSB)

content: James asks about a brother or sister lacking clothes and what?
explanation: Words alone do not feed anyone. “Suppose a brother or sister is without clothes and daily food.” (James 2:15, BSB)

content: In James, what is wrong with saying, “Go in peace; stay warm and well fed”?
explanation: Faith acts to help. “but does not provide for his physical needs, what good is that?” (James 2:16, BSB)

content: In James, how does a believer show his faith?
explanation: Deeds reveal faith. “and I will show you my faith by my deeds.” (James 2:18, BSB)

content: In James, which father is said to show faith by offering his son on the altar?
explanation: His faith worked with his actions. “Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?” (James 2:21, BSB)

content: In James, what was Abraham called because his faith was real?
explanation: He believed God. “and he was called a friend of God.” (James 2:23, BSB)

content: In James, which woman showed her faith by welcoming the spies?
explanation: She sent them off safely. “was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions when she welcomed the spies” (James 2:25, BSB)

content: In James, faith without deeds is dead, just as the body without what?
explanation: Faith and deeds go together. “As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.” (James 2:26, BSB)

content: In his letter, James says to consider it pure joy when you face what?
explanation: Trials build perseverance. “Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds” (James 1:2, BSB)

content: In James, if anyone lacks wisdom, what should he do?
explanation: God gives generously. “Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God” (James 1:5, BSB)

content: In James, the one who doubts is like what?
explanation: He is tossed by the wind. “because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.” (James 1:6, BSB)

content: In James, everyone should be quick to listen and slow to do what?
explanation: Listening comes first. “Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger” (James 1:19, BSB)

content: In James, believers are told to be doers of the word, not only what?
explanation: Otherwise we deceive ourselves. “Be doers of the word, and not hearers only.” (James 1:22, BSB)

content: In James, a small spark setting a great forest ablaze is like what?
explanation: Small words can do great harm. “the tongue is a small part of the body, but it boasts of great things.” (James 3:5, BSB)

content: In James, what happens when you resist the devil?
explanation: Submit to God first. “Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” (James 4:7, BSB)

content: In James, what does God do when you draw near to Him?
explanation: God welcomes those who come. “Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you.” (James 4:8, BSB)

content: In James, life is compared to what, which appears and then vanishes?
explanation: We do not know tomorrow. “You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.” (James 4:14, BSB)

content: To whom did James address his letter?
explanation: He wrote to believers in the Dispersion. “To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion: Greetings.” (James 1:1, BSB)

content: In James, which prophet prayed and no rain fell for three and a half years?
explanation: He was a man just like us. “Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain” (James 5:17, BSB)

content: In James, who also believe that God is one, and shudder?
explanation: Belief alone is not saving faith. “Even the demons believe that—and shudder.” (James 2:19, BSB)

content: In James, what does he say no man can tame?
explanation: It is full of deadly poison. “but no man can tame the tongue.” (James 3:8, BSB)

content: In James, what kind of person's prayer has great power to prevail?
explanation: So pray for each other. “The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.” (James 5:16, BSB)

content: When the angel of the LORD came, what was Gideon doing in a winepress?
explanation: He was hiding from the Midianites. “where his son Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites.” (Judges 6:11, BSB)

content: What did the angel of the LORD call Gideon when he first appeared?
explanation: God saw what Gideon could become. “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.” (Judges 6:12, BSB)

content: What did Gideon put on the threshing floor to test God's promise?
explanation: He asked for a sign with dew. “I will place a fleece of wool on the threshing floor.” (Judges 6:37, BSB)

content: Before fighting Midian, what did God tell Gideon about his army?
explanation: Israel must not boast it saved itself. “You have too many people for Me to deliver Midian into their hands” (Judges 7:2, BSB)

content: How many men lapped the water and stayed in Gideon's army?
explanation: God saved Israel with a small band. “And the number of those who lapped the water with their hands to their mouths was three hundred men” (Judges 7:6, BSB)

content: Besides a ram's horn, what did each of Gideon's men carry?
options: A jar with a torch inside
explanation: They broke the jars at night. “gave each man a ram’s horn in one hand and a large jar in the other, containing a torch.” (Judges 7:16, BSB)

content: What did Gideon's three hundred men shout around the Midianite camp?
options: A sword for the LORD and Gideon!
explanation: Then the enemy fled. “A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!” (Judges 7:20, BSB)

content: When Gideon's men blew horns and broke jars, what did the Midianite army do?
explanation: God gave the victory. “and the entire Midianite army fled, crying out as they ran.” (Judges 7:21, BSB)

content: Before Samson was born, what did the angel say must never touch his head?
explanation: He was a Nazirite from birth. “And no razor shall come over his head” (Judges 13:5, BSB)

content: Which enemies would Samson begin to save Israel from?
explanation: The angel told his mother. “and he will begin the deliverance of Israel from the hand of the Philistines.” (Judges 13:5, BSB)

content: When a young lion roared at Samson, what did he do?
explanation: The Spirit came on him powerfully. “and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands” (Judges 14:6, BSB)

content: What was the name of the woman Samson loved in the Valley of Sorek?
explanation: The Philistines paid her to trick him. “Samson fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.” (Judges 16:4, BSB)

content: What did Samson finally tell Delilah was the secret of his strength?
explanation: He was a Nazirite to God. “My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb.” (Judges 16:17, BSB)

content: While Samson was in prison, what began to grow back?
explanation: His strength would return. “However, the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.” (Judges 16:22, BSB)

content: At the end, what did Samson push on to bring down the Philistine temple?
explanation: He prayed for strength once more. “And Samson reached out for the two central pillars supporting the temple.” (Judges 16:29, BSB)

content: In the time of the Judges, whom did the LORD raise up to save Israel?
explanation: They rescued Israel from raiders. “Then the LORD raised up judges, who saved them from the hands of those who plundered them.” (Judges 2:16, BSB)

content: Which prophetess was judging Israel when Barak led the army?
explanation: She sat under a palm tree. “Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.” (Judges 4:4, BSB)

content: How does the book of Judges describe Israel when there was no king?
explanation: It was a time of trouble. “In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.” (Judges 21:25, BSB)

content: Where did Deborah sit when Israelites came to her for judgment?
explanation: It was in the hill country of Ephraim. “And she would sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel” (Judges 4:5, BSB)

content: What did Barak say to Deborah before going to battle?
options: I'll go only if you go
explanation: Deborah agreed to go with him. “If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.” (Judges 4:8, BSB)

content: Deborah told Barak that the enemy commander Sisera would fall into whose hand?
explanation: Barak would get no honor. “because the LORD will be selling Sisera into the hand of a woman.” (Judges 4:9, BSB)

content: To which mountain did Deborah tell Barak to march with ten thousand men?
explanation: God would draw out Sisera. “Go and march to Mount Tabor” (Judges 4:6, BSB)

content: When God called Gideon, what did He tell him to go in?
explanation: God was sending him. “Go in the strength you have and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Am I not sending you?” (Judges 6:14, BSB)

content: Why did Gideon say he could not save Israel?
options: He was the youngest of a weak clan
explanation: God promised to be with him. “my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father’s house.” (Judges 6:15, BSB)

content: In Gideon's first test, how much water did he wring from the fleece?
explanation: Only the fleece was wet. “he squeezed the fleece and wrung out the dew—a bowlful of water.” (Judges 6:38, BSB)

content: In Gideon's second fleece test, what happened?
explanation: Dew covered the ground instead. “Only the fleece was dry, and dew covered the ground.” (Judges 6:40, BSB)

content: When Gideon let the fearful go home, how many remained?
explanation: Twenty-two thousand turned back. “So twenty-two thousand of them turned back, but ten thousand remained.” (Judges 7:3, BSB)

content: How did God choose Gideon's three hundred at the water?
explanation: Those who lapped were kept. “Separate those who lap the water with their tongues like a dog from those who kneel to drink.” (Judges 7:5, BSB)

content: What did Manoah's wife name the son the angel promised her?
explanation: The LORD blessed the boy. “So the woman gave birth to a son and named him Samson.” (Judges 13:24, BSB)

content: What did Samson use to strike down a thousand Philistines?
explanation: God gave him strength. “He found the fresh jawbone of a donkey, reached out his hand and took it, and struck down a thousand men.” (Judges 15:15, BSB)

content: How many braids of Samson's hair were shaved off?
explanation: Then his strength left him. “she called a man to shave off the seven braids of his head.” (Judges 16:19, BSB)

content: When Samson woke after his hair was cut, what did he not know?
explanation: His strength was gone. “But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.” (Judges 16:20, BSB)

content: In prison in Gaza, what was Samson forced to do?
explanation: He was bound with bronze shackles. “and forced to grind grain in the prison.” (Judges 16:21, BSB)

content: In the Philistine temple, what did Samson ask God?
explanation: He prayed before pushing the pillars. “Strengthen me, O God, just once more” (Judges 16:28, BSB)

content: Who was the first deliverer God raised up in Judges, a relative of Caleb?
explanation: He was the son of Caleb's younger brother. “He raised up Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz as a deliverer to save them.” (Judges 3:9, BSB)

content: Which deliverer in Judges was a left-handed Benjamite?
explanation: He was sent to Eglon king of Moab. “He raised up Ehud son of Gera, a left-handed Benjamite, as their deliverer.” (Judges 3:15, BSB)

content: Sisera was the army commander of which king?
explanation: His army was drawn to the Kishon. “And I will draw out Sisera the commander of Jabin’s army” (Judges 4:7, BSB)

content: To which river did God draw Sisera's army in Deborah's day?
explanation: God delivered him to Barak. “his chariots, and his troops to the River Kishon” (Judges 4:7, BSB)

content: Under the oak in which town did the angel find Gideon?
explanation: It belonged to Joash his father. “the oak in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite” (Judges 6:11, BSB)

content: At what time of night did Gideon's men attack the Midianite camp?
options: The beginning of the middle watch
explanation: Just after the guard changed. “at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the changing of the guard.” (Judges 7:19, BSB)

content: Into how many companies did Gideon divide his three hundred men?
explanation: They surrounded the camp. “And he divided the three hundred men into three companies” (Judges 7:16, BSB)

content: What was the name of Samson's father?
explanation: He was a Danite from Zorah. “Now there was a man from Zorah named Manoah, from the clan of the Danites” (Judges 13:2, BSB)

content: Near which town's vineyards did a young lion attack Samson?
explanation: He tore it apart. “and came to the vineyards of Timnah. Suddenly a young lion came roaring at him” (Judges 14:5, BSB)

content: How much silver did each Philistine lord promise Delilah?
explanation: They wanted Samson's secret. “Then each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.” (Judges 16:5, BSB)

content: About how many people were on the roof of the Philistine temple watching Samson?
explanation: All the lords were there too. “and about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching Samson entertain them.” (Judges 16:27, BSB)

content: Where did the LORD send Jeremiah to receive His message?
explanation: God taught him with clay. “Go down at once to the potter’s house, and there I will reveal My message to you.” (Jeremiah 18:2, BSB)

content: At the potter's house, what did Jeremiah see the potter working at?
explanation: He was shaping clay. “So I went down to the potter’s house and saw him working at the wheel.” (Jeremiah 18:3, BSB)

content: At the potter's house, what was the potter shaping the vessel from?
explanation: God is like the potter. “But the vessel that he was shaping from the clay became flawed in his hand” (Jeremiah 18:4, BSB)

content: Jeremiah watched a potter. When the vessel became flawed, what did the potter do?
explanation: He reshaped it as seemed best. “so he formed it into another vessel, as it seemed best for him to do.” (Jeremiah 18:4, BSB)

content: After Jeremiah saw the potter, who did God say is like clay in His hand?
explanation: God can reshape His people. “Just like clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel.” (Jeremiah 18:6, BSB)

content: After the potter's house, what did God ask Israel through Jeremiah?
options: Can I not treat you as clay?
explanation: God has the right to reshape us. “can I not treat you as this potter treats his clay?” (Jeremiah 18:6, BSB)

content: Later, what did the LORD tell Jeremiah to buy from a potter?
explanation: It became another lesson for the elders. “Go and buy a clay jar from a potter.” (Jeremiah 19:1, BSB)

content: God told Jeremiah He knew him before when?
explanation: God set him apart as a prophet. “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you” (Jeremiah 1:5, BSB)

content: When God called Jeremiah, what excuse did he give?
explanation: God told him not to say that. “I surely do not know how to speak, for I am only a child!” (Jeremiah 1:6, BSB)

content: When God touched Jeremiah's mouth, what did He say He had put there?
explanation: Jeremiah would speak for God. “Behold, I have put My words in your mouth.” (Jeremiah 1:9, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, God says His plans for His people give them a future and what?
explanation: God's plans are good. “plans to prosper you and not to harm you, to give you a future and a hope.” (Jeremiah 29:11, BSB)

content: Why did God tell young Jeremiah not to be afraid?
explanation: God would deliver him. “Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you” (Jeremiah 1:8, BSB)

content: When God asked Jeremiah what he saw, what did he answer?
explanation: God watches over His word. “I see a branch of an almond tree” (Jeremiah 1:11, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, God says you will find Him when you search with all your what?
explanation: God is found by seekers. “You will seek Me and find Me when you search for Me with all your heart.” (Jeremiah 29:13, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, what does God promise to make with Israel and Judah?
explanation: His law will be on their hearts. “when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.” (Jeremiah 31:31, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah's new covenant, where will God write His law?
explanation: God's people will know Him. “I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts.” (Jeremiah 31:33, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, what does God promise if you call to Him?
explanation: He shows great things. “Call to Me, and I will answer and show you great and unsearchable things you do not know.” (Jeremiah 33:3, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, the one who trusts the LORD is like what planted by the waters?
explanation: It does not fear heat or drought. “He is like a tree planted by the waters” (Jeremiah 17:8, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah's prayer, what is too difficult for God?
explanation: He made heaven and earth. “Nothing is too difficult for You!” (Jeremiah 32:17, BSB)

content: Who wrote down Jeremiah's words on a scroll?
explanation: Jeremiah dictated to him. “So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah” (Jeremiah 36:4, BSB)

content: As Jeremiah's scroll was read to him, what did King Jehoiakim do with it?
explanation: He cut it piece by piece. “Jehoiakim would cut them off with a scribe’s knife and throw them into the firepot” (Jeremiah 36:23, BSB)

content: What was at the bottom of the cistern Jeremiah was dropped into?
explanation: Jeremiah sank down in it. “which had no water but only mud, and Jeremiah sank down into the mud.” (Jeremiah 38:6, BSB)

content: Which court official rescued Jeremiah from the cistern?
explanation: He was a Cushite. “Now Ebed-melech the Cushite, a court official in the royal palace, heard that Jeremiah had been put into the cistern.” (Jeremiah 38:7, BSB)

content: To pull Jeremiah from the cistern, what did Ebed-melech tell him to put under his arms?
explanation: They padded the ropes. “Put these worn-out rags and clothes under your arms to pad the ropes.” (Jeremiah 38:12, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, how long would the nations serve the king of Babylon?
explanation: Daniel later read this prophecy. “and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.” (Jeremiah 25:11, BSB)

content: Jeremiah came from a family of priests in which town?
explanation: It was in Benjamin's territory. “one of the priests in Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin.” (Jeremiah 1:1, BSB)

content: Who was Jeremiah's father?
explanation: He was one of the priests. “These are the words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah” (Jeremiah 1:1, BSB)

content: Who read Jeremiah's scroll aloud to King Jehoiakim?
explanation: The king burned each section. “And as soon as Jehudi had read three or four columns” (Jeremiah 36:23, BSB)

content: How many men did the king send with Ebed-melech to rescue Jeremiah?
explanation: They pulled him out with ropes. “Take thirty men from here with you and pull Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies.” (Jeremiah 38:10, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, which animal cannot change its spots?
explanation: Habitual evil is hard to change. “Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?” (Jeremiah 13:23, BSB)

content: When Jeremiah tried not to speak God's message, what was it like in his heart?
explanation: He could not hold it in. “His message becomes a fire burning in my heart, shut up in my bones” (Jeremiah 20:9, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, which family refused to drink wine because of their forefather's command?
explanation: Jonadab son of Rechab commanded it. “for our forefather Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us” (Jeremiah 35:6, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, what should a person boast about?
explanation: God delights in loving devotion. “But let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows Me” (Jeremiah 9:24, BSB)

content: In which land did Job, the blameless and upright man, live?
explanation: He feared God and shunned evil. “There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job.” (Job 1:1, BSB)

content: How does the Bible describe Job before his troubles began?
explanation: He feared God. “And this man was blameless and upright, fearing God and shunning evil.” (Job 1:1, BSB)

content: Before his troubles, how many sons and daughters did Job have?
explanation: He was greatly blessed. “He had seven sons and three daughters” (Job 1:2, BSB)

content: After losing everything, what did Job say about the LORD?
options: The LORD gave and has taken
explanation: He still blessed God's name. “The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.” (Job 1:21, BSB)

content: In all his early losses, what did Job not do?
explanation: He stayed faithful. “In all this, Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing.” (Job 1:22, BSB)

content: After losing his family and wealth, what covered Job's body?
explanation: From his feet to his head. “and infected Job with terrible boils from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.” (Job 2:7, BSB)

content: When Job's three friends first came, how long did they sit with him silently?
explanation: They saw his great suffering. “Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights, but no one spoke a word to him” (Job 2:13, BSB)

content: How did the LORD finally answer Job?
explanation: God spoke to Job directly. “Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind” (Job 38:1, BSB)

content: At the end of Job's story, how much did the LORD give him?
explanation: This came after he prayed for his friends. “the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.” (Job 42:10, BSB)

content: What did the LORD say about Job to Satan?
options: No one on earth is like him
explanation: Job was blameless and upright. “For there is no one on earth like him” (Job 1:8, BSB)

content: When God let Satan test Job, what could Satan not touch at first?
explanation: God set limits. “but you must not lay a hand on the man himself.” (Job 1:12, BSB)

content: After hearing all his losses, what did Job do after tearing his robe?
explanation: He still honored God. “He fell to the ground and worshiped” (Job 1:20, BSB)

content: What struck the house where Job's children were eating?
explanation: It came from the desert. “when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house.” (Job 1:19, BSB)

content: Who told suffering Job, “Curse God and die!”?
explanation: Job refused. “Then Job’s wife said to him, “Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!”” (Job 2:9, BSB)

content: What did Job ask his wife about accepting from God?
explanation: He did not sin in what he said. “Should we accept from God only good and not adversity?” (Job 2:10, BSB)

content: Sitting among the ashes, what did Job use to scrape his sores?
explanation: He was in great pain. “And Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself as he sat among the ashes.” (Job 2:8, BSB)

content: In his suffering, what did Job say he knows?
explanation: His hope was in God. “But I know that my Redeemer lives” (Job 19:25, BSB)

content: What did God ask Job about the earth's foundations?
explanation: God showed His greatness. “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?” (Job 38:4, BSB)

content: After God spoke to him, what did Job say had changed?
options: Now my eyes have seen You
explanation: He had only heard of God before. “My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.” (Job 42:5, BSB)

content: In the book of Job, what is called wisdom?
explanation: Turning from evil is understanding. “Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom” (Job 28:28, BSB)

content: Why was the LORD angry with Job's friends?
explanation: Job had spoken accurately. “For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.” (Job 42:7, BSB)

content: Which of these was one of Job's three friends?
explanation: The others were Eliphaz and Zophar. “Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite” (Job 2:11, BSB)

content: Before his troubles, how many camels did Job own?
explanation: He also had 7,000 sheep. “and he owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels” (Job 1:3, BSB)

content: Which younger man grew angry at Job for justifying himself rather than God?
explanation: He was the son of Barachel. “This kindled the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite” (Job 32:2, BSB)

content: What was the name of Job's first daughter after his restoration?
explanation: The others were Keziah and Keren-happuch. “He named his first daughter Jemimah” (Job 42:14, BSB)

content: How many more years did Job live after his restoration?
explanation: He saw four generations. “After this, Job lived 140 years” (Job 42:16, BSB)

content: God asked Job if he could loosen the belt of which constellation?
explanation: Only God rules the stars. “Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?” (Job 38:31, BSB)

content: Which raiders took Job's oxen and donkeys?
explanation: Only one servant escaped. “the Sabeans swooped down and took them away.” (Job 1:15, BSB)

content: When Job's family came to comfort him, what did each give him?
explanation: They ate with him in his house. “And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.” (Job 42:11, BSB)

content: In Joel, what kind of insects ate up the land?
explanation: Swarm after swarm came. “What the devouring locust has left, the swarming locust has eaten” (Joel 1:4, BSB)

content: In Joel, God promises to pour out His Spirit on whom?
explanation: Peter quoted this at Pentecost. “And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people.” (Joel 2:28, BSB)

content: In Joel, who will be saved?
options: Everyone who calls on the LORD
explanation: Paul quoted this in Romans. “And everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved” (Joel 2:32, BSB)

content: In Joel, what should you rend instead of your garments?
explanation: God wants true repentance. “So rend your hearts and not your garments” (Joel 2:13, BSB)

content: In Joel, how is God described when calling people to return?
explanation: He is slow to anger. “For He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion.” (Joel 2:13, BSB)

content: In Joel, what does God promise to repay?
explanation: God restores what was lost. “I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts” (Joel 2:25, BSB)

content: In Joel, when the Spirit is poured out, what will young men see?
explanation: Old men will dream dreams. “your young men will see visions.” (Joel 2:28, BSB)

content: Who was the prophet Joel's father?
explanation: The word of the LORD came to Joel. “This is the word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel” (Joel 1:1, BSB)

content: In Joel, where will there be deliverance?
explanation: Among the remnant called by the LORD. “for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance” (Joel 2:32, BSB)

content: In which town was the wedding where Jesus did His first sign?
explanation: Jesus' mother was there too. “On the third day a wedding took place at Cana in Galilee.” (John 2:1, BSB)

content: At the wedding in Cana, what ran out?
explanation: Jesus' mother told Him about it. “When the wine ran out” (John 2:3, BSB)

content: At the wedding in Cana, what did Jesus' mother tell the servants?
explanation: She trusted Jesus to help. “Do whatever He tells you.” (John 2:5, BSB)

content: At the wedding in Cana, what did Jesus tell the servants to fill the jars with?
explanation: They filled them to the brim. “Fill the jars with water.” (John 2:7, BSB)

content: At the wedding in Cana, what did the water in the jars become?
explanation: It was Jesus' first sign. “the water that had been turned into wine.” (John 2:9, BSB)

content: At Cana, what did the master of the banquet say about the wine Jesus made?
options: The best was saved until now
explanation: Jesus' wine was the finest. “But you have saved the fine wine until now!” (John 2:10, BSB)

content: Which of Jesus' signs was turning water into wine at Cana?
explanation: His disciples believed in Him. “Jesus performed this, the first of His signs, at Cana in Galilee.” (John 2:11, BSB)

content: Who was Nicodemus, the man who came to talk with Jesus?
explanation: He wanted to learn from Jesus. “Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews.” (John 3:1, BSB)

content: At what time of day did Nicodemus come to see Jesus?
explanation: He came quietly. “He came to Jesus at night” (John 3:2, BSB)

content: Jesus told Nicodemus no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is what?
explanation: Everyone needs a new start from God. “no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again.” (John 3:3, BSB)

content: When Jesus said he must be born again, what did Nicodemus ask?
options: How can an old man be born?
explanation: He did not understand yet. “How can a man be born when he is old?” (John 3:4, BSB)

content: In His talk with Nicodemus, why did Jesus say God gave His one and only Son?
explanation: It is the most famous verse in the Bible. “For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son” (John 3:16, BSB)

content: Jesus told Nicodemus that everyone who believes in God's Son will have what?
explanation: They will not perish. “that everyone who believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life.” (John 3:16, BSB)

content: Jesus told Nicodemus God sent His Son into the world not to condemn it, but to do what?
explanation: God's purpose was rescue. “but to save the world through Him.” (John 3:17, BSB)

content: Tired from His journey through Samaria, where did Jesus sit down?
explanation: It was about noon. “Since Jacob’s well was there, Jesus, weary from His journey, sat down by the well.” (John 4:6, BSB)

content: At Jacob's well, what did Jesus ask the Samaritan woman?
options: Is this the way to town?
explanation: She had come to draw water. “Give Me a drink.” (John 4:7, BSB)

content: Why was the Samaritan woman surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink?
explanation: Jesus broke the barrier. “(For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.)” (John 4:9, BSB)

content: At the well, what did Jesus say He could give the Samaritan woman?
explanation: He meant the gift of eternal life. “and He would have given you living water.” (John 4:10, BSB)

content: Jesus told the woman at the well that whoever drinks the water He gives will never what?
explanation: His water springs up to eternal life. “But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst.” (John 4:14, BSB)

content: When the woman at the well spoke of the coming Messiah, what did Jesus answer?
options: I who speak to you am He
explanation: Jesus told her plainly who He was. “I who speak to you am He.” (John 4:26, BSB)

content: After talking with Jesus, what did the Samaritan woman leave behind at the well?
explanation: She hurried to tell her town. “Then the woman left her water jar” (John 4:28, BSB)

content: Why did many Samaritans from the town believe in Jesus?
explanation: She told everyone what He said. “Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman’s testimony” (John 4:39, BSB)

content: When a huge crowd came to Jesus, which disciple did He ask where to buy bread?
explanation: Jesus was testing him. “He said to Philip, “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”” (John 6:5, BSB)

content: When Jesus fed the five thousand, who had the five loaves and two small fish?
explanation: Jesus used a small gift to feed many. “Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish.” (John 6:9, BSB)

content: What kind of loaves did the boy have when Jesus fed the five thousand?
explanation: Barley bread was simple food. “five barley loaves” (John 6:9, BSB)

content: Which disciple told Jesus about the boy with the loaves and fish?
explanation: He was Simon Peter's brother. “One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to Him” (John 6:8, BSB)

content: Before handing out the loaves and fish to the crowd, what did Jesus do?
explanation: Everyone got as much as they wanted. “Then Jesus took the loaves and the fish, gave thanks” (John 6:11, BSB)

content: After the crowd was full, why did Jesus have the leftovers gathered?
explanation: God's gifts are precious. “Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted.” (John 6:12, BSB)

content: How many baskets were filled with leftovers after Jesus fed the five thousand?
explanation: There was more left than at the start. “and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves” (John 6:13, BSB)

content: In which village did Lazarus and his sisters Mary and Martha live?
explanation: Jesus loved this family. “He lived in Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.” (John 11:1, BSB)

content: What message did Mary and Martha send Jesus about their brother Lazarus?
options: The one You love is sick
explanation: They knew Jesus could help. “Lord, the one You love is sick.” (John 11:3, BSB)

content: When Jesus arrived in Bethany, how long had Lazarus been in the tomb?
explanation: Everyone thought it was too late. “When Jesus arrived, He found that Lazarus had already spent four days in the tomb.” (John 11:17, BSB)

content: Before raising Lazarus, what did Jesus say to Martha about Himself?
options: I am the resurrection and the life
I am the light of the world
I am the bread of life
explanation: Whoever believes in Him will live. “I am the resurrection and the life.” (John 11:25, BSB)

content: Seeing the people mourning for Lazarus, what did Jesus do?
explanation: Jesus cares when we are sad. “Jesus wept.” (John 11:35, BSB)

content: At Lazarus's tomb, what did Jesus tell them to take away?
explanation: He was about to call Lazarus out. ““Take away the stone,” Jesus said.” (John 11:39, BSB)

content: What did Jesus call out in a loud voice at Lazarus's tomb?
explanation: And the dead man came out. “Lazarus, come out!” (John 11:43, BSB)

content: When Lazarus came out of the tomb, how were his hands and feet?
explanation: Jesus told them to unwrap him. “The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen” (John 11:44, BSB)

content: At supper with His disciples, what did Jesus wrap around His waist?
explanation: He took the place of a servant. “and wrapped a towel around His waist.” (John 13:4, BSB)

content: At the supper before He died, what did Jesus begin to do for His disciples?
explanation: It was a servant's job. “began to wash the disciples’ feet and dry them with the towel” (John 13:5, BSB)

content: When Jesus came to wash his feet, what did Peter first say?
options: Never shall You wash my feet!
explanation: Peter felt Jesus was too great to do this. ““Never shall You wash my feet!” Peter told Him.” (John 13:8, BSB)

content: After Jesus explained the foot washing, what did Peter ask Him to wash too?
explanation: Peter wanted to belong to Jesus fully. “not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!” (John 13:9, BSB)

content: After washing their feet, what did Jesus say His disciples should do?
explanation: They should serve each other. “you also should wash one another’s feet.” (John 13:14, BSB)

content: Why did Jesus say He washed His disciples' feet?
explanation: They should do as He did. “I have set you an example so that you should do as I have done for you.” (John 13:15, BSB)

content: After washing His disciples' feet, what new commandment did Jesus give?
explanation: As He loved them, they must love each other. “A new commandment I give you: Love one another.” (John 13:34, BSB)

content: In John's Gospel, who went to Jesus' tomb early while it was still dark?
explanation: She found the stone removed. “Mary Magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed from the entrance.” (John 20:1, BSB)

content: When Mary Magdalene first saw the risen Jesus, who did she think He was?
explanation: She did not recognize Him at first. “Thinking He was the gardener” (John 20:15, BSB)

content: How did Mary Magdalene recognize the risen Jesus?
explanation: The Good Shepherd knows His sheep by name. “Jesus said to her, “Mary.”” (John 20:16, BSB)

content: How does the Gospel of John begin?
options: In the beginning was the Word
explanation: The Word is Jesus. “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” (John 1:1, BSB)

content: John's Gospel says the Word became flesh and did what?
explanation: God came to live with us. “The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us.” (John 1:14, BSB)

content: When John the Baptist saw Jesus coming, what did he call Him?
explanation: He takes away the sin of the world. “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” (John 1:29, BSB)

content: What did Andrew tell his brother Simon after meeting Jesus?
explanation: Then he brought Simon to Jesus. “We have found the Messiah” (John 1:41, BSB)

content: When Jesus first met Simon, what new name did He give him?
explanation: Both names mean rock. “You will be called Cephas” (which is translated as Peter).” (John 1:42, BSB)

content: Jesus told Nicodemus the Son of Man must be lifted up, just as Moses lifted up what?
explanation: Looking to Jesus brings life. “Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up” (John 3:14, BSB)

content: Jesus told Nicodemus no one can enter God's kingdom unless born of what?
explanation: God gives new life. “unless he is born of water and the Spirit.” (John 3:5, BSB)

content: At the well, how many husbands did Jesus say the Samaritan woman had had?
explanation: Jesus knew her whole story. “In fact, you have had five husbands” (John 4:18, BSB)

content: Jesus told the woman at the well that God's worshipers must worship Him in what?
explanation: God is Spirit. “His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.” (John 4:24, BSB)

content: What did the Samaritan woman tell her town about Jesus?
options: He told me everything I did
explanation: She wondered if He was the Christ. “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did.” (John 4:29, BSB)

content: When Jesus asked about buying bread for the crowd, what did Philip say?
options: Two hundred denarii wouldn't be enough
explanation: Philip saw only the problem. “Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece.” (John 6:7, BSB)

content: Jesus said, “I am the bread of life.” Whoever comes to Him will never do what?
explanation: Jesus satisfies the soul. “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never hunger” (John 6:35, BSB)

content: Jesus said, “I am the light of the world.” Whoever follows Him will never walk in what?
explanation: They will have the light of life. “Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness” (John 8:12, BSB)

content: Jesus said He is the good shepherd. What does the good shepherd do for the sheep?
explanation: Jesus gave His life for us. “The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.” (John 10:11, BSB)

content: When Jesus heard Lazarus was sick, what did He say the sickness was for?
explanation: The Son of God would be glorified. “No, it is for the glory of God” (John 11:4, BSB)

content: After hearing Lazarus was sick, how long did Jesus stay where He was?
explanation: God's timing was perfect. “He stayed where He was for two days” (John 11:6, BSB)

content: When Jesus said to take away the stone, what did Martha warn Him?
explanation: Lazarus had been dead four days. “Lord, by now he stinks” (John 11:39, BSB)

content: When Peter questioned the foot washing, what did Jesus tell him?
explanation: Peter did not yet see its meaning. “You do not realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand.” (John 13:7, BSB)

content: Jesus said everyone will know you are His disciples by what?
explanation: Love is the mark of a Christian. “By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another.” (John 13:35, BSB)

content: Complete Jesus' words: “I am the way and the truth and the…”
explanation: No one comes to the Father except through Him. “I am the way and the truth and the life.” (John 14:6, BSB)

content: Complete Jesus' words: “I am the vine and you are the…”
explanation: Apart from Him we can do nothing. “I am the vine and you are the branches.” (John 15:5, BSB)

content: In John's Gospel, what did Jesus say just before He gave up His spirit?
explanation: His work of salvation was complete. “He said, “It is finished.”” (John 19:30, BSB)

content: What did Thomas say he had to see before he would believe Jesus had risen?
options: The nail marks in His hands
explanation: He wanted proof. “Unless I see the nail marks in His hands” (John 20:25, BSB)

content: When Thomas saw the risen Jesus, what did he say?
explanation: His doubt turned to worship. “Thomas replied, “My Lord and my God!”” (John 20:28, BSB)

content: After Thomas believed, whom did Jesus call blessed?
explanation: That includes believers today. “blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.” (John 20:29, BSB)

content: After breakfast by the sea, what did the risen Jesus ask Peter three times?
explanation: Peter had denied Him three times. “Simon son of John, do you love Me more than these?” (John 21:15, BSB)

content: When Peter first said he loved Jesus by the sea, what did Jesus tell him?
explanation: Jesus gave Peter a job to do. “Jesus replied, “Feed My lambs.”” (John 21:15, BSB)

content: At the wedding in Cana, how many stone water jars were there?
explanation: They were for Jewish purification rites. “Now six stone water jars had been set there” (John 2:6, BSB)

content: How much could each stone jar at the wedding in Cana hold?
explanation: Jesus made a huge amount of wine. “Each could hold from twenty to thirty gallons.” (John 2:6, BSB)

content: In which Samaritan town was the well where Jesus met the woman?
explanation: It was near land Jacob gave to Joseph. “So He came to a town of Samaria called Sychar” (John 4:5, BSB)

content: About what hour was it when Jesus sat down by Jacob's well?
explanation: It was about noon, the hottest time. “It was about the sixth hour.” (John 4:6, BSB)

content: Who was one of the two disciples of John the Baptist who first followed Jesus?
explanation: He then brought his brother Simon. “Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who heard John’s testimony and followed Jesus.” (John 1:40, BSB)

content: When Jesus first met Simon, whose son did He say Simon was?
explanation: Then He renamed him Cephas. “You are Simon son of John.” (John 1:42, BSB)

content: Which of Lazarus's sisters would anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair?
explanation: John mentions it to identify her. “(Mary, whose brother Lazarus was sick, was to anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair.)” (John 11:2, BSB)

content: When Lazarus came out of the tomb, what was his face wrapped in?
explanation: His hands and feet were bound with linen. “and his face wrapped in a cloth.” (John 11:44, BSB)

content: By what other name was the apostle Thomas called?
explanation: Didymus means twin. “Now Thomas called Didymus, one of the Twelve” (John 20:24, BSB)

content: How many days later did the risen Jesus appear again, this time with Thomas present?
explanation: The doors were locked, but Jesus stood among them. “Eight days later, His disciples were once again inside with the doors locked, and Thomas was with them.” (John 20:26, BSB)

content: What Hebrew word did Mary Magdalene say when she recognized the risen Jesus?
explanation: It means Teacher. ““Rabboni!” (which means “Teacher”).” (John 20:16, BSB)

content: The second time Peter said he loved Jesus, what did Jesus tell him?
explanation: Jesus restored Peter as a leader. “Jesus told him, “Shepherd My sheep.”” (John 21:16, BSB)

content: Before washing the disciples' feet, what did Jesus pour water into?
explanation: He dried their feet with His towel. “He poured water into a basin” (John 13:5, BSB)

content: Which great city did God send the prophet Jonah to preach against?
explanation: Its wickedness had come up before God. “Go to the great city of Nineveh and preach against it” (Jonah 1:2, BSB)

content: Instead of obeying God's call to Nineveh, where did Jonah try to run?
explanation: He tried to get away from the LORD. “Jonah, however, got up to flee to Tarshish” (Jonah 1:3, BSB)

content: What did the LORD send on the sea while Jonah was running away?
explanation: The ship was about to break apart. “such a violent storm arose that the ship was in danger of breaking apart.” (Jonah 1:4, BSB)

content: During the storm at sea, what was Jonah doing below deck?
explanation: The captain had to wake him up. “where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.” (Jonah 1:5, BSB)

content: How did the sailors find out Jonah was the cause of the storm?
explanation: The lot fell on Jonah. “So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.” (Jonah 1:7, BSB)

content: During the storm, what did Jonah tell the sailors to do to calm the sea?
explanation: Jonah knew the storm was his fault. “and cast me into the sea, so it may quiet down for you.” (Jonah 1:12, BSB)

content: What did the LORD appoint to swallow Jonah in the sea?
explanation: God saved Jonah's life this way. “Now the LORD had appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah” (Jonah 1:17, BSB)

content: How long was Jonah inside the belly of the great fish?
explanation: Jesus later spoke of this sign. “and Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish.” (Jonah 1:17, BSB)

content: When Jonah finally preached in Nineveh, how did the people respond?
explanation: Everyone put on sackcloth. “And the Ninevites believed God. They proclaimed a fast and dressed in sackcloth” (Jonah 3:5, BSB)

content: When God spared the city of Nineveh, how did Jonah feel?
explanation: Jonah did not want God to show them mercy. “Jonah, however, was greatly displeased, and he became angry.” (Jonah 4:1, BSB)

content: After preaching to Nineveh, where did Jonah sit to watch what would happen?
options: In a shelter east of the city
explanation: He waited to see if the city would be destroyed. “Then Jonah left the city and sat down east of it, where he made himself a shelter” (Jonah 4:5, BSB)

content: Outside Nineveh, what did God make grow to give Jonah shade?
explanation: Jonah was very pleased with it. “So the LORD God appointed a vine, and it grew up to provide shade over Jonah’s head” (Jonah 4:6, BSB)

content: What did God send to make Jonah's shade plant wither?
explanation: The plant died the next day. “God appointed a worm that attacked the plant so that it withered.” (Jonah 4:7, BSB)

content: After Jonah's shade plant withered, what beat down on his head?
explanation: Jonah grew faint. “and the sun beat down on Jonah’s head so that he grew faint” (Jonah 4:8, BSB)

content: At the end of Jonah's story, what did God say He cared about?
explanation: God cares even for Israel's enemies. “So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh” (Jonah 4:11, BSB)

content: From which port did Jonah board a ship to run from God?
explanation: He paid the fare to sail for Tarshish. “He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish.” (Jonah 1:3, BSB)

content: In the storm on Jonah's ship, what did the frightened sailors throw overboard first?
explanation: They tried to lighten the load. “And they threw the ship’s cargo into the sea to lighten the load.” (Jonah 1:5, BSB)

content: When the sailors asked who he was, what did Jonah say he was?
explanation: He worshiped the God who made sea and land. ““I am a Hebrew,” replied Jonah.” (Jonah 1:9, BSB)

content: What happened when the sailors threw Jonah into the sea?
explanation: The sailors then feared the LORD. “and the raging sea grew calm.” (Jonah 1:15, BSB)

content: Where was Jonah when he prayed to the LORD his God?
explanation: He cried out to God from the deep. “From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God” (Jonah 2:1, BSB)

content: What did the great fish do when the LORD commanded it?
explanation: Jonah got a second chance. “and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.” (Jonah 2:10, BSB)

content: What warning did Jonah proclaim in Nineveh?
options: Repent or the sea will rise
Forty days and Nineveh will fall
explanation: He walked through the city calling it out. “Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned!” (Jonah 3:4, BSB)

content: When the king of Nineveh heard Jonah's warning, what did he do?
explanation: Even the king humbled himself. “covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.” (Jonah 3:6, BSB)

content: When God saw Nineveh turn from its evil ways, what did He do?
explanation: God shows mercy to those who repent. “He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them.” (Jonah 3:10, BSB)

content: Why did Jonah say he had fled toward Tarshish in the first place?
options: He was afraid of the sea
explanation: He did not want Nineveh to be spared. “I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God” (Jonah 4:2, BSB)

content: Who was the father of the prophet Jonah?
explanation: The book opens with his name. “Now the word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai” (Jonah 1:1, BSB)

content: How long a journey was it to cross the great city of Nineveh?
explanation: It was an exceedingly great city. “requiring a three-day journey.” (Jonah 3:3, BSB)

content: How many people did God say lived in Nineveh who could not tell right hand from left?
explanation: There were many cattle as well. “which has more than 120,000 people” (Jonah 4:11, BSB)

content: What kind of wind did God send on Jonah after his shade plant withered?
explanation: Jonah wished to die. “God appointed a scorching east wind” (Jonah 4:8, BSB)

content: In the king of Nineveh's decree, who had to go without food or water?
explanation: The whole city fasted. “Let no man or beast, herd or flock, taste anything at all.” (Jonah 3:7, BSB)

content: How many spies did Joshua secretly send to look at Jericho?
explanation: They stayed at Rahab's house. “Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two spies from Shittim” (Joshua 2:1, BSB)

content: In Jericho, whose house did Joshua's two spies stay in?
explanation: She protected them. “So they went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there.” (Joshua 2:1, BSB)

content: Where did Rahab hide Joshua's spies from the king of Jericho's men?
explanation: She risked her life for them. “But Rahab had taken them up to the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax” (Joshua 2:6, BSB)

content: What did Rahab tell Joshua's spies she believed about the LORD?
options: He is God of heaven and earth
explanation: She had heard what God did. “for the LORD your God is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.” (Joshua 2:11, BSB)

content: How did Rahab help Joshua's spies escape from Jericho?
options: Let them down by a rope
explanation: Her house was built into the wall. “Then Rahab let them down by a rope through the window” (Joshua 2:15, BSB)

content: What did Joshua's spies tell Rahab to tie in her window?
explanation: It would mark her house to be spared. “you have tied this scarlet cord in the window through which you let us down” (Joshua 2:18, BSB)

content: When Jericho fell, why did Joshua spare Rahab and her family?
explanation: She had shown kindness. “And Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, with her father’s household and all who belonged to her, because she hid the men” (Joshua 6:25, BSB)

content: How many days did God tell Israel to march around Jericho once a day?
explanation: The seventh day was different. “March around the city with all the men of war, circling the city one time. Do this for six days.” (Joshua 6:3, BSB)

content: At Jericho, what did seven priests carry in front of the ark?
explanation: They blew them as they marched. “Have seven priests carry seven rams’ horns in front of the ark.” (Joshua 6:4, BSB)

content: On the seventh day at Jericho, how many times did Israel march around the city?
explanation: Then the priests blew the horns. “Then on the seventh day, march around the city seven times” (Joshua 6:4, BSB)

content: While marching around Jericho, what did Joshua tell the people not to do?
explanation: They had to wait for his signal. “do not let one word come out of your mouth until the day I tell you to shout.” (Joshua 6:10, BSB)

content: After the seventh time around Jericho, what did Joshua command the people?
explanation: The LORD had given them the city. “Shout! For the LORD has given you the city!” (Joshua 6:16, BSB)

content: When the people gave a great shout at Jericho, what happened?
explanation: God gave them the victory. “When they heard the blast of the horn, the people gave a great shout, and the wall collapsed.” (Joshua 6:20, BSB)

content: Before the battle of Jericho, what did the LORD tell Joshua?
options: I have delivered Jericho to you
explanation: The victory was God's. “Behold, I have delivered Jericho into your hand” (Joshua 6:2, BSB)

content: After Moses died, whom did the LORD speak to as Israel's new leader?
explanation: He had been Moses' assistant. “the LORD spoke to Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ assistant” (Joshua 1:1, BSB)

content: When Joshua became leader, what did God command him to be?
explanation: God was with him wherever he went. “Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous?” (Joshua 1:9, BSB)

content: How did Israel cross the Jordan River under Joshua?
explanation: The waters stood still. “while all Israel crossed over the dry ground” (Joshua 3:17, BSB)

content: After crossing the Jordan, how many stones did Israel take from the river?
explanation: One for each tribe. “Take up for yourselves twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan” (Joshua 4:3, BSB)

content: What did Joshua say he and his house would do?
explanation: He asked Israel to choose. “As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD!” (Joshua 24:15, BSB)

content: God told Joshua to meditate on the Book of the Law how often?
explanation: Then he would prosper. “meditate on it day and night” (Joshua 1:8, BSB)

content: God promised Joshua, “As I was with Moses, so will I be with…”
explanation: God would never leave him. “As I was with Moses, so will I be with you” (Joshua 1:5, BSB)

content: God promised Joshua every place his foot would tread on would be what?
explanation: God kept His promise to Moses. “I have given you every place where the sole of your foot will tread” (Joshua 1:3, BSB)

content: Who sent men to Rahab to demand she bring out the Israelite spies?
explanation: He heard spies had come. “So the king of Jericho sent to Rahab” (Joshua 2:3, BSB)

content: Where did Rahab tell the spies to hide for three days?
explanation: Their pursuers would not find them. “Go to the hill country” (Joshua 2:16, BSB)

content: Rahab told the spies Jericho had heard how the LORD dried up which sea?
explanation: Fear of Israel had spread. “For we have heard how the LORD dried up the waters of the Red Sea before you” (Joshua 2:10, BSB)

content: When Israel came to cross the Jordan, what state was the river in?
explanation: It was harvest season. “Now the Jordan overflows its banks throughout the harvest season.” (Joshua 3:15, BSB)

content: At the Jordan, the water stopped when whose feet touched it?
explanation: God went ahead of His people. “as soon as the priests carrying the ark reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water’s edge” (Joshua 3:15, BSB)

content: Why did Joshua have stones taken from the Jordan and set up?
options: To make an altar for Baal
explanation: Children would ask what they meant. “to serve as a sign among you.” (Joshua 4:6, BSB)

content: Near Jericho, who did the man with the drawn sword say He was?
explanation: Joshua fell facedown before Him. “I have now come as Commander of the LORD’s army.” (Joshua 5:14, BSB)

content: What did the Commander of the LORD's army tell Joshua to take off?
explanation: The place was holy. “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.” (Joshua 5:15, BSB)

content: Who took things devoted to the LORD after Jericho fell?
explanation: God's anger burned against Israel. “Achan son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was set apart.” (Joshua 7:1, BSB)

content: Where did Achan hide what he took from Jericho?
options: In the ground in his tent
explanation: He had coveted them. “They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath.” (Joshua 7:21, BSB)

content: How did the people of Gibeon trick Joshua?
options: Pretended to come from far away
explanation: They wore old clothes and carried moldy bread. “carrying on their donkeys worn-out sacks and old wineskins, cracked and mended.” (Joshua 9:4, BSB)

content: When Joshua prayed over Gibeon, what stood still in the sky?
explanation: God fought for Israel. “So the sun stood still and the moon stopped” (Joshua 10:13, BSB)

content: In his farewell, what did Joshua ask Israel to choose this day?
explanation: He chose the LORD. “then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve” (Joshua 24:15, BSB)

content: How old was Joshua when he died?
explanation: He was the servant of the LORD. “Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of 110.” (Joshua 24:29, BSB)

content: How old was Caleb when he asked Joshua for the hill country?
explanation: He was still strong. “So here I am today, eighty-five years old” (Joshua 14:10, BSB)

content: From which place did Joshua send the two spies to Jericho?
explanation: Israel camped there before crossing. “Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two spies from Shittim” (Joshua 2:1, BSB)

content: How long did Rahab tell the spies to hide in the hill country?
explanation: Until the pursuers returned. “Hide yourselves there for three days until they have returned” (Joshua 2:16, BSB)

content: When the Jordan stopped, near which city did the water pile up upstream?
explanation: It was in the area of Zarethan. “It backed up as far upstream as Adam, a city in the area of Zarethan” (Joshua 3:16, BSB)

content: Who carried the twelve stones out of the Jordan?
explanation: Each carried a stone on his shoulder. “So Joshua summoned the twelve men he had appointed from the Israelites, one from each tribe” (Joshua 4:4, BSB)

content: After Jericho fell, where did Israel put the silver, gold, bronze, and iron?
explanation: It was set apart for God. “they put the silver and gold and articles of bronze and iron into the treasury of the LORD’s house.” (Joshua 6:24, BSB)

content: What kind of beautiful cloak did Achan take at Jericho?
explanation: He also took silver and gold. “When I saw among the spoils a beautiful cloak from Shinar” (Joshua 7:21, BSB)

content: Achan, who took devoted things from Jericho, was from which tribe?
explanation: His sin brought trouble on Israel. “of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was set apart.” (Joshua 7:1, BSB)

content: When Joshua told the sun to stand still, over which valley did the moon stop?
explanation: The sun stood over Gibeon. “O moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.” (Joshua 10:12, BSB)

content: In which book was the day the sun stood still also written?
explanation: Joshua mentions this record. “Is this not written in the Book of Jashar?” (Joshua 10:13, BSB)

content: Where was Israel's camp when the Gibeonites came asking for a treaty?
explanation: They pretended to be from far away. “They went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal” (Joshua 9:6, BSB)

content: How many years had God kept Caleb alive since His promise to Moses?
explanation: Caleb was now eighty-five. “He has kept me alive these forty-five years since He spoke this word to Moses” (Joshua 14:10, BSB)

content: In the letter of Jude, whose brother is Jude?
explanation: He calls himself a servant of Jesus. “Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James” (Jude 1:1, BSB)

content: In Jude, what does Jude urge believers to contend for?
explanation: It was entrusted once for all. “urge you to contend earnestly for the faith entrusted once for all to the saints.” (Jude 1:3, BSB)

content: In Jude's closing praise, God is able to keep you from what?
explanation: He presents you with great joy. “Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling” (Jude 1:24, BSB)

content: In Jude, which archangel disputed with the devil over Moses' body?
explanation: He said, “The Lord rebuke you!” “But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses” (Jude 1:9, BSB)

content: In Jude, what did Michael say to the devil?
explanation: He left judgment to God. “but said, “The Lord rebuke you!”” (Jude 1:9, BSB)

content: In Jude, who is called the seventh from Adam?
explanation: He prophesied the Lord's coming. “Enoch, the seventh from Adam, also prophesied about them” (Jude 1:14, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, what is new every morning?
explanation: Great is His faithfulness. “They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness!” (Lamentations 3:23, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, what does the writer call great in the LORD?
explanation: His mercies never fail. “great is Your faithfulness!” (Lamentations 3:23, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, to whom is the LORD good?
explanation: And to the soul who seeks Him. “The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul who seeks Him.” (Lamentations 3:25, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, why are we not consumed?
explanation: His mercies never fail. “Because of the loving devotion of the LORD we are not consumed, for His mercies never fail.” (Lamentations 3:22, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, the ruined city once full of people has become like what?
explanation: Jerusalem had fallen. “She who was great among the nations has become a widow.” (Lamentations 1:1, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, how is it good to wait for the LORD's salvation?
explanation: Trust God in hard times. “It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD.” (Lamentations 3:26, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, after examining our ways, what should we do?
explanation: Repentance brings hope. “Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the LORD.” (Lamentations 3:40, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, what does the people's prayer ask God to renew?
explanation: Restore us to Yourself. “renew our days as of old” (Lamentations 5:21, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, the princess of the provinces has become what?
explanation: The city's glory was gone. “The princess of the provinces has become a slave.” (Lamentations 1:1, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, why does God tell Israel to be holy?
explanation: God's people should be like Him. “Be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy.” (Leviticus 19:2, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, God commands, “Love your neighbor as…”
explanation: Jesus quoted this command. “but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.” (Leviticus 19:18, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, for whom should farmers leave grapes and the edges of the harvest?
explanation: God cares for the needy. “Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.” (Leviticus 19:10, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, what should you do in the presence of the elderly?
explanation: Respect the aged and fear God. “You are to rise in the presence of the elderly, honor the aged, and fear your God.” (Leviticus 19:32, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, God says you must not steal and must not do what?
explanation: Do not deceive one another. “You must not steal. You must not lie or deceive one another.” (Leviticus 19:11, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, what was to be kept burning on the altar continually?
explanation: It must never go out. “The fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it must not be extinguished.” (Leviticus 6:13, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, what does God promise if Israel obeys?
explanation: You will be My people. “I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people.” (Leviticus 26:12, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, from where did the LORD call to Moses?
explanation: God gave laws for worship. “Then the LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting” (Leviticus 1:1, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, on whose head did Moses pour the anointing oil?
explanation: To set him apart as priest. “He also poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him.” (Leviticus 8:12, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, which of Aaron's sons offered unauthorized fire?
explanation: It was against God's command. “Now Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu took their censers” (Leviticus 10:1, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, on the Day of Atonement, onto what were Israel's sins confessed?
explanation: It was sent into the wilderness. “Then he is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities” (Leviticus 16:21, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, where was the goat carrying Israel's sins sent?
explanation: It carried their sins far away. “The goat will carry on itself all their iniquities into a solitary place” (Leviticus 16:22, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, what is the seventh day called?
explanation: No work is done. “but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest” (Leviticus 23:3, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, what was the fiftieth year called?
explanation: Liberty was proclaimed in the land. “It shall be your Jubilee” (Leviticus 25:10, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, to whom does the tithe of the land belong?
explanation: It is holy to the LORD. “Thus any tithe from the land, whether from the seed of the land or the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD” (Leviticus 27:30, BSB)

content: In Leviticus' food laws, which animals could Israel eat?
explanation: God set His people apart. “You may eat any animal that has a split hoof completely divided and that chews the cud.” (Leviticus 11:3, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, what had to be added to every grain offering?
explanation: It is the salt of the covenant. “And you shall season each of your grain offerings with salt.” (Leviticus 2:13, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, what was the second goat of the Day of Atonement called?
explanation: Lots were cast for the two goats. “one for the LORD and the other for the scapegoat” (Leviticus 16:8, BSB)

content: In Leviticus, on which day of the seventh month was the Day of Atonement?
