explanation: Ezra read to them there. “all the people gathered together in the square before the Water Gate” (Nehemiah 8:1, BSB)

content: Tobiah, who mocked Nehemiah's builders, was an official of which people?
explanation: Sanballat was a Horonite. “Tobiah the Ammonite official” (Nehemiah 2:19, BSB)

content: How many men did Moses send to spy out Canaan, one from each tribe?
explanation: Each was a tribal leader. “From each of their fathers’ tribes send one man who is a leader among them.” (Numbers 13:2, BSB)

content: What did the twelve spies carry on a pole between two men?
explanation: The land was very fruitful. “they cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes, which they carried on a pole between two men.” (Numbers 13:23, BSB)

content: How many days did the twelve spies explore Canaan?
explanation: Then they returned to Moses. “After forty days the men returned from spying out the land” (Numbers 13:25, BSB)

content: The twelve spies said Canaan was flowing with what?
explanation: It was a good land. “and indeed, it is flowing with milk and honey.” (Numbers 13:27, BSB)

content: Which spy said, “We can certainly conquer it!”?
explanation: He trusted God. “Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “We must go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly conquer it!”” (Numbers 13:30, BSB)

content: Beside Canaan's giants, the fearful spies said they seemed like what?
explanation: Fear made them feel small. “We seemed like grasshoppers in our own sight” (Numbers 13:33, BSB)

content: Which two spies tore their clothes and urged Israel to trust God?
explanation: They said the land was very good. “Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes” (Numbers 14:6, BSB)

content: After the spies' bad report, who alone of that generation would enter Canaan?
explanation: They had trusted God. “except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.” (Numbers 14:30, BSB)

content: What animal did Balaam ride when going with the princes of Moab?
explanation: God had a lesson for him. “So in the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab.” (Numbers 22:21, BSB)

content: What did Balaam's donkey see standing in the road?
explanation: He held a drawn sword. “When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand” (Numbers 22:23, BSB)

content: What amazing thing did the LORD let Balaam's donkey do?
explanation: She asked why he beat her. “Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam” (Numbers 22:28, BSB)

content: How many times had Balaam beaten his donkey when she spoke?
explanation: She had turned from the angel. “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?” (Numbers 22:28, BSB)

content: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel in a narrow place, what did she do?
explanation: There was no room to turn. “When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam” (Numbers 22:27, BSB)

content: When the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, what did Balaam do?
explanation: He saw the angel with a sword. “And Balaam bowed low and fell facedown.” (Numbers 22:31, BSB)

content: After meeting the angel, what was Balaam allowed to speak?
explanation: God controlled his words. “but you are to speak only what I tell you.” (Numbers 22:35, BSB)

content: How does the priestly blessing in Numbers begin?
explanation: Aaron's sons blessed Israel. “May the LORD bless you and keep you” (Numbers 6:24, BSB)

content: In Numbers, how is Moses described, more than any man on earth?
explanation: He did not seek glory. “Now Moses was a very humble man, more so than any man on the face of the earth.” (Numbers 12:3, BSB)

content: In Numbers, what did Moses put on a pole to heal bitten Israelites?
explanation: Whoever looked at it lived. “So Moses made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole.” (Numbers 21:9, BSB)

content: The priestly blessing in Numbers ends asking the LORD to give you what?
explanation: May He lift His face toward you. “may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and give you peace.” (Numbers 6:26, BSB)

content: In Numbers, how did the cloud over the tabernacle look at night?
explanation: God's presence led Israel. “the cloud would cover the tabernacle by day, and at night it would appear like fire.” (Numbers 9:16, BSB)

content: In Numbers, what food did complaining Israelites say they were tired of?
explanation: They wanted meat instead. “there is nothing to see but this manna!” (Numbers 11:6, BSB)

content: In Numbers, how many years did Israel wander, a year for each spying day?
explanation: They refused to trust God. “In keeping with the forty days you spied out the land, you shall bear your guilt forty years—a year for each day” (Numbers 14:34, BSB)

content: In Numbers, whose staff sprouted, blossomed, and produced almonds?
explanation: God chose Levi's house. “and saw that Aaron’s staff, representing the house of Levi, had sprouted, put forth buds, blossomed, and produced almonds.” (Numbers 17:8, BSB)

content: In Numbers, what did Moses do to the rock instead of speaking to it?
explanation: Water still gushed out. “Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff” (Numbers 20:11, BSB)

content: In Numbers, why could Moses and Aaron not lead Israel into the land?
explanation: They struck the rock. “Because you did not trust Me to show My holiness in the sight of the Israelites” (Numbers 20:12, BSB)

content: In Numbers, Balaam says God is not a man, that He should do what?
explanation: God keeps His promises. “God is not a man, that He should lie” (Numbers 23:19, BSB)

content: In Numbers, whom did God tell Moses to lay hands on as the next leader?
explanation: He had the Spirit in him. “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him.” (Numbers 27:18, BSB)

content: In Numbers, which giant people did the spies see in Canaan?
explanation: Their size frightened the spies. “We even saw the descendants of Anak there.” (Numbers 13:28, BSB)

content: In which valley did the spies cut the great cluster of grapes?
explanation: Eshcol means cluster. “When they came to the Valley of Eshcol” (Numbers 13:23, BSB)

content: Where was Israel camped when the twelve spies returned?
explanation: In the Wilderness of Paran. “in the Wilderness of Paran at Kadesh.” (Numbers 13:26, BSB)

content: In Numbers, which vegetables did Israel miss from Egypt?
explanation: They also missed fish and melons. “along with the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.” (Numbers 11:5, BSB)

content: In Numbers, in which wilderness did the LORD speak to Moses at the start of the book?
explanation: It was the second year after Egypt. “the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the Wilderness of Sinai.” (Numbers 1:1, BSB)

content: Which king's princes did Balaam travel with?
explanation: Balak was king of Moab. “So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.” (Numbers 22:35, BSB)

content: What did Balaam's donkey crush against a vineyard wall?
explanation: She was avoiding the angel. “crushing Balaam’s foot against it.” (Numbers 22:25, BSB)

content: In Numbers, what was a bitten Israelite to do to live?
explanation: Jesus compared Himself to this. “When anyone who is bitten looks at it, he will live.” (Numbers 21:8, BSB)

content: In Obadiah, which nation is the vision about?
explanation: God spoke against its pride. “This is what the Lord GOD says about Edom” (Obadiah 1:1, BSB)

content: In Obadiah, what had deceived Edom?
explanation: They thought no one could bring them down. “The pride of your heart has deceived you” (Obadiah 1:3, BSB)

content: In Obadiah, Edom soared like which bird?
explanation: God would still bring it down. “Though you soar like the eagle and make your nest among the stars” (Obadiah 1:4, BSB)

content: In Obadiah, where did Edom's people live?
options: In the clefts of the rocks
explanation: Their home was in the heights. “O dwellers in the clefts of the rocks whose habitation is the heights” (Obadiah 1:3, BSB)

content: In Obadiah, what will happen to Edom as it has done to others?
options: It will be done to it
explanation: The Day of the LORD is near. “As you have done, it will be done to you” (Obadiah 1:15, BSB)

content: In Obadiah, among what did proud Edom make its nest?
explanation: Even from there God would bring it down. “and make your nest among the stars, even from there I will bring you down” (Obadiah 1:4, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says he can do all things through whom?
explanation: His strength came from Jesus. “I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.” (Philippians 4:13, BSB)

content: In Philippians, what did Paul say he had learned to be in every circumstance?
explanation: He trusted God in plenty and in need. “for I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances.” (Philippians 4:11, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says he knows how to live humbly and also how to do what?
explanation: He was ready for any situation. “I know how to live humbly, and I know how to abound.” (Philippians 4:12, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says, “Rejoice in the Lord…”
explanation: He said it twice. “Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!” (Philippians 4:4, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says to be anxious for nothing, but in everything to do what?
explanation: Pray with thanksgiving. “Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.” (Philippians 4:6, BSB)

content: In Philippians, what does Paul say will guard our hearts and minds?
explanation: It surpasses all understanding. “And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds” (Philippians 4:7, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says God will supply all your what?
explanation: According to His glorious riches. “And my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:19, BSB)

content: In Philippians, complete Paul's words: “For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is…”
explanation: Death would bring him to Christ. “For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.” (Philippians 1:21, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul is confident God will carry the good work He began in you to what?
explanation: God finishes what He starts. “that He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion” (Philippians 1:6, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says in humility to consider others as what?
explanation: Do nothing from selfish pride. “but in humility consider others more important than yourselves.” (Philippians 2:3, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says Christ emptied Himself, taking the form of what?
explanation: He was made in human likeness. “but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant” (Philippians 2:7, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says Christ humbled Himself and was obedient to what?
explanation: That is how far His humility went. “He humbled Himself and became obedient to death— even death on a cross.” (Philippians 2:8, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says at the name of Jesus every what should bow?
explanation: God gave Him the highest name. “that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow” (Philippians 2:10, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says do everything without complaining or what?
explanation: Shine like stars in the world. “Do everything without complaining or arguing” (Philippians 2:14, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says he presses on toward the goal to win what?
explanation: He forgets what lies behind. “I press on toward the goal to win the prize of God’s heavenly calling in Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 3:14, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says our citizenship is where?
explanation: We await a Savior from there. “But our citizenship is in heaven” (Philippians 3:20, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul lists true, pure, lovely things and says to do what with them?
explanation: Fill your mind with good things. “think on these things.” (Philippians 4:8, BSB)

content: Who joined Paul in greeting the saints at Philippi in his letter?
explanation: Both were servants of Christ. “Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, To all the saints in Christ Jesus at Philippi” (Philippians 1:1, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says he was from which tribe of Israel?
explanation: He was a Hebrew of Hebrews. “of the tribe of Benjamin; a Hebrew of Hebrews” (Philippians 3:5, BSB)

content: In Philippians, which two women did Paul urge to agree in the Lord?
explanation: Unity matters in the church. “I urge Euodia and Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord.” (Philippians 4:2, BSB)

content: In Philippians, whom did Paul call his brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier?
explanation: He carried gifts to Paul. “Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier” (Philippians 2:25, BSB)

content: In Philippians, believers from whose household sent special greetings?
explanation: The gospel reached the palace. “especially those from the household of Caesar.” (Philippians 4:22, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says who learned he was in chains for Christ?
explanation: His chains spread the gospel. “it has become clear throughout the whole palace guard and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ.” (Philippians 1:13, BSB)

content: To whom did Paul write his short letter named Philemon?
explanation: Paul wrote as a prisoner. “To Philemon our beloved fellow worker” (Philemon 1:1, BSB)

content: In Philemon, for whom does Paul make his appeal?
explanation: Paul called him his child. “I appeal to you for my child Onesimus” (Philemon 1:10, BSB)

content: In Philemon, Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus as a beloved what?
explanation: No longer as a slave. “no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a beloved brother.” (Philemon 1:16, BSB)

content: In Philemon, Onesimus was once useless but has now become what?
explanation: His name means useful. “Formerly he was useless to you, but now he has become useful both to you and to me.” (Philemon 1:11, BSB)

content: In Philemon, what did Paul say to do with anything Onesimus owed?
explanation: Paul took on his debt. “But if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to my account.” (Philemon 1:18, BSB)

content: In Philemon, how does Paul describe himself?
explanation: He wrote from chains. “Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus” (Philemon 1:1, BSB)

content: In Philemon, what did Paul ask Philemon to prepare for him?
explanation: He hoped to be released. “In the meantime, prepare a guest room for me” (Philemon 1:22, BSB)

content: In Philemon, whom does Paul call our fellow soldier?
explanation: He was part of the house church. “to Archippus our fellow soldier” (Philemon 1:2, BSB)

content: Proverbs says to trust in the LORD with how much of your heart?
explanation: God wants our full trust. “Trust in the LORD with all your heart” (Proverbs 3:5, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs tells us not to lean on what?
explanation: Our own understanding is limited. “and lean not on your own understanding” (Proverbs 3:5, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says if you acknowledge God in all your ways, He will do what?
explanation: God guides those who trust Him. “and He will make your paths straight.” (Proverbs 3:6, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs warns us not to be wise in whose eyes?
explanation: Instead, fear the LORD and turn from evil. “Be not wise in your own eyes” (Proverbs 3:7, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says to honor the LORD with your wealth and with what?
explanation: God deserves our first and best. “Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your harvest” (Proverbs 3:9, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says the LORD disciplines whom?
explanation: Like a father who delights in his son. “for the LORD disciplines the one He loves” (Proverbs 3:12, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs tells a son not to reject what from the LORD?
explanation: God's correction is a sign of His love. “My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD” (Proverbs 3:11, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says a true friend loves when?
explanation: Real friends stay through hard times. “A friend loves at all times” (Proverbs 17:17, BSB)

content: Proverbs says what kind of answer turns away anger?
explanation: Kind words calm people down. “A gentle answer turns away wrath” (Proverbs 15:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs tells the lazy person to learn from which creature?
explanation: The ant works hard without being told. “Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker” (Proverbs 6:6, BSB)

content: Proverbs says what goes before destruction?
explanation: A haughty spirit comes before a fall. “Pride goes before destruction” (Proverbs 16:18, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a child trained in the way he should go will do what when he is old?
explanation: Good training lasts a lifetime. “Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.” (Proverbs 22:6, BSB)

content: In its opening chapter, Proverbs says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of what?
explanation: Fools despise wisdom and discipline. “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge” (Proverbs 1:7, BSB)

content: Proverbs says to guard what with all diligence, because springs of life flow from it?
explanation: What is in the heart shapes all of life. “Guard your heart with all diligence” (Proverbs 4:23, BSB)

content: Proverbs says what is detestable to the LORD?
explanation: Those who deal faithfully are His delight. “Lying lips are detestable to the LORD” (Proverbs 12:22, BSB)

content: Proverbs says to commit what to the LORD so that your plans succeed?
explanation: Then your plans will be achieved. “Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.” (Proverbs 16:3, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a joyful heart is good what?
explanation: A broken spirit dries up the bones. “A joyful heart is good medicine” (Proverbs 17:22, BSB)

content: Proverbs calls the name of the LORD a strong what?
explanation: The righteous run to it for safety. “The name of the LORD is a strong tower” (Proverbs 18:10, BSB)

content: Proverbs says as iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens whom?
explanation: Friends help each other grow. “As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.” (Proverbs 27:17, BSB)

content: Proverbs says every word of God is what?
explanation: He is a shield to those who trust Him. “Every word of God is flawless” (Proverbs 30:5, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a wife of noble character is far more precious than what?
explanation: Her worth is beyond price. “She is far more precious than rubies.” (Proverbs 31:10, BSB)

content: Proverbs says charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but who is to be praised?
options: A woman who fears the LORD
explanation: Character matters more than looks. “but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.” (Proverbs 31:30, BSB)

content: Proverbs says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of what?
explanation: Knowing the Holy One is understanding. “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom” (Proverbs 9:10, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a wise son brings joy to whom?
explanation: A foolish son brings grief to his mother. “A wise son brings joy to his father” (Proverbs 10:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a brother is born for what?
explanation: Family helps in hard times. “and a brother is born for adversity.” (Proverbs 17:17, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a harsh word does what?
explanation: A gentle answer turns away wrath. “but a harsh word stirs up anger.” (Proverbs 15:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a haughty spirit comes before what?
explanation: Pride goes before destruction. “and a haughty spirit before a fall.” (Proverbs 16:18, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of what?
explanation: The right word at the right time is beautiful. “A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.” (Proverbs 25:11, BSB)

content: Proverbs compares a fool repeating his folly to what?
options: A dog returning to its vomit
explanation: Fools keep making the same mistakes. “As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.” (Proverbs 26:11, BSB)

content: Proverbs says which small creatures make their homes in the rocks?
explanation: They are weak but wise. “the rock badgers are creatures of little power, yet they make their homes in the rocks” (Proverbs 30:26, BSB)

content: Proverbs says which creatures have no king, yet advance in formation?
explanation: They work together without a ruler. “the locusts have no king, yet they all advance in formation” (Proverbs 30:27, BSB)

content: Proverbs says which creature can be caught in the hand, yet is found in kings' palaces?
explanation: Small things can go far. “and the lizard can be caught in one’s hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.” (Proverbs 30:28, BSB)

content: Proverbs says the ants, though weak, do what in the summer?
explanation: They plan ahead. “yet they store up their food in the summer” (Proverbs 30:25, BSB)

content: Whose proverbs begin the section that says a wise son brings joy to his father?
explanation: Solomon wrote many proverbs. “The proverbs of Solomon” (Proverbs 10:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs says the righteous run to the name of the LORD and are what?
explanation: His name is a strong tower. “the righteous run to it and are safe.” (Proverbs 18:10, BSB)

content: Complete the start of David's famous psalm: “The LORD is my…”
explanation: God cares for His people like a shepherd. “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.” (Psalm 23:1, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, where does the LORD make him lie down?
explanation: The Shepherd gives rest. “He makes me lie down in green pastures” (Psalm 23:2, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, beside what does the LORD lead him?
explanation: The Shepherd leads to peaceful places. “He leads me beside quiet waters.” (Psalm 23:2, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, what does the LORD restore?
explanation: God refreshes us from the inside. “He restores my soul” (Psalm 23:3, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, why does he fear no evil in the dark valley?
explanation: God's presence takes away fear. “I will fear no evil, for You are with me” (Psalm 23:4, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, which two things comfort him?
explanation: A shepherd uses them to guide and protect. “Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.” (Psalm 23:4, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, what will follow him all the days of his life?
explanation: He will dwell in the house of the LORD forever. “Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life” (Psalm 23:6, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, what happens to his cup?
explanation: God blesses him more than enough. “my cup overflows.” (Psalm 23:5, BSB)

content: In the very first psalm, what does the blessed man delight in?
explanation: He loves God's word. “But his delight is in the Law of the LORD” (Psalm 1:2, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, when does the blessed man meditate on God's law?
explanation: God's word fills his thoughts. “and on His law he meditates day and night.” (Psalm 1:2, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, the blessed man is like what?
explanation: He grows strong and bears fruit. “He is like a tree planted by streams of water” (Psalm 1:3, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, what are the wicked like?
explanation: They have nothing that lasts. “For they are like chaff driven off by the wind.” (Psalm 1:4, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, the blessed man does not sit in the seat of whom?
explanation: He avoids the company of scoffers. “or sit in the seat of mockers.” (Psalm 1:1, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, what does the LORD guard?
explanation: The way of the wicked will perish. “For the LORD guards the path of the righteous” (Psalm 1:6, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, what happens to the leaf of the tree by the streams?
explanation: The blessed man prospers in all he does. “whose leaf does not wither” (Psalm 1:3, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the longest psalm, God's word is called a lamp to what?
explanation: God's word shows us where to step. “Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.” (Psalm 119:105, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In the longest psalm, God's word is called a light to what?
explanation: It guides the whole way ahead. “a light to my path.” (Psalm 119:105, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In the longest psalm, where did the writer hide God's word?
explanation: Knowing God's word helps us resist sin. “I have hidden Your word in my heart that I might not sin against You.” (Psalm 119:11, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In the longest psalm, how can a young person keep his way pure?
options: By guarding it with God's word
explanation: God's word keeps young people on the right path. “How can a young man keep his way pure? By guarding it according to Your word.” (Psalm 119:9, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In the longest psalm, God's words taste sweeter than what?
explanation: The writer loved God's words. “sweeter than honey in my mouth!” (Psalm 119:103, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In the longest psalm, why did the writer hide God's word in his heart?
explanation: God's word protects us from sin. “that I might not sin against You.” (Psalm 119:11, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In a psalm of David, what do the heavens declare?
explanation: Creation shows how great God is. “The heavens declare the glory of God” (Psalm 19:1, BSB)

content: In a psalm of David, what do his enemies do to get his clothing?
explanation: The Gospels saw this happen at Jesus' cross. “They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.” (Psalm 22:18, BSB)

content: In a psalm of David, the LORD is called his light and his what?
explanation: So David asks, whom shall I fear? “The LORD is my light and my salvation” (Psalm 27:1, BSB)

content: A psalm invites us to taste and see what?
explanation: Blessed is the one who takes refuge in Him. “Taste and see that the LORD is good” (Psalm 34:8, BSB)

content: A psalm says if you delight yourself in the LORD, He will give you what?
explanation: Delighting in God shapes what we desire. “Delight yourself in the LORD, and He will give you the desires of your heart.” (Psalm 37:4, BSB)

content: A psalm says the soul longs for God as a deer pants for what?
explanation: The writer thirsts for God. “As the deer pants for streams of water” (Psalm 42:1, BSB)

content: A psalm calls God our refuge and what?
explanation: He is an ever-present help in trouble. “God is our refuge and strength” (Psalm 46:1, BSB)

content: In a psalm, what does God tell us to be, so we know that He is God?
explanation: God will be exalted among the nations. “Be still and know that I am God” (Psalm 46:10, BSB)

content: In David's psalm of repentance, what does he ask God to create in him?
explanation: David wanted to be made right with God. “Create in me a clean heart, O God” (Psalm 51:10, BSB)

content: A psalm of thanksgiving tells all the earth to make what to the LORD?
explanation: Worship can be loud and glad. “Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth.” (Psalm 100:1, BSB)

content: A psalm of thanksgiving says we are God's people and the sheep of what?
explanation: God made us and we belong to Him. “we are His people, and the sheep of His pasture.” (Psalm 100:3, BSB)

content: A psalm of thanksgiving says to enter God's gates with what?
explanation: And His courts with praise. “Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise” (Psalm 100:4, BSB)

content: A psalm says God removes our sins from us as far as what?
options: The east is from the west
The sky is from the sea
explanation: God's forgiveness is complete. “As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us.” (Psalm 103:12, BSB)

content: A psalm says: This is the day that the LORD has made; we will do what?
options: Rejoice and be glad in it
explanation: Every day is a gift from God. “This is the day that the LORD has made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.” (Psalm 118:24, BSB)

content: In a song of ascents, where does the writer say his help comes from?
options: The LORD, Maker of heaven and earth
explanation: He lifts his eyes beyond the hills to God. “My help comes from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.” (Psalm 121:2, BSB)

content: A song of ascents says the Protector of Israel will neither slumber nor what?
explanation: God never stops watching over His people. “the Protector of Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.” (Psalm 121:4, BSB)

content: In a psalm of David, how does he say he was made?
explanation: David praised God for how He made him. “for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” (Psalm 139:14, BSB)

content: The very last psalm calls on everything that has breath to do what?
explanation: The book of Psalms ends in praise. “Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!” (Psalm 150:6, BSB)

content: A psalm says God will command His angels to do what for you?
options: Guard you in all your ways
explanation: God protects those who trust Him. “For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.” (Psalm 91:11, BSB)

content: A song of ascents says how good and pleasant it is when brothers do what?
explanation: Unity among God's people is a blessing. “how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony!” (Psalm 133:1, BSB)

content: A psalm says the length of our days is seventy years, or how many if we are strong?
explanation: Life passes quickly. “The length of our days is seventy years— or eighty if we are strong” (Psalm 90:10, BSB)

content: A psalm says that in God's sight a thousand years are like what?
explanation: God is not limited by time. “For in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes” (Psalm 90:4, BSB)

content: In a psalm of the exile, by which rivers did God's people sit and weep?
explanation: They wept when they remembered Zion. “By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.” (Psalm 137:1, BSB)

content: In the psalm of the exiles in Babylon, where did they hang their harps?
explanation: They were too sad to sing. “There on the willows we hung our harps” (Psalm 137:2, BSB)

content: The psalm about a deer panting for water is a Maskil of whom?
explanation: The sons of Korah wrote several psalms. “A Maskil of the sons of Korah.” (Psalm 42:1, BSB)

content: To which tune was the psalm “My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?” set?
explanation: It is a psalm of David for the choirmaster. “To the tune of “The Doe of the Dawn.”” (Psalm 22:1, BSB)

content: In a psalm of David, the heavens are called the work of what?
explanation: David wondered why God cares for people. “When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers” (Psalm 8:3, BSB)

content: In the shortest psalm, who is called to praise the LORD?
explanation: God's love reaches every people. “Praise the LORD, all you nations!” (Psalm 117:1, BSB)

content: In a psalm of David, where did God knit him together?
explanation: God formed him before he was born. “You knit me together in my mother’s womb.” (Psalm 139:13, BSB)

content: In Revelation, Jesus says, “Behold, I stand at the door and…”
explanation: He wants to come in. “Behold, I stand at the door and knock.” (Revelation 3:20, BSB)
tags: Jesus Stands at the Door and Knocks

content: In Revelation, what will Jesus do if anyone opens the door?
options: Come in and dine with him
explanation: He desires friendship. “If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in and dine with him, and he with Me.” (Revelation 3:20, BSB)
tags: Jesus Stands at the Door and Knocks

content: In Revelation, to which church did Jesus say, “I stand at the door and knock”?
explanation: It was the last of the seven churches. “To the angel of the church in Laodicea write” (Revelation 3:14, BSB)
tags: Jesus Stands at the Door and Knocks

content: In Revelation, Jesus told the church in Laodicea they were neither cold nor what?
explanation: They were lukewarm. “I know your deeds; you are neither cold nor hot.” (Revelation 3:15, BSB)
tags: Jesus Stands at the Door and Knocks

content: In Revelation, what did the church in Laodicea say about itself?
explanation: But they were really poor. “You say, ‘I am rich; I have grown wealthy and need nothing.’” (Revelation 3:17, BSB)
tags: Jesus Stands at the Door and Knocks

content: In His letter to Laodicea, whom does Jesus say He rebukes and disciplines?
explanation: So be earnest and repent. “Those I love, I rebuke and discipline.” (Revelation 3:19, BSB)
tags: Jesus Stands at the Door and Knocks

content: At the end of His letter to Laodicea, who should hear what the Spirit says?
explanation: The message is for everyone. “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.” (Revelation 3:22, BSB)
tags: Jesus Stands at the Door and Knocks

content: In Revelation, what did John see after the first heaven and earth passed away?
explanation: God makes all things new. “Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth” (Revelation 21:1, BSB)
tags: A New Heaven and a New Earth

content: In Revelation, which holy city did John see coming down from heaven?
explanation: It was prepared like a bride. “I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God” (Revelation 21:2, BSB)
tags: A New Heaven and a New Earth

content: In the new heaven and earth, what will God wipe from every eye?
explanation: No more death or pain. “He will wipe away every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4, BSB)
tags: A New Heaven and a New Earth

content: In the new heaven and earth, what will be no more?
explanation: The former things have passed away. “and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain” (Revelation 21:4, BSB)
tags: A New Heaven and a New Earth

content: In Revelation, what did the One on the throne say He makes?
explanation: These words are faithful and true. “Behold, I make all things new.” (Revelation 21:5, BSB)
tags: A New Heaven and a New Earth

content: In the new Jerusalem, what was each gate made of?
explanation: There were twelve gates. “And the twelve gates were twelve pearls, with each gate consisting of a single pearl.” (Revelation 21:21, BSB)
tags: A New Heaven and a New Earth

content: Why does the new Jerusalem need no sun or moon?
explanation: The Lamb is its lamp. “because the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp.” (Revelation 21:23, BSB)
tags: A New Heaven and a New Earth

content: At the end of Revelation, Jesus says, “I am the Alpha and the…”
explanation: The First and the Last. “I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.” (Revelation 22:13, BSB)
tags: I Am the Alpha and the Omega

content: At the end of Revelation, Jesus calls Himself the Beginning and the what?
explanation: He is over all time. “the Beginning and the End.” (Revelation 22:13, BSB)
tags: I Am the Alpha and the Omega

content: In Revelation, what flows from the throne of God and of the Lamb?
options: A river of the water of life
explanation: It is clear as crystal. “Then the angel showed me a river of the water of life, as clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb” (Revelation 22:1, BSB)
tags: I Am the Alpha and the Omega

content: In Revelation, which tree stands on either side of the river of life?
explanation: Its leaves heal the nations. “On either side of the river stood a tree of life” (Revelation 22:2, BSB)
tags: I Am the Alpha and the Omega

content: At the end of Revelation, what will there be no more of in the city?
explanation: The Lord God will shine on them. “There will be no more night in the city” (Revelation 22:5, BSB)
tags: I Am the Alpha and the Omega

content: At the end of Revelation, what does Jesus promise?
explanation: John answers, Come, Lord Jesus! “Yes, I am coming soon.” (Revelation 22:20, BSB)
tags: I Am the Alpha and the Omega

content: At the end of Revelation, Jesus calls Himself the bright what?
explanation: He is also David's Root. “I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the bright Morning Star.” (Revelation 22:16, BSB)
tags: I Am the Alpha and the Omega

content: On which island was John when he received the Revelation?
explanation: He was there for his testimony. “was on the island of Patmos because of the word of God and my testimony about Jesus.” (Revelation 1:9, BSB)

content: In Revelation, to how many churches was John told to send his scroll?
explanation: Ephesus through Laodicea. “Write on a scroll what you see and send it to the seven churches” (Revelation 1:11, BSB)

content: In Revelation, what had the church in Ephesus abandoned?
explanation: Jesus called them back. “You have abandoned your first love.” (Revelation 2:4, BSB)

content: In Revelation, what word describes the church in Laodicea?
explanation: Neither hot nor cold. “So because you are lukewarm—neither hot nor cold” (Revelation 3:16, BSB)

content: In Revelation, what do the four living creatures never stop saying?
explanation: Day and night they praise God. “Holy, Holy, Holy, is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is to come!” (Revelation 4:8, BSB)

content: In Revelation, who triumphed to open the scroll and its seven seals?
explanation: He is the Root of David. “Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed to open the scroll” (Revelation 5:5, BSB)

content: In Revelation, what did the great multitude before the throne hold?
explanation: They wore white robes. “They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.” (Revelation 7:9, BSB)

content: In the new Jerusalem, what was the main street made of?
explanation: It was clear as glass. “The main street of the city was pure gold, as clear as glass.” (Revelation 21:21, BSB)

content: Why was there no temple in the new Jerusalem?
options: God and the Lamb are its temple
explanation: God dwells with His people. “because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple.” (Revelation 21:22, BSB)

content: In Revelation, only those whose names are written where may enter the city?
explanation: Nothing unclean will enter. “but only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” (Revelation 21:27, BSB)

content: In the new Jerusalem, whose names were written on the twelve gates?
explanation: An angel stood at each gate. “twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel” (Revelation 21:12, BSB)

content: In the new Jerusalem, whose names were on the twelve foundations?
explanation: Apostles of the Lamb. “The wall of the city had twelve foundations bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.” (Revelation 21:14, BSB)

content: In Revelation, how many kinds of fruit does the tree of life bear?
explanation: A fresh crop each month. “bearing twelve kinds of fruit and yielding a fresh crop for each month.” (Revelation 22:2, BSB)

content: In Revelation, what are the leaves of the tree of life for?
explanation: Healing for all peoples. “And the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.” (Revelation 22:2, BSB)

content: In Revelation, on which day was John in the Spirit?
explanation: He heard a voice like a trumpet. “On the Lord’s day I was in the Spirit” (Revelation 1:10, BSB)

content: In Revelation, where will God's name be on His servants?
explanation: They will see His face. “They will see His face, and His name will be on their foreheads.” (Revelation 22:4, BSB)

content: In Revelation, at whose feet did John fall to worship before being stopped?
explanation: The angel told him to worship God. “I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown me these things.” (Revelation 22:8, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says God works all things together for the good of whom?
explanation: They are called by His purpose. “And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him” (Romans 8:28, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says God works how many things together for good?
explanation: Even hard times are in His hands. “God works all things together for the good” (Romans 8:28, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: Complete Paul's words to the Romans: “If God is for us, who can be…”
explanation: No one can defeat God's people. “If God is for us, who can be against us?” (Romans 8:31, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says that in all troubles we are more than what?
explanation: It is through Him who loved us. “No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.” (Romans 8:37, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says nothing in all creation can separate us from what?
explanation: God's love in Christ holds us fast. “will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” (Romans 8:39, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says the Spirit helps us when we don't know how to do what?
explanation: The Spirit intercedes for us. “For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us” (Romans 8:26, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says there is now no condemnation for those who are where?
explanation: Jesus took our punishment. “Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” (Romans 8:1, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says the Spirit testifies with our spirit that we are what?
explanation: We belong to God's family. “The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.” (Romans 8:16, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul writes that all have sinned and fall short of what?
explanation: Everyone needs God's grace. “for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (Romans 3:23, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says God proved His love because Christ died for us while we were what?
explanation: God loved us first. “While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is what?
explanation: It comes in Christ Jesus our Lord. “For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” (Romans 6:23, BSB)

content: In Romans, what does Paul say we must confess with our mouth to be saved?
explanation: And believe God raised Him. “that if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,”” (Romans 10:9, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be what?
explanation: The promise is for everyone. “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.” (Romans 10:13, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul quotes, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring…”
explanation: Preachers must be sent. “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!” (Romans 10:15, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says faith comes by what?
explanation: Hearing comes through the word of Christ. “Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.” (Romans 10:17, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul urges believers to offer their bodies as what?
explanation: That is true worship. “to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God” (Romans 12:1, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says be transformed by the renewing of what?
explanation: Do not copy this world. “Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.” (Romans 12:2, BSB)

content: In Romans, how does Paul tell believers to overcome evil?
explanation: Do not let evil win. “Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.” (Romans 12:21, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says rejoice with those who rejoice and do what with those who weep?
explanation: Share in others' feelings. “Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.” (Romans 12:15, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, and persistent in what?
explanation: Keep praying in every season. “Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.” (Romans 12:12, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says that in Christ we who are many are one what?
explanation: Each member belongs to the others. “so in Christ we who are many are one body” (Romans 12:5, BSB)

content: In Romans, what does Paul call the fulfillment of the law?
explanation: Love does no wrong to a neighbor. “Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.” (Romans 13:10, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says he is not ashamed of what?
explanation: It is God's power for salvation. “I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation” (Romans 1:16, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul quotes that who believed God and was counted righteous?
explanation: Faith was credited as righteousness. “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.” (Romans 4:3, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says that since we are justified through faith, we have what with God?
explanation: It comes through our Lord Jesus Christ. “we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ” (Romans 5:1, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul quotes that no one is what, not even one?
explanation: All need a Savior. “There is no one righteous, not even one.” (Romans 3:10, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says, if possible, live at peace with whom?
explanation: Do your part for peace. “If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.” (Romans 12:18, BSB)

content: To believers in which city did Paul write the letter of Romans?
explanation: They were loved by God. “To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints” (Romans 1:7, BSB)

content: Who wrote down Paul's letter to the Romans for him?
explanation: He added his own greeting. “I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.” (Romans 16:22, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul commends Phoebe, a servant of the church in which place?
explanation: She likely carried the letter. “I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.” (Romans 16:1, BSB)

content: In Romans, what word does Paul say we cry out to God by the Spirit of sonship?
explanation: We are God's adopted children. “by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”” (Romans 8:15, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says suffering produces perseverance, which produces what?
explanation: Character then produces hope. “perseverance, character; and character, hope.” (Romans 5:4, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says we were buried with Christ through baptism so we may walk in what?
explanation: Christ was raised from the dead. “we too may walk in newness of life.” (Romans 6:4, BSB)

content: In Romans, which couple does Paul greet as his fellow workers?
explanation: They were tentmakers like Paul. “Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus” (Romans 16:3, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says God's children are co-heirs with whom?
explanation: We share in His glory. “heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ” (Romans 8:17, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says present sufferings cannot compare to what?
explanation: Hope looks forward. “I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.” (Romans 8:18, BSB)

content: In the days of the judges, why did Naomi's family leave Bethlehem?
explanation: There was not enough food in the land. “there was a famine in the land.” (Ruth 1:1, BSB)

content: During the famine, where did Naomi's family go to live?
explanation: There her sons married Moabite women. “went to reside in the land of Moab.” (Ruth 1:1, BSB)

content: When Naomi told her to go home, what did Ruth promise her?
options: I will go back to Moab
Wherever you go, I will go
explanation: Ruth would not leave her mother-in-law. “For wherever you go, I will go” (Ruth 1:16, BSB)

content: Ruth told Naomi, “Your people will be my people, and your God will be…” what?
explanation: Ruth chose to follow the God of Israel. “your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.” (Ruth 1:16, BSB)

content: When Naomi urged her daughters-in-law to go home, what did Orpah do?
explanation: But Ruth clung to Naomi. “and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.” (Ruth 1:14, BSB)

content: In Bethlehem, what did Ruth go into the fields to do?
explanation: Poor people gathered leftover grain after the harvesters. “Please let me go into the fields and glean heads of grain” (Ruth 2:2, BSB)

content: In Bethlehem, whose field did Ruth happen to glean in?
explanation: Boaz was from the clan of Naomi's husband. “And she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz” (Ruth 2:3, BSB)

content: Why was Boaz so kind to Ruth in his field?
options: She had been kind to Naomi
explanation: He had heard how she left her own land for Naomi. “I have been made fully aware of all you have done for your mother-in-law” (Ruth 2:11, BSB)

content: At the end of the book of Ruth, whom did Ruth marry?
explanation: The LORD gave them a son. “So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife.” (Ruth 4:13, BSB)

content: Ruth's son Obed became the grandfather of which famous king?
explanation: A Moabite woman became part of King David's family. “He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.” (Ruth 4:17, BSB)

content: In the book of Ruth, what was the name of Naomi's husband?
explanation: He died in Moab. “The man’s name was Elimelech, his wife’s name was Naomi” (Ruth 1:2, BSB)

content: What were the names of Naomi's two Moabite daughters-in-law?
explanation: Both were women of Moab. “one named Orpah and the other named Ruth.” (Ruth 1:4, BSB)

content: When Naomi came back to Bethlehem, what did she ask the women to call her instead?
explanation: She felt the Almighty had dealt bitterly with her. “Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20, BSB)

content: Naomi said she went away full, but the LORD brought her back how?
explanation: She had lost her husband and both sons. “I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty.” (Ruth 1:21, BSB)

content: At what time of year did Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem?
explanation: It was the right time for Ruth to glean. “And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.” (Ruth 1:22, BSB)

content: How was Boaz related to Naomi?
options: A relative on her husband's side
explanation: He was from the clan of Elimelech. “Now Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side” (Ruth 2:1, BSB)

content: In his field, what did Boaz tell Ruth to do when she was thirsty?
options: Drink from the young men's jars
explanation: Boaz made sure she was cared for. “And when you are thirsty, go and drink from the jars the young men have filled.” (Ruth 2:9, BSB)

content: When Boaz showed her kindness, what did Ruth say she was?
explanation: She was amazed he noticed her. “even though I am a foreigner?” (Ruth 2:10, BSB)

content: Boaz told Ruth she had taken refuge under whose wings?
options: The LORD's, the God of Israel
explanation: Ruth had come to trust Israel's God. “under whose wings you have taken refuge.” (Ruth 2:12, BSB)

content: What did Naomi tell Ruth that Boaz was to their family?
explanation: A kinsman-redeemer could buy back family land. “He is one of our kinsman-redeemers.” (Ruth 2:20, BSB)

content: Where was Boaz winnowing barley the night Ruth went to see him?
explanation: Naomi told Ruth where to find him. “tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.” (Ruth 3:2, BSB)

content: On the threshing floor, what did Ruth ask Boaz to spread over her?
explanation: She was asking him to redeem her as a kinsman. “Spread the corner of your garment over me, for you are a kinsman-redeemer.” (Ruth 3:9, BSB)

content: Where did Boaz sit down to settle the matter of redeeming Naomi's land?
explanation: Legal matters were settled at the gate. “Meanwhile, Boaz went to the gate and sat down there.” (Ruth 4:1, BSB)

content: In old Israel, how did a man make a land deal legally binding?
options: Removed his sandal and gave it
explanation: This was a confirmation in Israel. “a man would remove his sandal and give it to the other party” (Ruth 4:7, BSB)

content: What was the name of the son born to Ruth and Boaz?
explanation: He became King David's grandfather. “and they named him Obed.” (Ruth 4:17, BSB)

content: What were the names of Naomi's two sons?
explanation: Both sons died in Moab. “and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion.” (Ruth 1:2, BSB)

content: About how long had Naomi's family lived in Moab when her sons died?
explanation: Naomi was left without husband or sons. “And after they had lived in Moab about ten years” (Ruth 1:4, BSB)

content: How much barley did Ruth gather on her first day in Boaz's field?
explanation: She worked in the field until evening. “it was about an ephah of barley.” (Ruth 2:17, BSB)

content: Why did the closer kinsman-redeemer refuse to redeem Naomi's land?
options: It would jeopardize his own inheritance
explanation: So Boaz became the redeemer. “or I would jeopardize my own inheritance.” (Ruth 4:6, BSB)

content: At the city gate, Boaz said Ruth was the widow of which man?
explanation: Boaz kept the dead man's name alive in Israel. “I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife” (Ruth 4:10, BSB)

content: Naomi's family were Ephrathites from which town?
explanation: They returned there after the famine. “They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah” (Ruth 1:2, BSB)

content: Who gave Ruth's baby the name Obed?
explanation: They said a son had been born to Naomi. “The neighbor women said, “A son has been born to Naomi,” and they named him Obed.” (Ruth 4:17, BSB)

content: Whose Song of Songs is named in the book's first line?
explanation: It is a song about love. “This is Solomon’s Song of Songs.” (Song of Songs 1:1, BSB)

content: In the Song of Songs, what is the banner over the beloved?
explanation: It is a song of love. “and his banner over me is love.” (Song of Songs 2:4, BSB)

content: In the Song of Songs, which season is past?
explanation: The rain is over and gone. “For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.” (Song of Songs 2:11, BSB)

content: In the Song of Songs, what has appeared in the countryside now that winter is past?
explanation: The season of singing has come. “The flowers have appeared in the countryside” (Song of Songs 2:12, BSB)

content: In the Song of Songs, which animals ruin the vineyards?
explanation: Catch them while the vines bloom. “the little foxes that ruin the vineyards” (Song of Songs 2:15, BSB)

content: In the Song of Songs, what can mighty waters not quench?
explanation: Rivers cannot sweep it away. “Mighty waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot sweep it away.” (Song of Songs 8:7, BSB)

content: In the Song of Songs, love is as strong as what?
explanation: Its sparks are fiery flames. “For love is as strong as death” (Song of Songs 8:6, BSB)

content: In the Song of Songs, which bird's cooing is heard in the land?
explanation: The season of singing has come. “and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.” (Song of Songs 2:12, BSB)

content: In the Song of Songs, what does the beloved ask to be set as over the heart?
explanation: Also as a seal upon the arm. “Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm.” (Song of Songs 8:6, BSB)

content: In the Song of Songs, the beloved's eyes are like what behind her veil?
explanation: He praises her beauty. “Your eyes are like doves behind your veil.” (Song of Songs 4:1, BSB)

content: In the Song of Songs, the beloved's hair is like a flock of goats on which mountain?
explanation: It streams down the slope. “Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.” (Song of Songs 4:1, BSB)

content: In the letter to Titus, what does Paul call Titus?
explanation: They shared a common faith. “To Titus, my true child in our common faith” (Titus 1:4, BSB)

content: In Titus, what has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone?
explanation: Salvation is for all. “For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone.” (Titus 2:11, BSB)

content: In Titus, Paul tells Titus to show himself an example by doing what?
explanation: Teach with integrity. “In everything, show yourself to be an example by doing good works.” (Titus 2:7, BSB)

content: In Titus, on which island did Paul leave Titus?
explanation: To appoint elders in every town. “The reason I left you in Crete was that you would set in order what was unfinished” (Titus 1:5, BSB)

content: In Titus, God saved us not by our deeds but according to His what?
explanation: Through new birth by the Spirit. “He saved us, not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy” (Titus 3:5, BSB)

content: In Titus, whom was Titus to appoint in every town of Crete?
explanation: To set the churches in order. “and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.” (Titus 1:5, BSB)

content: In Titus, where did Paul plan to spend the winter?
explanation: He asked Titus to come there. “make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to winter there.” (Titus 3:12, BSB)

content: In Titus, whom did Paul plan to send, Artemas or whom?
explanation: Then Titus could come to Paul. “As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you” (Titus 3:12, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, on what animal does the coming King ride?
explanation: Jesus fulfilled this on Palm Sunday. “humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.” (Zechariah 9:9, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, “Not by might nor by power, but by My…”
explanation: God's work is done His way. “Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of Hosts.” (Zechariah 4:6, BSB)

content: In Zechariah's vision of Jerusalem, who will fill the streets playing?
explanation: Peace will return to the city. “And the streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing there.” (Zechariah 8:5, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, how is the King coming to Zion described?
explanation: He is also righteous and victorious. “See, your King comes to you, righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey” (Zechariah 9:9, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, God asks who has despised the day of what?
explanation: Small beginnings matter to God. “For who has despised the day of small things?” (Zechariah 4:10, BSB)

content: In Zechariah's vision, who will sit along Jerusalem's streets again?
explanation: Each with a staff because of age. “Old men and old women will again sit along the streets of Jerusalem” (Zechariah 8:4, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, what happens when the Shepherd is struck?
explanation: Jesus quoted this before His arrest. “Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered” (Zechariah 13:7, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, to whom was the word “Not by might nor by power” given?
explanation: He led the temple rebuilding. “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel” (Zechariah 4:6, BSB)

content: Who was the prophet Zechariah's father?
explanation: His grandfather was Iddo. “the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo” (Zechariah 1:1, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, what will the seven eyes of the LORD rejoice to see in Zerubbabel's hand?
explanation: The temple would be finished. “will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel.” (Zechariah 4:10, BSB)

content: In Zephaniah, how does the LORD rejoice over His people?
explanation: He quiets them with His love. “He will rejoice over you with singing.” (Zephaniah 3:17, BSB)

content: In Zephaniah, where is the LORD your God?
explanation: He is mighty to save. “The LORD your God is among you; He is mighty to save.” (Zephaniah 3:17, BSB)

content: In Zephaniah, what great day is near and coming quickly?
explanation: Zephaniah warned of judgment. “The great Day of the LORD is near— near and coming quickly.” (Zephaniah 1:14, BSB)

content: In Zephaniah, with what will the LORD quiet His people?
explanation: He rejoices over them. “He will quiet you with His love” (Zephaniah 3:17, BSB)

content: In whose days as king did Zephaniah prophesy?
explanation: Josiah was son of Amon. “in the days of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah” (Zephaniah 1:1, BSB)

content: Who was the prophet Zephaniah's father?
explanation: Zephaniah was a descendant of Hezekiah. “the word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi” (Zephaniah 1:1, BSB)
